name: Exact mixed difference over hybrids plus common-hybrid witness cover (singleton cancellation under vertex deletion)
statement: For a closed word with singleton prime set U, the deletion-damaged centred word expectation is at most 1_lit-consistent * b_L * E[R |Delta G|], where Delta G = sum_{H subset U} (-1)^{|U|-|H|} G_H runs over 'hybrid' residue configurations (singletons in H overwritten by their forced residues). If |U| > L^{1/4} and Delta G != 0, expanding G = prod_w (1 - I_w) shows that some single hybrid contains positive witnesses whose prime supports cover U. A minimal cover yields T = L^{1/12} witnesses with …
why: This is the trace's 'turning point' and the most original-looking device in Part I. But the problem it solves is stated verbatim in HR21 section 5. The principle that only deletion terms covering every singleton survive is the content of Pilatte Lemma 9.2 together with the rank argument of Prop. 9.1, and both are in L. 007's contribution is to replace the truncated sieve, with its coefficient and remainder bounds, by an exact discrete-derivative identity used only for existence, plus a minimal-…

name: Two-band weighted divisor graph: uncentred heavily weighted core primes plus vertex-normalised centre primes with non-mean-zero centring theta = beta_Z^2
statement: Edge kernel g_d(x,y) = w_d(x)w_d(y) A^{omega_C(d)} 1_{d_C | x} prod_{p|d, p in Z}(1_{p|x} - theta/p). The core band C (weight A = e^{2 kappa}, uncentred) supplies size and cutoff savings; the centre band Z (weight 1) supplies cancellation. With vertex weight W(x) = prod_a beta_a^{-omega_a(x)} and closed-walk products normalised by W at each departure, a centre prime on a single good edge has total multiplier theta(1-theta/p) on its lit residue and -theta beta_Z^{nu_p(a)}/p elsewhere. The choice…
why: This is the strongest candidate in the family. It is insight-coded in the trace, passes test 2, and is load-bearing for the qualitative theorem. No arithmetic precedent was found. Two things stop it at N2. (a) theta = beta_Z^2 is the standard 'centre by the expectation under the operative measure' rule, applied once vertex normalisation has been chosen. The trace shows beta^2/p centring already present in the single-band design taken from Pilatte, so the matching is not where the step lies. (b)…

name: Finite residue comparison via Braverman's bounded independence, with the Alon-Goldreich-Mansour exact-independence correction
statement: Every event given by a depth-at-most-20, size-at-most-exp(L^6) circuit in residue-equality tests modulo primes up to e^L has the same probability, up to e^{-L^{10}}, under a uniform origin in any interval of length at least exp(L^A/2) as under the independent product law. Proof: encode residues by B = L^15 jittered dyadic bits; bound t-wise bit marginals by CRT; correct to exact t-wise uniformity by a Fourier/AGM step; apply Braverman (Corollary 2).
why: A known theorem (Braverman) and a known correction (AGM) are imported into a role that HR21 filled with the Kubilius model. By the codebook, cross-field transfer is N0, however large the field distance. The first application of bounded-independence fooling of AC0 to analytic number theory that we found is recorded as a new bridge, not as a eureka step.

name: Fixed-scale order of limits (graph fixed at B, X -> infinity first, then B -> infinity) with finite-prime stability of uniform non-pretentiousness
statement: Since uniform non-pretentiousness has no rate, all graph parameters are fixed at an auxiliary scale B. The analytic centring error is o(1/B) as X -> infinity, against B^{-1-c*/2} from the graph; then B -> infinity.
why: Conceptually important to the qualitative theorem, but a standard device.

name: First-visit tree organisation of closed walks with the exact weighted-subtree identity
statement: Walks are organised by their first-visit tree. Sum_Q u_a(Q) = S_a(T) = sum_v (1 - beta_a^{s(v)}), proved by a branching-percolation probability argument, cancels the background normalisation exponential exactly.
why: A standard encoding plus an elementary identity, tuned to C2's weights.

name: Conditional cylinder sieve: truncated inclusion-exclusion applied after conditioning, with centre residues left unconditioned
statement: Vertex-deletion conditions are expanded by a finite-cylinder truncation of the intersection poset (Rota chain expansion) after conditioning on fixed coordinates, so that centre-prime residues stay unconditioned and signed averages can be taken before absolute values.
why: An adapted construction with a precedent the paper names. Its new feature (conditioning before truncation, centre coordinates free) is the Part II counterpart of C1's purpose.

name: J disjoint centred prime supplies with whole-tuple nonbacktracking matrix and spectral passage
statement: Steps carry one prime from each of J supplies of reciprocal mass ~W, giving W^J mass against an operator cost (C sqrt W)^J. H_{d,d'} = 1_{d != d'} A_{d'} forbids repeating a whole tuple consecutively. J ~ log log X gives a power-of-log saving.
why: Retrieved framework, moved to ordinary averages

name: Padding divisors: uncentred squarefree q from primes not 1 mod 5, weight 4^{omega(q)}, normalised by sqrt(w), w = 5^{omega_Q}, for anti-concentration in short …
statement: An independent padding factor q makes the distribution of log(dq) spread at scale eta = e^{-J} (characteristic-function decay via PNT mod 5), so that each of the O(L/eta) short multiplicative intervals carries mass with a 1/L edge normalisation. The forest code counts repetition patterns uniformly over padding values, so padding weights are summed afterwards in one residue environment.
why: A constructed auxiliary object with no named precedent, but it implements a standard smoothing principle. It is also the Part I sibling of C2's two-role design, and that sibling weakens C2.

name: Random-prime rank estimate over R for lit-consistency congruences
statement: If B in M_r(Z) is nonsingular over R and primes are drawn from a measure with max atom alpha, then the probability that B x = f(x) mod the primes is small. This gives a saving for words with many independent lit-consistency pairs without invertibility modulo the summed primes.
why: Adapted from HR21 sections 6-7 to the present coefficients

name: Single narrow core band in place of layered core bands (second insight step)
statement: One narrow upper band of core primes replaces several layered core bands
why: Constructed simplification inside C2. Graded only because the PLAN makes every insight step a candidate.

name: Mixed-difference / common-hybrid witness cover (Part II, PV9)
against: Nearest neighbours: Pilatte 2026 Lemmas 11.6, 13.1, 13.6 (witnesses, active primes) and HR21's singleton cancellation. The 'pairwise changes' variant it improves on was probably closer to them. The identity E[(1_{Z=a} - 1/p)F(Z)] = (1/p)E[F(a) - F(Z)] is elementary, and mixed differences are standard (Gowers-type / inclusion-exclusion). Triggered by an explicitly stated requirement one sentence e…
why: The summarizer calls it the 'combinatorial turning point', and the model writes it in VERBATIM: the idea is visibly the model's. No reference is invoked at L164-171, and the paper gives no attribution for the mixed-difference / hybrid mechanism itself; it attributes only the downstream active-prime and triangular steps to Pilatte. It is non-analytic. Hybrids (configurations overwritten at a subset H of singleton coordinates) and the existence-only algebraic expansion of prod(1 - I_w) appear now…

name: Two-band weighted divisor graph with non-mean-zero centering theta = beta_Z^2 matched to endpoint normalization (Part I, PV4)
against: Weights A^{omega(d)} and centering at beta^2/p were already present in the single-band version (L66-68), modelled on Pilatte, so the split is one design step from a retrieved template. Driven by stated local problems (C12, C13), so conflict-driven refinement rather than a hidden leap. Its pay-off needs the first-visit tree and the conditional cylinder sieve (chain depth 2), whose novelty is low.
why: Coded as an insight backtrack: a viable single-band design is replaced by a structural re-design, with no reference invoked. The paper stresses that the center factor 'is not itself mean zero under uniform residues' and cancels only through the closed-walk normalization. This departs from the mean-zero centered factors of HR21 and Pilatte. Decoupling savings (core) from cancellation (center) is what lets a qualitative result work with no rate in the non-pretentiousness hypothesis.

name: Bounded-independence (Braverman AC0) bridge for comparing finite integer intervals with independent residues (Part II, PV8)
against: Transfer of a known theorem is not a eureka step by the project's codebook. A known route exists: Linial-Nisan's approximate inclusion-exclusion links Brun-type sieves and bounded independence (the paper sets out the lineage). The paper needs an extra correction to EXACT bounded independence (Alon-Goldreich-Mansour) that is not visible in the trace.
why: Large field distance (TCS pseudorandomness -> multiplicative number theory). It is invoked right after a stated obstruction, so the retrieval is targeted. The encoding of deletion predicates as constant-depth circuits is problem-specific.

name: Fixed-scale order of limits (graph at fixed B, X -> infinity, then B -> infinity) (Part I, PV5)
against: A routine order-of-limits device; well known in analysis and in MRT-type arguments.
why: It is the conceptual key to a qualitative every-scale result under a rate-free hypothesis, and it inverts the entropy-decrement failure (C4).

name: Shafarevich conjecture on holomorphic convexity; holomorphic hull
statement: Universal cover of every smooth connected projective complex variety is holomorphically convex; hull K^_V = {v: |g(v)| <= sup_K |g| for all g in O(V)}; convexity = all hulls compact.
why: Textbook SCV notion and the posed problem.

name: infinite Nori string
statement: Connected curve whose normalized components have finite pi_1-image but whose union has infinite image; a closed infinite Nori string cannot lie in a holomorphically convex space.
why: Classical obstruction (Lasell-Ramachandran, Katzarkov-Ramachandran, Coltoiu-Joita).

name: meridian
statement: Boundary of a small disk transverse to a divisor.
why: Standard.

name: special (Campana)
statement: No line bundle L with nonzero L -> Omega^p and kappa(M,L)=p; used only to conclude the surface is not special via OpenAIAbelianity2026 Cor. 1.4.
why: Cited definition; corollary-only use of a model-produced result.

name: semialgebraic subset
statement: Finite Boolean combination of real polynomial (in)equalities in affine charts; surface's universal cover is not biholomorphic to a semialgebraic open subset by OpenAISemialgebraicCovers2026 Cor. 8.1.
why: Standard; corollary-only use of a model-produced result.

name: Thm main (surface)
statement: There is a smooth connected projective surface X containing a connected nodal curve Z_0 with smooth rational components such that im(pi_1(Z_0)->pi_1(X)) is infinite; a component above Z_0 in X~ is closed, noncompact, a locally finite union of compact rational curves; hulls of its points are noncompact; X~ is not holomorphically convex.
why: Headline.

name: Lemma rational-hull (compact-curve obstruction, rational case)
statement: If Z subset X compact connected nodal with smooth rational components and infinite pi_1 image, every component W of its preimage in X~ is closed, noncompact, locally finite union of compact rational curves, holomorphic functions constant on W, hull of any point noncompact.
why: Paper names the precedent explicitly.

name: free pro-2 group F_d, weighted Magnus expansion, valuation nu
statement: g_i -> 1+U_i in A=F_2<<U_1..U_d>>, deg U_i=w_i; nu(g)=least degree of g-1; faithfulness and cofinality re-proved.
why: Textbook (Magnus, Lazard, Vinberg).

name: degree rules nu(gh)>=min, nu([g,h])>=nu(g)+nu(h), nu(g^{2^e})>=2^e nu(g)
statement: As stated.
why: Standard.

name: Lemma substitution
statement: If nu(alpha(g_i)g_i^{-1}) >= w_i + a then (alpha - id)(A_{>=n}) subset A_{>=n+a}; degree-raising operators may be substituted for Magnus variables.
why: Routine filtered-algebra substitution; folklore in pro-p/Magnus theory.

name: Frattini quotient; Frattini basis criterion; Hopfian property
statement: Elements spanning G/closure(G^2[G,G]) topologically generate; d elements of F_d with Frattini-basis images are a free basis.
why: Textbook (Burnside basis theorem, Hopficity of f.g. profinite groups).

name: Lemma weighted infinitude criterion (weighted Golod-Shafarevich)
statement: If nu(r_lambda) >= v_lambda, finitely many v below any bound, relator series converges and 1 - sum t^{w_i} + sum t^{v_lambda} < 0 for some 0<t<1, the pro-2 quotient is infinite.
why: Ershov 2011 Thm 2.1/Cor 2.2 states it; re-proved for the infinite-relator convention.

name: witness family: Eisenstein curve E, q, f induced by [4], parameter curve B, markings A_s (48 points)
statement: E=C/(Z+Z omega), omega^3=1; q:E->P^1 sign quotient; f induced by [4]; B=P^1 minus q(E[2]) cup q(ker(1-omega)) (5 points); A_s={z: f(z)=omega_bar^j s, j=0,1,2}.
why: Specific genus-zero marked family with torus lift; BK/EF use genus>=2 families; no equivalent found in quick search.

name: Lemma family (5 excluded points; 48 points as etale multisection; 24 collisions at s_*)
statement: As stated.
why: Routine verification on the witness.

name: torus group F=pi_1(T,0) free on x,y,a_0,a_1,a_2,c_0,c_1 with weights 1,1,1,1,1,2,2; Gamma=pi_1(B) free rank 4
statement: As stated; surface relation [x,y]c_0c_1c_2=1 gives nu_F(c_2)>=2.
why: Choice of weighted basis; routine once S13 fixed.

name: H=(Z/4)^2, K=ker(F->H) (rank 97), T^(4), S=P^1 minus A_{s0}, Pi=pi_1(S) (rank 47), p:K->Pi
statement: Multiplication-by-4 cover and sign quotient relate the small torus group F to the actual sphere group Pi; 'Keeping this connection based ... is essential'.
why: Lifting a sphere family to an elliptic (isogeny) cover to control monodromy is a known move (Kummer/Legendre style), here used based.

name: corrected based monodromy phi_m = iota^{eps(m)} H_1; 'pure'
statement: Endpoint of an iota-equivariant isotopy fixing 0, corrected by the sign so each puncture is fixed.
why: Standard point-pushing monodromy with a sign correction.

name: Prop based-monodromy
statement: phi_m form a homomorphism Gamma->Aut(F), pure, commute with iota_*, preserve K, p o phi_m|_K = beta_m o p (actual based sphere monodromy); p:K->Pi surjective.
why: Covering-space bookkeeping.

name: Lemma degree-one (three invariant double covers Y_j^2 = q(z) - omega_bar^j s)
statement: Every phi_m and iota_* act trivially on V=F/{nu_F>=2}: the two handle characters and three characters chi_j of explicit double covers with global basepoint lifts form a basis of V* and are monodromy- and sign-invariant.
why: Explicit invariant characters via double covers branched at puncture pairs; idea (monodromy acting trivially on H_1 mod 2 => unipotent on pro-2 completion) is standard in pro-l monodromy.

name: Prop monodromy-raising
statement: For every m in Gamma, phi_m - id raises weighted degree by >=1 on the completed Magnus algebra of F^.
why: Pro-2 unipotence of monodromy; known shape (Johnson/weight filtration), new specific verification for weight-2 boundaries.

name: core collapse: L free pro-2 on a_{h,j} (48), Phi:F -> L x| H, x->T_1, y->T_2, a_j->a_{0,j}, c_0,c_1->1
statement: Collapsing the lifted core kills its pi_1; Phi|_K is the collapse map followed by completion.
why: Van Kampen collapse; the semidirect-product substitution is a natural device.

name: pinched involution sigma(a_{h,j}) = a_{b_j-h,j}^{-1}, b_j mod 2H != 0
statement: As stated.
why: Computation.

name: Lemma pinched-sphere
statement: Pi_pair (kill 24 pair boundaries) free rank 24 with completion L/<<sigma(g)g^{-1}>>; any sigma-trivial quotient lambda:L->R gives theta:Pi->R dense with theta p = lambda Phi|_K; equalizer condition on K implies theta beta_m = theta on all of Pi.
why: Diagram chase; the key design choice is comparing on K before pinching.

name: Lemma finite-geometric-monodromy
statement: Action of Gamma on markings and sign factors through a finite 2-group (in H^3 x| Z/2); gamma_* has nontrivial sign, gamma_*^2 fixes markings and acts trivially on Pi_pair.
why: Half-twist/full-twist local computation.

name: shift-adapted basis u_{il,j} = delta_{T1}^i delta_{T2}^l (a_{0,j}), weights i+l+1; Lemma shift-basis
statement: u_{il,j} form a free pro-2 basis of L (Frattini images are the monomial basis xi^i eta^l of F_2[H]=F_2[xi,eta]/(xi^4,eta^4)); T_1-id, T_2-id, sigma-id each raise degree by >=1.
why: Basis adapted to a unipotent group action via iterated differences = Jennings/Lazard-type basis of the permutation module F_2[H]; close to known filtrations.

name: cyclic endpoint estimate: T^4=id and nu(w_i)>=d+i (i<=3) imply nu(w_4)>=d+4
statement: Proved via formal triangular automorphism T'(z_i)=z_{i+1}z_i, (T')^4-id=(T'-id)^4 in char 2, and the observation that T'^3(z_0) contains z_3 once as first letter.
why: Short char-2 binomial trick.

name: Prop involution: 24 relators r_g = sigma(g)g^{-1} impose sigma=id with cost tG(t); P=(1+t)G, G(t)=3t(1+t)(1+t^2)^2
statement: Frattini differential d = u + u^2 d/du + v^2 d/dv on R=F_2[u,v]/(u^4,v^4) satisfies d^2=0 and R = C (+) dC with C=span{u^a v^b: a in {0,2}}; lifting a basis of C to elements g gives 24 relators of degree w_g+1 whose normal closure is exactly the sigma-coinvariant kernel.
why: Self-described reusable mechanism; acyclic Frattini complex trick not found in quick search; nearest precedent Koch-Venkov (sigma-inverted relators lie deeper) found later.

name: Lemma transfer (nu_F >= n => L-component nu_L >= n)
statement: Represent L x| H on A_L; substitute degree-raising operators.
why: Direct application of S10.

name: deep monodromy relators Phi(phi_m(k_i)k_i^{-1}), m in M_N (basis of D_N/D_{N+1}, |M_N|<=4^N), cost 97 sum_{N>=J} 4^N t^{N+1}
statement: Counting monodromies by Magnus depth avoids estimating the rank of Gamma_J.
why: Depth-counting of relators is in the spirit of GS/Golod; application to monodromy invariance is specific.

name: Lemma deep-invariance
statement: f_K o phi_m = f_K for all m in D_J; hence Pi -> Q_0 is invariant under actual monodromy of Gamma_J.
why: Closed-subgroup argument.

name: t=49/200; J; M=<gamma_*^2>Gamma_J; B',C'; U subset P^1 x B'; pi_1(U)=Pi x| M; rho_0
statement: As stated.
why: Standard base change bookkeeping.

name: Y -> C' by blowing up section collisions; D=Y\U SNC; distinguished fiber D_* = main sphere + 24 tails
statement: As stated, with an explicit local induction for SNC.
why: Standard.

name: Lemma distinguished-meridians
statement: Every meridian of a component of D_* has trivial image under rho_0.
why: Local computation.

name: boundary power relators mu~_i^{2^e} with b t^{2^e} < 1/100
statement: High powers of the remaining boundary meridians.
why: Golod's method, named.

name: Prop infinite-quotient
statement: Q infinite; rho dense on every punctured fiber; component meridians of D finite order, of D_* trivial. Margin: G(49/200)>257/250, total < -1/125.

name: Lemma finite local detection and descent
statement: Given rho:pi_1(Y\D)->Q dense profinite with finite-order meridians, there is a finite quotient P_f injective on every local boundary image; the corresponding cover extends to smooth projective X->Y with SNC boundary and rho_X:pi_1(X)->Q with rho_X i_* = rho pi_*.
why: Standard 'choose a finite quotient faithful on local groups' device (orbifold uniformization / Kato-Namba / BK-EF style).

name: Lemma rational-special-fiber
statement: Resolution can be chosen so Z=h^{-1}(c_*)_red has smooth rational components and ordinary crossings.
why: Local models + Riemann-Hurwitz.

name: Lemma infinite-special-image (with deformation-retract neighbourhood via Lojasiewicz triangulation)
statement: Some component Z_0 of Z has infinite image in pi_1(X).
why: Standard regular-neighbourhood argument.

name: large fundamental group
statement: For every positive-dimensional closed irreducible Z, im(pi_1(Z^nu)->pi_1(X)) infinite.
why: Kollar's definition.

name: Thm main (fourfold)
statement: There exist a smooth connected projective fourfold X and a simple abelian surface A subset X with X of large pi_1 and im(pi_1(A)->pi_1(X)) = Z; X~ has no positive-dimensional compact analytic subvariety and is not Stein.
why: Headline.

name: Prop large-reduction (simple abelian surface with Z image => large-pi_1 fourfold with non-Stein cover)
statement: Given A subset S' with im(pi_1 A) = Z, X = complete intersection of c=d+2 general sections of I_F (x) L^m in W=S' x B (B abelian 6-fold, F=A x {0}) is smooth, pi_1(X)=pi_1(S') x pi_1(B), fibers over B have <=3 points off F, X large, X~ not Stein.
why: Lefschetz/Bertini/incidence count are standard; the 'add an abelian 6-fold to make everything else large' trick is new-looking but elementary.

name: Lemma red:compact-criterion
statement: X~ has no positive-dimensional compact analytic subvariety iff X has large pi_1.
why: Known equivalence (Kollar).

name: Lemma red:interpolation
statement: H^0(I_F (x) L^m) -> (+) L^m|_{p_i} surjective for large m uniformly in l distinct points off F.
why: Standard.

name: non-Stein obstruction: A_K = C^2/K, K=Z^3, A_K ~ T^3 x R, H_3 = Z, Andreotti-Frankel
statement: A component of the preimage of A in X~ is the closed submanifold C^2/K with nonzero H_3, impossible in a Stein manifold (Andreotti-Frankel); simplicity of A prevents compact curves in it.
why: Elementary given Andreotti-Frankel; closest precedents: toroidal (Cousin) groups C^2/Z^3 as non-Stein noncompact Lie groups, and Nori-string obstruction (compact components). New as an obstruction to the large-pi_1 Shafarevich conjecture in quick search.

name: reading framework: graphs with charts (D_v,d_v), readings [p]_v of paths of length <=N, axioms (P1)-(P3), 'closes on reading', groupoid Q
statement: (P1) prefixes/reverses/edge bijections; (P2) prefix-change compatibility for paths of length <= N/2; (P3) uniform Gromov hyperbolicity of all chart components.
why: A developing-map/Cartan-Hadamard frame in combinatorial dress.

name: Lemma local path criterion
statement: There is N_0 depending only on the hyperbolicity constant such that if readings satisfy (P1)-(P3) with N>=N_0 and e is a single-edge loop at v with [e]_v != d_v, then e is nontrivial in Q.
why: Variant of Gromov's Cartan-Hadamard / local-to-global theorem (Gromov 1987; Delzant-Gromov; Coulon; DGO).

name: ladder of width h; Lemma narrowing (width <=1000H => width <=H)
statement: Ladders compare readings; composition adds widths; narrowing via quadrangle slimness.
why: Fellow-traveller narrowing for local geodesics; standard in hyperbolic geometry.

name: guide (k-local geodesic in charts)
statement: Path each of whose subpaths of length <= k reads as a geodesic in the chart at its initial vertex.
why: Renaming of k-local geodesic.

name: Lemma extension (continue a guide by one edge, width <=50H)
statement: Repair by minimizing sum of chart distances between chosen nearby vertices at marks spaced in [L,2L].
why: Minimization repair is a careful variant of the local-geodesic-is-quasigeodesic argument.

name: synchronous comparison of geodesics with width 10(h+Delta)
statement: As stated.
why: Standard fellow-travelling.

name: six real algebraic slopes (4 red |lambda|<0.01, 2 blue |lambda|>4) with Galois group S_6; genus-two C with simple Jac (Zarhin)
statement: Weak approximation + Frobenius cycle types (6),(5,1),(2,1,1,1,1) give S_6; Zarhin gives End(Jac C)=Z.
why: Standard (Zarhin; Dedekind/Frobenius).

name: arrangement D: z-family (six slope hyperplanes z_2=lambda_i z_1, couplings z_1=+-c) and w-family; ball |z|^2+|w|^2<a; sigma(z,w)=(w,-z); 0.85<c/sqrt(a)<0.9
statement: Coupling hyperplanes meet exactly the four red slopes; z- and w-couplings disjoint (2c^2>a); sigma order 4 integral unitary.
why: No arrangement with 'coupling' hyperplanes identifying red meridians found in quick search.

name: Prop arrangement-local (exact local arrangements in deep congruence quotients)
statement: For W,R_0 there is torsion-free sigma-normalized principal congruence Gamma_0 with: every W-ball sees distinct labels isometric to a subarrangement of D; injectivity radius > R_0; exactly D near o.
why: Gram-matrix finiteness + congruence separation; standard in Stover-Toledo / Deraux style arguments.

name: Stover-Toledo virtual cyclic ramified covers
statement: Compact simplest-type congruence ball quotient, divisor with disjoint smooth totally geodesic components: a finite cover admits a degree-d cyclic cover branched over its preimage.
why: Cited, invoked as black box (C5).

name: global sign characters chi_z, chi_w with chi_w = sigma^* chi_z
statement: Sum of eight Stover-Toledo characters per family; equivariance by passing to sigma-invariant covers.
why: Routine.

name: filling rule (blow up centers, branch exceptional divisor iff k odd), smooth (Z/2)^2 cover V -> M^, distinguished fiber F_*=C x C, normal bundle pr1*L (+) pr2*…
statement: As stated.
why: Standard branched-cover filling of arrangements (Hirzebruch-type).

name: ordinary resolution near F_*: blow up F_*, quotient by s^2, blow up the two fixed curves, quotient by residual involution; glue with [V/<s>] to get orbifold S
statement: As stated.
why: Standard local linearization/blowup.

name: Abel map Sym^2 C = Bl_pt Jac(C); rational section [tau(p), i tau(q)]; f:Y->S; Prop orbifold-surface
statement: Y iterated point blowup of A=Jac(C) mapping into the ordinary locus over o.
why: Classical genus-two geometry.

name: dihedral labels q_z: pi_1(U_T) -> D_inf (red meridians -> r, blue -> b), modified over the red disk by coupling square roots (1 -+ z_1/c)^{1/2}; translation la…
statement: Defined chart-by-chart on finite models; need not define a representation of the global orbifold group.
why: Local (non-global) D_inf labels compatible on buffered overlaps; nothing equivalent found in quick search.

name: Lemma mod:extension
statement: l_z, l_w extend across the blowups and branched fillings of every finite model.
why: Local meridian computation.

name: sum label l = l_z + l_w (s-invariant); Lemma mod:central (order-4 lift of s commuting with deck group; descent to coarse quotient)
statement: As stated; 'central model' vs 'individual model'.
why: Equivariant-cover descent is standard; using the sum only near o is a design choice.

name: Lemma buffer-bound
statement: Nonzero z-translation on a loop over B(x,R) forces dist(x,L_z) <= B_1(R).
why: Compactness/hyperbolic-geometry estimate.

name: Prop kernel-compatibility (buffered agreement of individual kernels; sum kernel = intersection far from o)
statement: As stated.
why: Key compatibility; specific to this design.

name: graphs G_T(u): vertices = points of the covering, edges = paths with projected diameter < u; central quotient graph
statement: 'A word of arbitrary length in loops supported in one fixed bounded region can be one edge.'
why: Equivalent in effect to coning off bounded regions (electrification, Farb 1998; coned-off Cayley graphs).

name: Prop model-hyperbolicity
statement: Uniform u, delta such that every component of every G_T(u) and G_cen(u) is delta-hyperbolic, also after omitting analytic subsets.
why: Quasi-isometry to a hyperbolic cone over the ideal arrangement complement.

name: Lemma bounded-core
statement: Vertices over a bounded radial region have bounded graph diameter.
why: Direct.

name: arrangement-preserving collar near the sphere at infinity; metric d_K=|1-<xi,eta>|^{1/2}; ideal metric d_I via projected path diameter
statement: As stated, with transversality from arithmetic nondegeneracy.
why: d_K is the Koranyi-type (Carnot) gauge; collar standard.

name: Lemma mod:cone (hyperbolic cone over any bounded metric space)
statement: Graph C(I) with vertical edges and horizontal edges at height t when d_I <= e^{-t} is hyperbolic with absolute constant; distance formula t+t'-2j(+3).
why: Bonk-Schramm hyperbolic cone / Groves-Manning combinatorial horoball.

name: Thm orbifold-cyclic
statement: For sufficiently deep arithmetic level, im(f_*:pi_1(Y)->pi_1(S)) = Z.
why: Assembly.

name: Lemma app:surface-comparison
statement: Images of generators of pi_1(Y) equal images of loops in C x {q_0} subset V, representable near F_* in the sign-covered arrangement complement.
why: Normal push-off.

name: Lemma app:cyclic-upper (coupling relations k h_i = 1 identify the red meridians)
statement: Image of pi_1(C x {q_0}) in pi_1(V), hence of pi_1(Y) in pi_1(S), is cyclic (quotient of D_inf even part).
why: Short local computation once F14 is given.

name: graph G on the ordinary open set O; central charts (dist < J to Gamma o) vs individual charts (hyperplanes meeting B(x,K)); constants R=(2N+100)(u+1), J, K
statement: As stated.
why: Bookkeeping.

name: Lemma app:chart-axioms
statement: The readings satisfy (P1)-(P3).
why: Case analysis.

name: Lemma app:orbifold-meridians
statement: pi_1(U)->pi_1(T) surjective with kernel normally generated by transverse-disk boundaries (m-th powers of meridians).
why: Standard orbifold van Kampen.

name: Lemma app:true-relations
statement: A loop of edges of G nullhomotopic in S is trivial in P(G).
why: Subdivision + local closure; correctness-critical.

name: infinite order: the pushed loop e has nonzero sum label; every power e^n is a single edge with distinct read endpoints
statement: Hence every nonzero power of e is nontrivial in pi_1(S).
why: Payoff of F26; one step once F08 and F26 are in place.

name: Lemma ambient-realization (relative Godeaux-Serre)
statement: Smooth effective proper DM stack T with projective coarse space, Y -> T in ordinary locus => smooth projective fivefold S containing Y with pi_1(S) = pi_1(T).
why: Godeaux-Serre/Totaro method with a containment constraint plus Ehresmann deformation trick.

name: Lemma ambient-blowdown
statement: Given Y_1 subset S with (-1)-curve E and blowdown b:Y_1->Y_0, there are S_0 superset Y_0 and theta:pi_1(S)=pi_1(S_0) compatible with b_*.
why: Atiyah-flop-type contraction with an explicit polarization; classical local model, new global packaging.

name: Thm cyclic-embedding
statement: Simple abelian surface A subset S' smooth projective with im(pi_1 A -> pi_1 S') = Z.
why: Assembly.

name: Proof of Thm main (fourfold)
statement: Apply F03 to F41.
why: Assembly.

name: Fourfold witness: coupled red/blue pencil arrangement whose coupling hyperplanes collapse the genus-two surface group to the even part of D_inf, read by local …
why: Nothing in the goal or in L mentions arrangements, dihedral labels or coupling hyperplanes; the object is invented to make im(pi_1 A) exactly Z. It is simultaneously the source of the relations (cyclic upper bound) and of the local covers (infinite lower bound); all of sections 4-6 depend on it. The labels are deliberately NOT a global representation: a global one is impossible because some power of the generator must die in every bounded-rank linear representation (EKPR).

name: Surface witness: genus-zero 48-marked family from [4] on the Eisenstein curve, controlled through its torus lift so monodromy is pro-2 degree-raising
why: Makes the Bogomolov-Katzarkov route work in genus zero with a provable infinite quotient; BK's infinitude stayed conditional and Eyssidieux-Funar showed most BK candidates ARE holomorphically convex. Not a subterm of the goal.

name: Economical involution presentation: 24 relators sigma(g)g^{-1} of degree w_g+1 impose sigma-coinvariance with cost tG(t), P=(1+t)G, via the acyclic Frattini di…
why: Self-described reusable mechanism; it is exactly what produces the GS margin (1-G(t)<0 at t<1/4); without it the relations of the pinched sphere would exhaust the generator budget. The d^2=0 acyclicity computation is not in L.

name: Local path criterion with projected-diameter edges: detect infinite order from charts alone, every power of a short loop being one edge
why: Proves infinite order with no global representation and no finite quotients: the only conceivable kind of argument, since EKPR forces non-linearity. The diameter-not-length edge convention is the trick that makes Z^2 translation covers hyperbolic and powers single edges.

name: Abelian-surface reduction: simple A with pi_1-image Z gives C^2/Z^3 ~ T^3 x R in X~ (H_3 != 0, non-Stein), while adding a large abelian factor makes X large
why: Clean new obstruction to the large-pi_1 form: no compact subvarieties, yet a closed non-Stein submanifold. Separates the geometry (step 1) from the group theory (everything else).

name: Fourfold witness: coupled red/blue pencil arrangement with local dihedral translation labels
statement: Two 6-slope pencils in B^4 (z- and w-families; 4 red slopes |lambda|<0.01, 2 blue |lambda|>4) plus coupling hyperplanes z_1=+-c, w_1=+-c (0.85<c/sqrt a<0.9) meeting only the red slopes, symmetric under sigma(z,w)=(w,-z), embedded exactly in deep congruence ball quotients. Coupling relations k h_i=1 force the image of the genus-two surface group to lie in the even part <rb> of D_inf = <r,b>; chart-local labels q_z: red->r, blue->b, modified over the red disk by (1-+z_1/c)^{1/2}, give integer tra…
why: No equivalent object found in searches A-D (see test1.searches); it is not a subterm of the goal or of L; it is load-bearing for the entire fourfold. F3 (auxiliary construction): the arrangement plus its chart-local labels exist only to drive the proof. The N3 grade is provisional; it would fall to N2 if test 4 shows that the frame (pencil + D_inf + 'collapse red meridians') is readily proposed, or if an expert identifies coupling-type arrangements in the ball-quotient literature.

name: Surface witness: genus-zero 48-marked Eisenstein family controlled through its torus lift (degree-raising pro-2 monodromy)
statement: Spheres with markings f^{-1}(omega_bar^j s), where f is induced by [4] on E=C/Z[omega]; at s_*=q(e_0) the 48 markings collide in 24 pairs. Monodromy is computed on the 7-generator torus group F (weights 1,1,1,1,1,2,2), where three explicit double covers Y_j^2=q(z)-omega_bar^j s show it is trivial in degree one and hence degree-raising on the pro-2 Magnus algebra. The comparison with the actual 47-generator sphere group goes through the surjection p:K->Pi and the core-collapsed L.
why: No equivalent object found in searches A-D, and it passes tests 2-3. Confidence is lower than C1 because the paper names BK's passage as its architecture and the degree-raising principle is known; the witness is a careful instantiation of a named programme. It falls to N2 if test 4 arm R (BK route plus 'use a pro-2 GS quotient') yields isogeny-lifted genus-0 families readily.

name: Economical involution presentation: 24 relators sigma(g)g^{-1} imposing sigma-coinvariance at cost tG(t), via the acyclic Frattini differential and the shift-a…
statement: On L free pro-2 with basis u_{il,j}=delta_{T1}^i delta_{T2}^l(a_{0,j}) (weights i+l+1), choose g lifting a basis of C=span{u^a v^b: a in {0,2}} in F_2[u,v]/(u^4,v^4); the relators r_g=sigma(g)g^{-1} have degree w_g+1, their normal closure equals the sigma-coinvariant kernel, and P(t)=(1+t)G(t) with G=3t(1+t)(1+t^2)^2, leaving 1-G(t)<0 just below t=1/4.
why: Mechanism precedented by Koch-Venkov's sigma-group refinement of GS (sigma-inverted relators lie one level deeper), with a Jennings-type basis; the implementation (acyclic Frattini differential, P=(1+t)G) is new but is a variant. Downgraded from the analyst's weak N3.

name: Local path criterion with projected-diameter edges (representation-free infinite-order detection)
statement: If readings of paths of length <= N in charts satisfy prefix/reverse compatibility, prefix-change compatibility and uniform delta-hyperbolicity, with N >= N_0(delta), then a single-edge loop that does not close on reading is nontrivial modulo short closing loops. Edges are paths of projected diameter < u, so every power of a short loop is one edge, and Z^2 translation covers become hyperbolic.
why: Variant of Gromov/Delzant-Gromov Cartan-Hadamard, with named viewpoint in the paper; diameter edges are electrification. Strategically important (it is the representation-free argument EKPR forces), but not new machinery.

name: Abelian-surface reduction and the C^2/Z^3 non-Stein obstruction
statement: A simple abelian surface A in S' with pi_1-image Z yields, by a general complete intersection in S' x B (B an abelian 6-fold), a fourfold with large pi_1 whose universal cover contains C^2/Z^3 ~ T^3 x R (H_3=Z), which is not Stein by Andreotti-Frankel; simplicity of A excludes compact curves.
why: No exact precedent found, but it is a short combination of Andreotti-Frankel, toroidal groups and the Nori-string pattern, and it is borderline analytic. Its value is strategic (it reduces the large-pi_1 problem to a single group-theoretic image).

name: Finite local detection and descent
statement: Choose a finite quotient of a dense profinite image that is injective on every local boundary group; the associated cover compactifies to a smooth projective X with rho_X factoring.
why: Self-described 'reusable mechanism', but a standard device; serves as a negative control.

name: Ambient realization and ambient blowdown (relative Godeaux-Serre + Atiyah-type contraction with explicit polarization)
statement: Replace an orbifold by a smooth projective fivefold containing a given surface with the same pi_1; realize a point blowdown of an embedded surface in a new smooth projective ambient variety preserving pi_1 and the surface homomorphism.
why: Named classical constructions adapted with routine global care.

name: The hypersurface H and algebra A=P/(H)
statement: P=C[p,s,u,F,J], x=s^2+u^3+p^2F, H=x^2F-(1+2sx)J-p^2J^2-pu, A=P/(H). In localized coordinates (x,y,z,u) over C[p,p^-1] it reads H=p^-2(xy-z(z+1))-pu (I02).
why: Counterexample objects to a 70-year-old problem in char 0 do not exist in L (Gupta's char-p families do not lift; Dubouloz-Ghosh 2025 give only 'potential' counterexamples). The example is tiny (one quintic-ish polynomial in 5 variables) yet occurs nowhere in the goal-as-posed or L, matching the Cook-Reckhow profile. Risk: the design may be templated (El Kahoui-Ouali residual coordinate + Asanuma-type twist p^3u=xy-z(z+1) of a non-line), which would cap it at N2.

name: x,y,z and xy-z(z+1)=p^2(H+pu)
statement: y=s+x(x-u^3), z=sx+p^2J; identity xy-z(z+1)=p^2(H+pu). Over C[p,p^-1], (x,y,z,u) are coordinates with inverse s=y-x(x-u^3), F=p^-2(x-s^2-u^3), J=p^-2(z-sx).
why: Given H, a computation; conceptually it is the design key of I01, already credited there.

name: Lemma con:domain (A integral, dim 4, A[p^-1]=Laurent poly ring)
statement: A is a domain of dimension 4, p!=0 in A, A[p^-1]=C[p,p^-1,x,y,z].
why: Routine UFD/transcendence-degree argument. Lean proves it differently (L03).

name: Locally nilpotent derivation Delta=-p^2 d/du and exponential shift Phi=exp(w Delta)
statement: Delta fixes p,x,y,z, Delta u=-p^2; its values on s,F,J lie in P so Delta is an LND of P with Delta H=p^3, Delta^2H=0; Phi(H)=H+p^3w, A[w]=T:=P[w]/(H+p^3w).
why: Explicitly the El Kahoui-Ouali method.

name: Determinant-one change (L,M) in (F,J) and B=C[p,s,u,M]
why: Explicit coordinate change; existence is guaranteed by the residual-coordinate property built into I01.

name: Root L*=pu-p^2C mod p^3 and fifth coordinate e0 with certificate p^3e0-(L-L*)=(p^2Q1(L)-1)(H(L)+p^3w)
statement: C=Q(0), Q1=(Q-C)/L, L*=pu-p^2C, h=u-pQ-p^3F^3-p^2w, e0=-w-pF^3-Q1h; then p^3 e=L-L* in T and T=B[e]=C[p,s,u,M,e].
why: Explicit inverse for a case covered by cited theorems (Edo-Venereau Thm 7, Maubach Thm 4.5, El Kahoui-Ouali Thm 1.1).

name: Prop stabilization: A[w] = C^[5]
statement: There is a C-algebra isomorphism A[w]=C^[5]; explicit generators Phi^-1(p,s,u,M,e0).
why: Known theorem applied to I01; novelty lies in I01 being residual.

name: Cor stable-coordinate: H is a coordinate of P[w] but not of P (SCC fails in ambient dim 5)
statement: Via Dutta-Lahiri Thm 3.4 and Thm main.
why: Immediate from main theorem + cited theorem.

name: S=C[p,x,y,z,u]/(xy-z(z+1)-p^3u), R=S/pS=C[x,y,z,u]/(xy-z(z+1))
statement: Auxiliary subalgebra S of A with S[p^-1]=A[p^-1]; R is the smooth quadric threefold (SL2/T) times A^1_u.
why: A Danielewski/Asanuma-type hypersurface over a known quadric; abbreviation once I01 is fixed.

name: Lemma deg:valuation (S->A injective, ord_p DVR valuation, divisibility)
statement: S embeds in A with same localization; R smooth domain; ord_p from S_{pS} with ord_p(b)>=i iff b in p^iS.
why: Routine.

name: valuation degree deg h=-ord_p(h), filtration F_dA, gr A, initial form in(h), graded injection gr A -> R[tau,tau^-1]
statement: deg is a degree function; gr A injects into R[tau^±] via [h]_d -> (p^d h mod p) tau^-d.
why: Standard construction.

name: s_R, f, g and center I=(f,g) in R
statement: s_R=y-x(x-u^3), f=x-s_R^2-u^3, g=z-s_R x, I=(f,g).
why: Defined by reduction of p^2F, p^2J; abbreviation.

name: Prop graded: gr A = G = R[tau, I/tau^2] = P/(H_top), smooth domain; exact-weight representatives
statement: With weights (p,s,u,F,J)=(-1,0,0,2,2), every h in A has a representative of max weight exactly deg h, G=P/(H_top), H_top=x^2F-(1+2sx)J-p^2J^2; G is an affine modification of R[tau] (Kaliman-Zaidenberg) and smooth.
why: The technique is standard; the specific identification G=R[tau,I/tau^2] (an affine modification with smooth total space) is a nontrivial computation specific to this example.

name: Locally nilpotent derivation (LND); homogeneous derivation of degree shift j
statement: D is LND if every element is killed by some iterate; homogeneous of shift j if it maps degree d to d+j.
why: Textbook.

name: Lemma induced-lnd: LND of A induces nonzero homogeneous LND D_0 of G, invariants pass to initial forms
statement: j=max over generators of deg(Dh_i)-deg h_i; D_0([h]_d)=[Dh]_{d+j}.
why: Standard (re-proved for Z-filtrations).

name: Prop positive-invariant: if A=C^[4], G has a nonzero homogeneous LND with a nonzero homogeneous invariant of positive degree
statement: Some coordinate q_r has positive degree (F_0A is proper since deg F=2); D=d/dq_i kills q_r.
why: Paper names its own precedent (Gupta's Derksen-invariant strategy).

name: Remark: Delta descends to G but moves R (u -> -tau^2)
statement: Coefficient preservation can fail; motivates lifting via line bundle rather than via R.
why: Remark.

name: Determinant ring R~=C[a,d,b,c,u]/(ac-bd-1) with x=ab, y=dc, z=db
statement: SL2 (with u adjoined) mapping to the quadric R; the standard torus bundle SL2 -> SL2/T.
why: Standard object; its use here is I20.

name: v=a^2(x-u^3)-d^2=a^3b-a^2u^3-d^2
statement: Single generator of I R~; fiber weight 2, valuation degree 0.
why: Determined by the example and the bundle; not a free choice.

name: Prop principalization: Spec R~ -> Spec R is a G_m-torsor (line bundle minus zero section), I R~=(v), G~=G⊗_R R~=R~[tau,V]/(tau^2V-v)
statement: Charts D(z+1), D(z); certificate f=C1 v, g=b^2 v, v=alpha f+beta g with alpha C1+beta b^2=1; two commuting gradings (valuation degree, fiber weight).
why: Change-of-representation step: pull back along a known torsor so that the center becomes principal. Close neighbours: Cox-ring/torsor tricks, Danielewski-variety arguments on SL2. Could be N3 if discoverability is low; graded N2 provisionally.

name: Prop linearization: Pic(A^1 x X)=Pic(X) for smooth affine X; unique normalized linear lift of any G_a-action to a line bundle
statement: Picard invariance via Weil divisors; uniqueness via C[t]*=C*; cocycle; induced LND preserves fiber weights.
why: Known results re-proved.

name: Prop homogeneous-lift: D_0 lifts to an LND D~ of G~ of fiber weight 0 and the same valuation shift j
statement: Conjugating by the degree-scaling sigma_lambda, uniqueness of normalized lifts forces homogeneity.
why: Short consequence of I21 uniqueness.

name: Lemma lnd-order: nu_delta additive, kernel factorially closed, delta(h) not in hT
statement: Order nu_delta(h)=max{n: delta^n h != 0}; nu(fg)=nu(f)+nu(g).
why: Textbook (Freudenburg, Algebraic Theory of LNDs, Prop 1.9).

name: Homogeneous pieces of G~: G~_e = tau^-e R~ (e<0), V^l R~ (e=2l), tau V^{l+1} R~ (e=2l+1)
statement: Exact description of each valuation-degree component.
why: Routine computation once I20 is in place. Lean: ModificationGrading.piece_negative/even/odd.

name: Prop extracted-lnd: if A=C^[4], R~ has a nonzero LND E of fiber-weight shift q<=0 with E^2(v)=0
statement: Positive-degree invariant divisible by V forces D~V=0; Case 1 D~tau=0: E=tau^j D~|R~, E(v)=0, q=0. Case 2: j=2l+1 odd, D~(r)=tau V^{l+1}E(r), q=-2(l+1), LND order shows E LND and E^2(v)=0.
why: New lemma, but assembled from standard LND-order and degree-piece bookkeeping; analytic once I20/I24 are given (pivot distance 1). Strengthening via a sign condition q<=0 is the key extra tracked quantity (Remark red:sign-essential).

name: Remark red:sign-essential: E_+ (b->a, c->d) has shift +2, E_+(v)=a^4, E_+^2(v)=0
statement: Shows the sign condition is necessary.
why: Example.

name: Lemma Mason-Stothers (abc for polynomials)
statement: max deg <= r(XYZ)-1 for coprime X+Y=Z not all constant.
why: Classical; in Mathlib.

name: Lemma rig:one-variable: LND of F[t] has delta(t) in F
why: Classical. Lean: LND.polynomial_dX_constant.

name: Auxiliary grading on R~: weights (a,d,b,c,u)=(0,3,-3,0,2)
statement: Z-grading commuting with fiber weight, under which N=d^2+a^2u^3 is homogeneous of degree 6 while a^3b has degree -3.
why: Choosing a grading making a target piece top-degree is a standard move in LND rigidity proofs; the specific vector is found by solving linear constraints (relation homogeneous, N homogeneous, a^3b lower). Low search cost once the strategy is fixed.

name: Highest auxiliary component E'=E_lambda
statement: E'=greatest nonzero shift component; still LND, same fiber shift.
why: Standard (Lean GradedLND.highest).

name: Orbit polynomials a(q),d(q),u(q)=exp(qE')(.) and N(q)=N+qE'(N); nonsquare of -u^3 in K=C(a,d,b)(u)
statement: d(q)^2+a(q)^2u(q)^3=N(q) of degree <=1; pairwise coprime; abc gives D_u=0, D_d=D_a; leading coefficients give (delta/alpha)^2=-u^3 in K, impossible; hence E' fixes a,d,u.
why: Paper names Finston-Maubach precedent; the nonsquare twist is a small variant.

name: h=cE'(b)-bE'(c); R~∩Q=C0=C[a,d,u]; fiber weight e-2<0 contradiction
statement: ah=E'(b), dh=E'(c); h in C0 has nonnegative weight but weight e-2<0.
why: Short computation.

name: Prop rigidity: no nonzero LND E of R~ with fiber shift e<=0 and E^2(v)=0
statement: Combines I29-I32. (Argument actually works for e<=1.)
why: New rigidity statement for a specific ring, proved by a known method (highest component + abc).

name: Theorem main (A integral dim 4, A[w]=C^[5], A not C^[4])
statement: Assembly: I03, I07; contradiction chain I16 -> I22 -> I25 -> I33.
why: Target.

name: Cor affine-fibrations: p:Spec A->A^1 and (p,H):A^5->A^2 are smooth A^3-fibrations, not Zariski-locally trivial (Dolgachev-Weisfeiler fails)
statement: Residual coordinate gives fibers; Jacobian gives smoothness; local triviality + Bass-Connell-Wright + Suslin would give A=C^[4] or H a coordinate.
why: Corollary via cited theorems.

name: residual coordinate; one-stably a coordinate; A^3-fibration; Stable Coordinate Conjecture; fiber weight; normalization of a lift; Pic
statement: Background vocabulary.
why: Literature definitions.

name: The witness polynomial H = x^2F-(1+2sx)J-p^2J^2-pu, x=s^2+u^3+p^2F
why: Resolves a problem open since the 1940s-70s in char 0; none of the many candidate families (Koras-Russell, Asanuma-Gupta, Venereau, Dubouloz-Ghosh 2025 'potential counterexamples') worked. Tiny object (one polynomial in 5 variables), not a subterm of the posed problem or L - the Cook-Reckhow profile. Must satisfy two antagonistic constraints simultaneously: residual coordinate over C[p] (so the cylinder is trivial) and a degeneration whose principalized center v=a^3b-a^2u^3-d^2 carries the nons…

name: Principalizing the center by pulling back along the SL2 -> SL2/T torus bundle, giving G~=R~[tau,V]/(tau^2V-v)
why: Converts the question 'does G carry a homogeneous LND with positive-degree invariant?' into an explicit single-relation ring where degree pieces are explicit (I24); non-analytic relative to the goal. The lift must work even though D_0 does not preserve R (Remark I17) - the paper explicitly flags this obstacle. Large drop in difficulty: after this step, extraction is bookkeeping.

name: Extraction lemma: polynomiality => nonzero LND E of R~ with fiber shift q<=0 and E^2(v)=0
why: New statement; the sign constraint q<=0 is exactly what rigidity needs (Remark I26 shows it is essential). Case 2 (tau moving) uses an LND-order count to get E^2(v)=0 and odd shift j - not obvious.

name: Weighted rigidity: auxiliary grading (0,3,-3,0,2), orbit identity d(q)^2+a(q)^2u(q)^3=N(q) of degree <=1, Mason-Stothers + nonsquare -u^3
why: The auxiliary weight vector isolating N=d^2+a^2u^3 from a^3b is a specific find; non-analytic. Combining abc with a nonsquare argument in the original fraction field is a small new twist (paper's own remark).

name: Positive-degree invariant obstruction from polynomiality
why: Neat replacement of the Derksen invariant by a single positive-degree coordinate.

name: The witness polynomial H (and the fourfold A = P/(H))
statement: P = C[p,s,u,F,J], x = s^2+u^3+p^2F, H = x^2F - (1+2sx)J - p^2J^2 - pu, A = P/(H). Design: over C[p^{+-1}], H = p^{-2}(xy - z(z+1)) - pu is a coordinate; mod p, H is linear in F,J with unimodular coefficients (x0^2, -(1+2s x0)), so H is a residual coordinate over C[p]; A contains S = C[p,x,y,z,u]/(xy - z(z+1) - p^3u) (Danielewski-type twist of (SL2/T quadric) x A^1) and A = S[f/p^2, g/p^2] is an affine modification along the non-principal divisor V(f,g) = A^2_{s,u} of R = S/pS, whose pullback to…
why: No near-equivalent witness found in any field; the char-0 problem was listed as open by human experts in July 2026 and by Ghosh (April 2026). The strategy is not new (Asanuma's ring, Gupta's 'tempting' affine-fibration route, El Kahoui-Ouali stabilization are all in L), so the eureka content is the specific design that makes non-polynomiality PROVABLE: the Danielewski twist of the SL2/T quadric plus a non-principal A^2 centre whose Cox/torsor pullback is a single v carrying the -u^3 nonsquare. …

name: Principalizing the centre through the SL2 -> SL2/T torus bundle and lifting the additive action
statement: Spec R~ -> Spec R (R~ = C[a,d,b,c,u]/(ac-bd-1)) is a G_m-torsor in which I R~ = (v), v = a^3b - a^2u^3 - d^2, so G~ = G (x)_R R~ = R~[tau,V]/(tau^2V - v); every homogeneous LND of G lifts uniquely (normalized, fibre-linear) to a homogeneous LND of G~ of fibre weight 0.
why: Its form is precedented: principalize on the Cox torsor and lift the action there (Arzhantsev-Gaifullin 2010, ADHL book); Brion (in L) covers the lift. It is N2 rather than N1 because the object it acts on (gr A of a new witness) and the homogeneity bookkeeping are specific. It would be F5 if it were N3. Borderline N1.

name: Extraction lemma: polynomiality gives an LND E of R~ with fibre shift q <= 0 and E^2(v) = 0
statement: If A = C^[4], the positive-degree invariant is divisible by V, so D~V = 0; Case 1 (D~tau = 0): E = tau^j D~|R~, E(v) = 0, q = 0; Case 2: j odd, D~(r) = tau V^{l+1} E(r), q = -2(l+1) < 0, and LND-order counting gives E^2(v) = 0.
why: A new statement for a new ring, assembled from textbook LND-order facts once C2 is in place. Tracking the sign of the fibre shift is the key extra datum (Remark I26 shows it is necessary). The 'templated strengthening' cap concerns induction hypotheses and does not apply directly, but the content is bookkeeping. Sibling 049 reuses it.

name: Weighted rigidity: auxiliary grading (0,3,-3,0,2) + Mason-Stothers + nonsquare -u^3
statement: No nonzero LND E of R~ with fibre shift <= 0 has E^2(v) = 0: the highest auxiliary component E' satisfies (E')^2(d^2 + a^2u^3) = 0; orbit polynomials obey d(q)^2 + a(q)^2u(q)^3 = N(q) of degree <= 1; abc plus the nonsquareness of -u^3 in C(a,d,b)(u) force E' to fix a, d, u; then h = cE'(b) - bE'(c) in C[a,d,u] has weight e - 2 < 0, a contradiction.
why: The paper names its own precedent, which is in L. The new elements are the weight vector (fixed by linear constraints) and keeping leading coefficients in Frac(R~) for the nonsquare. That is a small variant. 049 shows the step depends on the witness's exponents rather than being a free-standing device.

name: Positive-degree invariant obstruction
statement: If A = C^[4], some coordinate has positive valuation degree (since deg F = 2), and d/dq_i for another coordinate kills it; the induced homogeneous LND of G = gr A has a nonzero homogeneous invariant of positive degree.
why: Downgraded from the analyst's N2: it specializes Gupta's Derksen-invariant method, which the paper names and which is in L. Borderline N2 only because of the Z-filtration care noted in the paper and the Lean's non-homogeneous variant.

name: Exact graded identification gr A = G = R[tau, I/tau^2] = P/(H_top)
statement: With weights (p,s,u,F,J) = (-1,0,0,2,2), each h in A has a representative of top weight exactly deg h; G = P/(H_top), with H_top = x^2F - (1+2sx)J - p^2J^2, is a smooth affine modification of R[tau] (Kaliman-Zaidenberg).
why: Downgraded from the analyst's N2. Computing gr of a hypersurface by its top-weight form is standard; the identification with R[tau, I/tau^2] is a computation once H is fixed, and Lean does it by a routine Rees argument. Borderline N2 if one credits the exactness check.

name: L log L Orlicz class
statement: L log L(T) = {f : int |f| log(2+|f|) dmu < infinity}, mu normalized Lebesgue measure on T = R/2piZ.
why: Textbook Zygmund class.

name: Fourier coefficients and symmetric partial sums S_N f
statement: hat f(k) = int f e^{-ikx} dmu, S_N f = sum_{|k|<=N} hat f(k) e^{ikx}.
why: Textbook.

name: Thm main: a.e. convergence in L log L (thm:main)
statement: For every complex f in L log L(T) there is a null set N_f with S_N f(x) -> f(x) for x outside N_f, along the full sequence N = 0,1,2,...
why: Headline claim; graded via its machinery.

name: Uncentred interval maximal function M rho and good set G_rho = {M rho <= e^{4h}}, h = log log d
statement: M rho(x) = sup over arcs I containing x of the average of rho on I; G_rho = {M rho <= e^{4h}}; weak (1,1) gives |G_rho^c| <= C e^{-4h} = C (log d)^{-4}.
why: Maximal function is N0; restricting to its sublevel set at height (log d)^4 is a parameter choice of a known good-set strategy (Lie 2013).

name: Thm good-set: truncated integral estimate (thm:good-set)
statement: Absolute C, d_*: if d >= d_*, rho >= 0 periodic, int rho = 1, rho <= e^d a.e., then int over G_rho of sup_N |S_N rho| <= C d.
why: A good-set L1 estimate for one height layer is a known reduction template (Lie 2013 Prop 3.1); the novelty is the endpoint quantification (loss exactly d, exceptional set (log d)^{-4}), which is the whole difficulty but not a new concept.

name: Prop bounded inputs: a.e. convergence for bounded f (prop:fourier-bounded)
statement: Every bounded complex periodic function has a.e. convergence of S_N f along the full sequence; proof via Fejer means P_l, Thm good-set with d_l = d_* + log(2B/m_l), Markov.
why: Statement is classical (a special case of Carleson-Hunt). The proof route is new only in that it goes through Thm good-set.

name: Doubly exponential height layers f_j and d_j = 2^{j+1} + log^- m_j
statement: f = f_bd + sum_j f_j, f_j = f 1{e^{2^j} <= |f| < e^{2^{j+1}}}; four nonnegative parts q_j with mass m_j, rho_j = q_j/m_j <= e^{d_j}; sum m_j d_j < infinity iff int |f| log|f| < infinity (plus an entropy term).
why: Standard dyadic-in-log layer decomposition; the doubly exponential spacing is what makes (log d_j)^{-4} summable.

name: Cor weak-L1 maximal bound with Luxemburg norm (cor:fourier-weak-l1)
statement: Phi(t) = t log(2+t), ||f||_Phi Luxemburg; sup_lambda lambda mu{S* f > lambda} <= C ||f||_Phi for all f in L log L(T; C).
why: Direct application of Stein's 1961 continuity principle to the a.e.-finite maximal function.

name: Signed span [D] of a finite list
statement: [D] = { sum_{v in D} eps_v v : eps_v in {-1,0,1} }.
why: Standard.

name: Two laws: uniform output law U versus true input law P (dP = rho/m_top dU)
statement: U follows a uniformly chosen output point (fair bits); P is weighted by the current input; noisy labels are observations of the input point; processing choices depend only on spatial and membership state.
why: A change-of-measure / duality framing; the specific coupling of the two laws through a Fisher-information identity is new, but the device of weighting by the density is classical.

name: Compression parameters h, T, w, L, m_*
statement: h = log log d, T = floor(d h^{-5}), w = (log d)^{1/4}, L = d exp(w), m_* = floor(exp(w^3)).
why: Parameter choices.

name: Lemma entropy compression (lemma:compression)
statement: q strictly positive pmf on Z with q(x)/q(0) = int chi_{gx} d omega, -log q(0) <= D0 d; finite S with log|nS| <= D0 d h^{P0} log d for n <= d^2; d/h^2 <= E <= D0 d and -log E_lambda H_q(X_1+..+X_T - X'_1-..-X'_T) <= E for every prob lambda on S. Then there are x0 in S and S' subset S with log|S| - log|S'| <= C(D0) d^2/(E h^2) and, for EVERY probability v on S', int exp(-L sum_x v(x)(1 - Re chi_{g(x-x0)})) d omega >= e^{-CE}.
why: Passes a quick no-near-equivalent check: its conclusion (one centre and one omega-region good for all weights on S') and its hypothesis (uniform bound on noisy 2T-fold sums) do not match Chang/Lee/Bloom/Kelley-Meka statements. Risk: a judge may call it an entropy variant of Chang's lemma (N2).

name: Lemma noisy sum with prescribed marginals (entropy-foundations:variational)
statement: There is an exchangeable law of X^T with uniform marginals on S and Gamma in TS-TS such that D(X^T || U_S^T) + I(X^T; Z) + E c(Gamma) <= E, Z = sum X_i + Gamma; proved by finite Gibbs variational duality (dual: sup over multipliers a of sum E a - log max_z sum e^{sum a(x_i)} H_q(z - sum x_i)).
why: Close neighbour named by the paper (Lee 2017 entropy maximization).

name: Noisy-sum entropy cost C_p(X^s, Gamma) = D(X^s||p^s) + I(X^s; Z) + E c(Gamma)
statement: Cost of a correlated letter vector with an error Gamma relative to a product law p; nonnegative, convex in the joint law.
why: A conjunction of standard quantities (relative entropy, mutual information, expected cost); new as a packaged potential. Borderline N1/N2.

name: Lemma projection and conditioning rules (entropy-foundations:cost-rules)
statement: (i) dropping letters and keeping the error does not increase C_p; (ii) conditioning on finite J costs at most H(J); (iii) conditioning on a prefix is free and the comparison product can be changed to nu^k.
why: Direct chain-rule consequences.

name: Lemma selection of a conditional marginal (entropy-foundations:exchangeable)
statement: Conditioning the exchangeable law on a random prefix of length in [T/4, T/2] gives a marginal nu with log|S| - H(nu) <= CE/T, cost <= CE, and m_*-blocks within TV C m_* sqrt(E)/T of nu^{m_*}.
why: Pinning lemma is a close known neighbour (not cited by the paper).

name: Context W, refinement, and the functionals G_s(W), I_r(W), K_m(W; r)
statement: Context = finite variable jointly distributed with X ~ nu; G_s = H(sum of s iid letters | contexts); I_r = inf over couplings of r H(X|W) - H(X^r | sum, W^r); K_m(W; r) = noisy block cost with error Gamma.
why: Built from entropic-sumset vocabulary; new functionals but close to known quantities.

name: Lemma monotonicities and uniform entropy bounds (entropy-foundations:context-bounds)
statement: G_s nondecreasing in s, nonincreasing under refinement, <= D_* = C(D0) d for s <= m_*; I_r nonnegative, nondecreasing in r, nonincreasing under refinement, <= D_* for r <= T0.
why: Routine.

name: Lemma lifting block sums and refining contexts (entropy-foundations:block-cost)
statement: K_m unchanged if block sums are replaced by full iid m-letter rows; K_m nonincreasing under refinement.
why: Routine coupling lemma.

name: Lemma low-end noisy cost via thinning (entropy-foundations:thinning)
statement: For m <= m_*, 2mr <= T0, r <= T e^{-w^2}/2: K_m(W; r) <= CE, by tagging blocks with the common submeasure min(mu, Q), weighted acceptance B/(2r), and filling with R = (Q - eta)/delta.
why: Coupling bookkeeping.

name: Lemma gluing two couplings (entropy-refinement:gluing)
statement: Observing (sum of m letters, other contexts) refines W to W' with G_1(W)-G_1(W') = G_m(W)-G_{m-1}(W) and I_r(W)-I_r(W') >= K_m(W;r) - K_{m-1}(W;r); partial (Bernoulli-marked) observations scale both.
why: Elementary but well-aimed inequality; a judge would likely see it as a variant of entropy-increment arguments.

name: Prop finite refinement search with two visit orders (entropy-refinement:search)
statement: There is a finite refinement W and index j with G_1(empty) - G_1(W) <= C D_*^2/(E h^2) and K_{m_{j,1}}(W; r_j) <= K_{m_{j,0}}(W; r_j) + E. Proof: macroblocks ascending, subblocks descending, indices ascending, with skip rules p > c0/alpha0 + delta0 and P > c1/alpha1 + delta1; two telescopes (endpoint telescope for skips, exact-cost telescope for completed targets).
why: Weak N3: a hard-to-find combinatorial schedule that buys the h^{-2} saving the endpoint needs; nearest neighbours are generic increment/pigeonhole schedules. Could be graded N2 (it is a scheduling device inside a templated increment argument).

name: Freezing contexts and extracting one phase region (completion of lemma:compression)
statement: Freeze a context stack, compare with independent law p x q, find an atom z_* with Q_Z(z_*) >= q(0) e^{-CE}, write it as int prod |E chi_{gX}| d omega, restrict to R = {sum(1-|phi_i|^2) <= C_R E}, pick a coordinate and centre x0 by Markov, prune to S' of mass >= 1/2.
why: Standard extraction.

name: Thermal forms A = sum lambda_s (1 - Re chi_s), form order, q_A, F(A), K_A, Delta_A, B_A(r) (Definition Thermal forms)
statement: q_A(u) = Fourier coefficients of e^{-A}; F(A) = -log q_A(0) (free energy); K_A = e^{F-A} probability density; Delta_A(u) = ||1 - chi_u||_{L2(K_A)}; B_A(r) = {u : Delta_A(u) <= r}.
why: Transfer of XY-model Gibbs densities plus a Bohr-type metric; new packaging, close neighbours in stat mech and additive combinatorics (Bohr sets).

name: Lemma thermal positivity and monotonicity (lemma:thermal-monotonicity)
statement: q_A is a nonnegative even pmf; Cov_{K_A}(Re chi_u, Re chi_v) >= 0; hence coefficients increase and Delta_A decreases in form order, Delta_A is subadditive, F is increasing with decreasing increments; envelope bound for products of shifted thermal weights.
why: Cross-field transfer from statistical mechanics (Griffiths-Ginibre inequalities); re-proved for this one-site case.

name: Thermal labels Z = Y + theta, theta ~ K_A; label updates A+ = A + S_p + D_i; spatial forms S_p = R_p^2 (1 - Re chi_1)
statement: A noisy observation of the input point with XY-Gibbs noise; on each success the form is tightened by a spatial term at the current interval and a metric term D_i = lambda B; label errors independent given Y; choices never inspect sampled labels.
why: An auxiliary random variable built only to transfer frequency information into information-theoretic currency; no near neighbour found in the Carleson literature (quick search). Risk: noisy-channel/Gaussian-smoothing devices are common in information theory (e.g. de Bruijn identity, stochastic localization), so a judge may see transfer (N2).

name: Global label Fisher sum: sum over live jumping pieces of U(p) alpha_e J_p <= C d, with J_p = int |D|^2/M
statement: M_pm, M, D are the label-weighted child masses; the Fisher sum is bounded by the total information budget d + log h + E B_mem + O(d) via the chain rule and 'squared bias <= 2 x relative entropy to a fair bit'.
why: Known mechanism (entropy chain rule over a dyadic filtration, cf. Friedgut-style entropy proofs, martingale square function), new application.

name: Separated spectrum -> compression problem: high integers, separated collections avoiding B_A(r_sep) + {|j| <= sigma R_p}, snapping to gZ, polarizing v_x, sumse…
statement: Verifies the hypotheses of I12 for the label-weighted child moments: sumset size via a positive Riesz-type product over a dissociated subset (|Lambda| <= C d/beta^2) and the moment cap E_T(nu) <= D0 d via thermal envelope bounds.
why: Transfer of Chang/Lee dissociated-spectrum argument; the label side information is the only adaptation.

name: Gap potential F(A) - log|B_A(r)| with tracked radius r = r_sep/4 + eta x (number of additions)
statement: Starts at 0, bounded below by a numerical constant, increases by <= C2 t at a regular success, decreases by >= k_b/2 at a cheap success; telescoping gives sum_cheap k_b <= 2 C2 sum_regular t + C.
why: A non-obvious monovariant mixing two currencies (free energy and packing entropy) whose drop at cheap updates is exactly what is needed; no near-equivalent found. Risk: increment-potential arguments are a standard template (N2).

name: Lemma spectral update (lemma:spectral-update)
statement: Under count/form caps, a request at level b yields t in [d/h^2, D0 d], t >= eps k_b, a metric form D_i = lambda B with flat free-energy increment, and an input-only success set; either (i) regular test with success probability >= beta/2 and E_T(nu) >= t/4, or (ii) cheap deterministic update with t = eps k_b and uniform nu; log|S'| >= 0.8 k_b; gap potential bounds as in I29.
why: The regular/cheap dichotomy with an iterated compression (t shrinks by 4 each round) and a flat-increment selection is specific to this proof; components are N0-N2 but the update as a whole has no near neighbour found.

name: Prop regular evidence (prop:thermal-evidence)
statement: With N_h = ceil(h^{120}) fresh evidence clones per regular success, the observable event {some clone Z' with A(Z'-Z) <= 4 s_d and |sum nu(x) v_x(Z') chi_{gx}(V)| >= beta/4} has reference probability <= e^{-t/8}, while under the true law it occurs at every regular success except with probability o(h^{-20}).
why: Standard hypothesis-testing logic with a specific device (evidence clones).

name: Prop modulated delayed Haar estimate (prop:dyadic)
statement: For d >= d0, interval I with |I| in [1/2,1], rho <= e^d, mean <= 2, F_{j+1}-measurable multipliers |eps_j| <= 1 shared by all modulations, stopping time tau(x) = first j with E_{p_j(x)} rho > e^{4h}: int over I of max_{|u| <= Q} |sum_{j < tau} E_{p_j}[rho chi_u r_{j+1}] eps_j r_{j+2}| dx/|I| <= C d, uniformly in I, rho, J, Q, multipliers.
why: The lemma itself is a strong eureka candidate: a model-operator estimate whose statement encodes the right endpoint (L1 bound Cd per layer, stopping at (log d)^4) and whose proof is wholly new. As a statement it is a 'dyadic version of the conjecture', which a judge could call analytic (N2).

name: Finite procedure: live/static pieces, epochs, plateaus (normalization alpha, reset if m > 2 alpha), transfer rules (m < e^{-d}, Q > R0 d, n >= C0 h), membershi…
statement: A deterministic stopping/splitting procedure on the dyadic tree that partitions rho into plateau pieces whose normalized contributions sum exactly to the transform.
why: A stopping-tree decomposition (classical template: CZ / Carleson-measure stopping times, Lacey-Thiele tree selection) with new splitting rules.

name: Prop live budgets (prop:live-budgets)
statement: (i) per-branch sum k_b + sum t + sum relative metric costs <= Cd, n <= Ch; (ii) ||B_mem||_{L2(P)} + ||X_*||_{L2(P)} <= Ch, P(transfer) <= C h^{-10}; (iii) sum_live U(p_e) alpha_e <= Ch and kill sums <= 1; (iv) global label Fisher sum <= Cd (I27); (v) spatial bit relative entropies O(d), O(h) if stopped at the cutoff.
why: Many budgets, each by a standard probabilistic tool; the inductive caps (form cap, count cap) are an IH strengthening by tracked quantities (templated).

name: Reference law Q (fair membership coins) and score supermartingale S with factor exp((t/16) 1{success and evidence}) / (1 + e^{-t/16})
statement: Change of measure: P(S > R e^d) <= e^{-d}; combined with R <= exp(d + log h + B_mem) excludes Q > 1000 d outside probability O(h^{-10}).
why: Standard change-of-measure.

name: Prop capture on a plateau (prop:capture) incl. trimmed masks, polynomial products Q_z, edge charges, snapshots, activation
statement: Cumulative list D with appends at jumping post states; non-bad high u is within poly(1+|D|, d_1, 1/b)/|p| of [D]; E|D|_final <= C d_1 b^{-C}; bad-edge charges O(d) (one scalar level) and poly(h)(h + log d) (all main levels); snapshots of <= ceil(e^{k_{b/2}}) main or exp(C(d_1 + log 1/b)) scalar representatives with expected count poly(D_max, d_1, 1/b); non-bad high jumps before activation lie in one block of <= H_b depths.
why: Riesz-product entropy increment (Lee 2017) + windowed likelihood charging; strong but templated.

name: Lemma predictable signs (lemma:paths-sign)
statement: For fair signs r_{i+1} and F_i-measurable c_i: outside probability e^{-t}, sum c_i r_{i+1} <= (theta/2) sum c_i^2 + t/theta for every prefix.
why: Textbook.

name: Prop scalar plateau paths (prop:scalar-path) with potential psi(x) = b^{1/2}((|x|^2+b^2)^{3/4} - b^{3/2})
statement: Masked delayed transform on any contiguous interval is <= C b^{1/4}(1 + K_e + t) outside probability C e^{-t}.
why: Bellman-function technique (Burkholder; Nazarov-Treil-Volberg) with a new specific potential.

name: Lemma energy drift and innovations (lemma:paths-innovation)
statement: G_pre = G + g + r U_p; |a - vD|^2 <= M g_z; |U_p|^2 <= C max(G_pm)(J + g); (int|a|)^2 <= C(GJ + g); forward budgets E sum g <= C, E sum J <= Cd, E sum xi <= 2.
why: Routine.

name: Lemma delayed norm estimate on a run with absolute Fisher coefficient (lemma:paths-run-norm)
statement: On an outer-valid run, outside probability C e^{-t}, int |W_P(z)| dz <= C sum J_p + C lambda^{-1}(1 + sum xi + sum e') + C lambda t, lambda = b^{1/2}; proof via two-step blocks and concavity of the norm of X_0 = (W, f, lambda M).
why: Likely N2: a Bellman-function-style concavity estimate; the augmentation of the state by lambda M to get an absolute Fisher coefficient is clever but templated (add a tracked coordinate).

name: Prop vector estimates on inner-valid intervals with Fisher checkpoints (prop:vector-path) and Lemma simultaneous representatives / random dyadic list caps (lem…
statement: Predictable origins (run starts + checkpoints whenever accumulated J reaches 1) with expected number <= P(d, 1/b0); every inner-valid interval I satisfies int|sum a_p eps r| <= C sum_I J + C b^{-1/2}(1 + K_e + E_{e,b}) + C b^{1/2} t; parameters t_b, H_b chosen simultaneously over all representatives and all dyadic caps with E t_b <= C k_{b/4} + C log(Cd/b).
why: Bookkeeping.

name: Assembly of Prop dyadic: plateau reduction, exact decoding c_A(n) = 1 - Delta_A(n)^2/2 >= 1/2, scalar prefix, static families, rare transfers
statement: sup_u |T_e^u| is bounded by a frequency-independent majorant (eq 09-live-majorant); main levels cost O(d/h) per live plateau, times total live weight O(h) gives O(d); static families cost C U(q) m (1 + h + log^- m)(d + 2 + log^- m); transfers controlled by P(transfer) <= C h^{-10} and ||X_*||_2 <= Ch.
why: Summation bookkeeping; the key 'O(d/h) per plateau x O(h) weight' split is the design choice of I33/I27.

name: Haar profiles h, g, finite shift S_{a,s,J}, kernel kappa(u) = int g(v) h(v-u) dv, K_J(t) = int_{2^{-J}}^1 kappa(t/r) dr/r^2, c = int_0^1 kappa = -1/8
statement: Translation and scale averaging of the delayed Haar shift is convolution with K_J; kappa is odd, Lipschitz, supported in [-1,1]; c = -1/8 agrees with Hytonen's Haar-shift kernel evaluation.
why: Transfer of Petermichl-Hytonen dyadic representation.

name: Hilbert transform to Fourier projections: H_delta -> H in L2, Pi_{>=0} = (I + iH + P0)/2, S_N rho = chi_{-N} Pi(rho chi_N) - chi_{N+1} Pi(rho chi_{-(N+1)}), su…
statement: Standard reduction of the Carleson maximal operator to maximally modulated Hilbert transforms, with symbol identity int sin(2 pi k t) cot(pi t) dt = 1.
why: Textbook.

This is the device that converts frequency selection into information-theoretic currency: a new random variable Z = Y + theta, never present in the goal or in L, whose Fisher information along output paths is globally bounded by O(d) via the entropy chain rule, while decoding int chi_n a^s = c_A(n) c^{s+n} recovers each modulation. It is the literal analogue of an extension variable: tiny to state, absent from the problem, and it makes the 'separate costs for information and for choosing freque…

Not a subterm of the goal; its conclusion is uniform over all weights on the retained subset (one centre, one omega-region), which is what lets the spectral update choose the weight afterwards. The cardinality loss d^2/(E h^2) is exactly calibrated to the endpoint. The two-visit-order search buys an O(h^{-2}) entropy cost for the block-length jump, which the endpoint needs. Lean isolates the search as an abstract reusable Arena (Compress/Search.lean:16-325).

id: I29 + I30: gap potential F(A) - log|B_A…
why: A monovariant that mixes free energy with packing entropy of a Bohr-type ball. Cheap deterministic updates lower it by k_b/2 and regular ones raise it by at most C t, so cheap updates are charged to regular ones, whose total is bounded by likelihood evidence. This closes the per-branch budget sum k_b + t <= Cd and the count n <= Ch. No near-equivalent was found.

id: I32: Prop modulated delayed Haar estima…
why: A dyadic model of the Carleson operator at the exact L log L endpoint: stopped at (log d)^4, L1 bound Cd, uniform in depth and frequencies, with delayed multipliers. It is the right intermediate target and carries all the difficulty; DAG-wise everything flows through it (Lean: GridBound).

id: I40: delayed vector norm estimate with …
why: The b-independent coefficient on the Fisher sum is what allows Fisher charges to be summed once globally while representative-choice costs carry the logarithmic factors in a separate tail.

name: Thermal noisy labels of the input point (Z = Y + theta, theta ~ K_A = e^{F(A)-A}, A a ferromagnetic cosine form, updated adaptively)
statement: Attach to the input point Y a label Z = Y + theta mod 1 whose error law has density K_A proportional to exp(-sum_s lambda_s(1 - cos 2 pi s y)). Spectra and transforms are read through the label: G^u = int |E[a chi_u(Y) K_A(z-Y)]|^2 / E[a K_A(z-Y)] dz measures how much the label reveals the phase chi_u(Y). Each successful spectral update adds a spatial form S_p and a metric form D_i to A, so the noise concentrates (in the error variable) on a smooth Bohr set of the discovered frequencies. Integr…
why: The closest analogue of an extension variable in this family: a new random variable, tiny to state, absent from goal and L, which is what lets frequency selection be paid for in information. Downgrade risks: (i) a judge may read it as a randomised form of Bohr-set localisation (Bourgain/Sanders), i.e. a cross-field transfer with a stochastic twist (N2); (ii) noise-channel smoothing is generic information theory. It pays off only together with C2 (information accounting), C3 (compression) and C5…

name: Two-law accounting and the global label Fisher sum (information charged under the true input law, paid back along uniform output paths)
statement: With dP = (rho/m_top) dU, the sum over live jumping pieces of U(p) alpha_e J_p, with J_p = int |D|^2/M, is at most Cd. Information about labels and memberships is counted under P, whose relative entropy to U is at most d because rho <= e^d, and converted into L1 bounds along uniformly sampled output paths.
why: The mechanism (entropy chain rule over a dyadic filtration, information counted under the density law) is standard. The budget d is the L log L hypothesis read as relative entropy, which is what calibrates the method to the endpoint and makes Test 2 fail. Its novelty is inherited from C1 and from the conversion to uniform-output bounds, which is bookkeeping (Sec. 9).

name: Entropy compression lemma (one centre and one phase region valid for every weight on a large retained subset)
statement: If for every law lambda on a finite S the 2T-fold symmetric noisy sum has E_lambda H_q(X_1+...+X_T - X'_1-...-X'_T) >= e^{-E}, then there are x_0 in S and S' in S with log|S|-log|S'| <= C d^2/(E h^2) such that for every probability v on S', int exp(-L sum_x v(x)(1 - cos 2 pi g(x-x_0) theta)) d omega >= e^{-CE}.
why: A member of the Chang/Lee/inverse-Littlewood-Offord family. The paper names Lee 2017 as the related method, which caps it at N2 under the PLAN rule. The distinctive features (conclusion uniform over all weights so that the spectral update can choose the weight afterwards; loss calibrated to the endpoint) are real, but they are a strengthening of a known statement type, not a new concept. Upgrade to N3 only if Test 4 (P-C3, arm B) shows that models given Chang + Lee do not produce the uniform-in…

name: Finite refinement search with two visit orders (block-length increase at O(h^{-2}) entropy cost)
statement: A finite sequence of context refinements reaching an index j with K_{m_{j,1}}(W; r_j) <= K_{m_{j,0}}(W; r_j) + E while losing at most C D_*^2/(E h^2) one-letter entropy. Updates are 'offers' from block observations; because the width p_j need not shrink under refinement, indices are visited in two orders with a stopping rule comparing the entry upper g-value with the current lower one.
why: A clever scheduling device inside a templated telescoping/increment argument. It buys the h^{-2} saving the endpoint needs, so it is load-bearing for L log L as opposed to L log L log log L. Once the obstruction is identified it is the natural fix, and the paper itself motivates it that way. Potential-driven increment search is a template, so N2. It would be F4 if upgraded.

name: Gap potential F(A) - log|B_A(r)| with a tracked radius
statement: With F(A) = -log int e^{-A} and B_A(r) = {u : Delta_A(u) <= r}, the gap F(A) - log|B_A(r)| starts at 0, stays >= -C (summability of q_A), rises by at most C t at a regular success and falls by at least k_b/2 at a cheap success, with r growing by eta at each main addition.
why: A neat monovariant, but read through the Bohr-set lens it is the uncertainty-principle slack of a smooth Bohr set, tracked as density-increment arguments track Bohr-set size and rank. Its novelty is derivative of C1. It would be F4 if upgraded.

name: Spectral update with the regular/cheap dichotomy (iterated compression, flat free-energy range, input-only success set)
statement: From a request (e^{k_b} separated high label-weighted frequencies), iterate compression with t shrinking by 4 per round to obtain either a regular test (success probability >= beta/2, E_T(nu) >= t/4) or a cheap deterministic update; choose the metric coefficient lambda on a flat interval of free energy among ~e^{h/4}/log h adjacent ranges.
why: Load-bearing and intricate, but assembled from standard templates (increment dichotomy, regular-radius pigeonhole, Chang/Lee transfer). Not graded N3 separately: its non-template content is C1 + C3 + C5.

name: Prop modulated delayed Haar estimate (finite dyadic model at the L log L endpoint)
