statement: For rho <= e^d of mean <= 2 on a dyadic tree, with stopping when the average exceeds e^{4h}, the maximally (trigonometrically) modulated delayed Haar multiplier sum_j E_{p_j}[rho chi_u r_{j+1}] eps_j r_{j+2} has L1 norm of its max over u bounded by Cd, uniformly in depth and number of frequencies.
why: As a statement it is the natural dyadic target, close to known maximally modulated Haar models and to Lie's good-set template, and analytic relative to goal + L. Its proof (Secs 3-9) is where the novelty lives, and that is credited to C1-C6. Downgraded from the analyst's provisional N3.

name: Endpoint reduction: Thm good-set with doubly exponential height layers
statement: int over {M rho <= e^{4h}} of sup_N |S_N rho| <= C d for mass-one rho <= e^d; layers e^{2^j} <= |f| < e^{2^{j+1}}, Borel-Cantelli on the exceptional sets (summable (log d_j)^{-4}).
why: The paper-named reduction template with endpoint parameters. Borderline N1/N2; graded N1 because it is a parameterisation of the known strategy.

name: Finite splitting procedure, live/static plateaus and live budgets (inductive caps on form, count, charge, radius)
statement: A stopping-tree decomposition of the input by spectral tests and membership splits, with per-branch invariants (A, n, Q, r, gap) carried by induction; budgets: sum k_b + sum t <= Cd, n <= Ch, membership surprisal O(h) in L2, plateau weight O(h), transfer O(h^{-10}).
why: The induction carries extra tracked quantities (form, count, charge, radius, gap potential): the 'carry an extra tracked quantity' template, so capped at N2 by the templated-strengthening rule.

name: Capture on a plateau: signed-span frequency lists, edge charges, snapshots refreshed by relative entropy
statement: Cumulative signed-span lists via Riesz-product entropy increments; likelihood-window edge charges; snapshots of representatives refreshed when mass measures change enough; one miss block before activation.
why: Strong but templated (Riesz-product entropy increment plus likelihood charging).

name: Path estimates: scalar Bellman-type potential psi and delayed vector norm estimate with absolute Fisher coefficient
statement: Maximal inequalities along output paths; the label-valued delayed estimate charges Fisher information with a b-independent coefficient by adding the coordinate lambda M to the state.
why: Bellman-function technique. Augmenting the state with lambda M is the templated 'track an extra quantity' move, so capped at N2. The Lean uses a different potential, which shows that the specific psi is not essential.

name: Half-wave propagator U, Bessel potential J^alpha, local smoothing norm
statement: Uf(x,t)=(2pi)^-3 int e^{i(x.xi+t|xi|)} fhat; J^alpha=(1-Delta)^{alpha/2}; estimate ||Uf||_{L^3(R^3x[1,2])} <= C_eps ||J^eps f||_3.
why: Standard (Sogge 1991; Peral/Miyachi).

name: Theorem 1.1 Critical local smoothing (L^3, every eps>0)
statement: For every eps>0, ||Uf||_{L^3(R^3x[1,2])} <= C_eps ||J^eps f||_{L^3(R^3)}.
why: The statement is the conjecture itself; its novelty is as a theorem, not as an item.

name: Fixed polynomial setup; negligible error; upper exponent Gamma (eq fw-upper-exponent)
statement: Structural constants, polynomial bounds and bounded number of operations fixed before s->0; Gamma = sup over setups and admissible sequences of limsup log B_s / log(1/s).
why: Critical/worst-case exponent formulation is standard in induction-on-scales (e.g. Guth's survey exponent beta for Wang-Zahl Kakeya, GWZ induction on scales); here formalised with explicit limit ordering. Close neighbours exist.

name: Uniform bound within a fixed setup
statement: Gamma real => B_s <= s^{-Gamma-eps} uniformly on families admissible in one setup.
why: Definitional.

name: Disjoint row restrictions and copies (energy accounting)
statement: Bessel-type inequality for V^*P_jV; copies only give N||g||^2.
why: Standard Hilbert space.

name: Extraction from finitely many classes (q-subadditive functional; l^3 sum of Hilbert norms)
statement: F(sum g_j)^{1/q}<=sum F(g_j)^{1/q} => some class has F(g_j)>=N^-q F(sum); applies to sum w^{-1/2}||A g||^3.
why: Standard dyadic pigeonholing.

name: Extrema of bounded exponent data (lexicographic minimisation in closure)
statement: Successive extrema on compact (or boundedly-minimised closed) slices are attained.
why: Compactness.

name: Strict improvement in a closure
statement: No data with z_n->z_0 and limsup c_n < c_0 = min on slice.
why: Closedness.

name: Pullback of a strict exponent contradiction
statement: Constructions with exponent Gamma+tau-r_m, r_m->0, in setups S_m are impossible.
why: Definitional.

name: Capacity tails / uniform integrability of normalised scores i_s
statement: P{P(X|Y)<e^-u/N}<=e^-u; normalised scores uniformly integrable.
why: Standard (AEP-type tail bound).

name: Stability under restriction (likelihood ratio bounds)
statement: Conditioning on E with P(E)>=s^alpha changes scores by <= alpha+tau outside 2s^tau.
why: Standard.

name: Negligible information and positive restrictions
statement: Pointwise information density tails; I_Q <= (I_P+log2)/q_0.
why: Standard.

name: Classical and hybrid cylinder states (base flow (X,B,Y)->(B+TX,Y+TX^2); hybrid normal fiber evolves by Schrodinger e^{-itHp^2/2sigma}; Gaussian analysis V_l)
statement: Classical cylinder: exact index (N,D) moving D_T=D+TN. Hybrid: normal fiber in L^2(R_D;H) with coherent-state analysis at widths d_l=(H/l)^{1/2}, q_l=(Hl)^{1/2}.
why: Cones locally look like parabolic cylinders (Bourgain-Demeter cone decoupling via cylinder; GWZ intermediate scales); Gaussian coherent-state wave packets are classical. The mixed classical-base/quantum-normal model is a new packaging.

name: Cylinder tests with polynomial normal shear and weight w=r^{3+eta} f^{1-eta}; kappa-regularity
statement: Heisenberg base box (|X-x|<=r,|B_T-b|<=lr,|Y_T-y-2x(B_T-b)|<=lr^2) and normal velocity/position windows after subtracting the shear alpha X+beta(T)X^2+K(Y_T-2XB_T); mu(Q)<=kappa w(Q).
why: Frostman / Katz-Tao convex-set nonconcentration and Wolff-type packet regularity are close neighbours; the specific sheared tests and eta-weight are new variants.

name: Assignments and normalised cubic functional B_s = s^{-1/2}/(e sqrt kappa) sum m^{3/2} w^{-1/2}
statement: Fractional assignments of final row mass to tests; cubic readout normalised by energy and regularity.
why: Reformulation of L^3 norm as l^{3/2} sum of packet masses (standard Wolff/GWZ style).

name: Polynomial cylinder setup
statement: Polynomial bounds on e/kappa, H, supports, densities.
why: Instance of P03.

name: Symmetries and Gaussian localization; repeated-cut regularity
statement: Invariance under translations, boosts, dilations, common shear; hybrid frame transfer negligible outside |N'-N|<=s^-eps d, |D'-D-tN|<=s^-eps q.
why: Standard Gaussian wave packet / Schur test.

name: Polynomial test reduction and sublevel estimate vol{|Q|<=rho||Q||}<=C rho^{2^-d}
statement: Only polynomially bounded tests matter; quadratic-polynomial sublevel bound.
why: Standard (Carbery-Christ-Wright type).

name: Theorem 2.4 Cylinder exponent bound Gamma_cl, Gamma_hyb <= eta/2
statement: Both cylinder exponents are at most eta/2.
why: New intermediate estimate; its novelty is carried by the items it uses.

name: One-time bound mu(Q)<=s^-o(1) kappa w(Q) l^{1+eta/2}; Gamma finite
statement: Single descendant test mass bound; gives B_s<=s^{-1+eta/4}.
why: Routine.

name: Extremal exponent data (p,d): m/(kappa w)=s^{p}, sum m = e s^{-d}, Gamma=d+(1-p)/2; minimal p in closure
statement: Dyadic binning gives homogeneous extremizers; choose smallest p; weight count sum w <= (e/kappa)s^{-(p+d)}.
why: Homogeneous pigeonholing of masses and 'worst-case' extremal choice are standard (Wang-Zahl, Guth); minimal-p selection inside the extremal slice is a variant.

name: Regularity peeling (coherent decomposition into subpower levels)
statement: Dyadic thresholds b; each level O(b)-regular, heavy tests of mass ~bw, total weight <= z/b.
why: Greedy dyadic peeling is standard (e.g. Wolff, Bourgain).

name: Saturation of a preserving split: b=kappa s^{pa}, z=e s^{-da}
statement: Any exponent-preserving split at depth a has regularity and energy exponents forced to the linear benchmarks.
why: Analogous to 'sticky/self-similar at all scales' consequences of extremality (Wang-Zahl stickiness; branching-function linearity in Orponen-Shmerkin). Variant.

name: Benchmarks l_i=s^i, E_i=e s^{-di}, kappa_i=kappa s^{pi}
why: Abbreviation.

name: Documented gate (row projection + synthesis with retained rows partitioned among tests)
why: Bookkeeping.

name: Matched-chain construction (common widths, read mass, width ratio and shear compatibility (M))
statement: On any finite mesh, masks can be inserted so documented tests have common widths, mass >= s^o(1)E_i, and successive shears satisfy (M).
why: New technical construction; analogous to compatible multiscale structure in sticky Kakeya. Variant.

name: Two-shear intersection (I) and partner count
statement: mu(Q- cap Q~-) <= s^-o(1) delta^-C kappa w /M where M = size of shear difference.
why: Sublevel/transversality counting; variant of standard incidence counting.

name: Group extraction
statement: Partition rows into groups with bounded reachability; extract near-extremal groups realising Gamma,p with relative weight count.
why: Pigeonholing variant.

name: Bottom Planck floor (Pl): H/(s f_1^2)=s^o(1) if Gamma_hyb>Gamma_cl
statement: Strictly nonclassical hybrid extremizers sit at the uncertainty scale at every depth.
why: Uncertainty-scale saturation is natural; classical comparison via phase lattice is a variant.

name: Shear costs R_2=(r^2/f)(|beta|+s|K|), R_1=(r/f)|alpha+2beta x-2Kb|; lexicographic minimal costs c=c_2, then c_1
statement: Exponents of growth of the curvature and linear shear of terminal tests, minimised in closure among extremizers.
why: New device (borderline N3): a second-level extremal choice of a geometric 'cost' among extremizers. Neighbours: minimal-delay / canonical profile in 074 (same release); Wang-Zahl multi-parameter extremal choices.

name: Finite costs and compact (Lipschitz) width profiles u(i), n(i), b_t(i)=n-tu; inequalities (A),(B)
statement: Arzela-Ascoli limits of width exponents; telescoped shear comparisons.
why: Branching-function / Lipschitz profile technique (Orponen-Shmerkin, Shmerkin) is a close neighbour.

name: Shape constraints: b_2(i)>=c(i-1), equality when c!=1; linear analogue
statement: Minimality of the cost forces the normal-minus-twice-angular width exponent to be the line c(i-1).
why: Same family as P30; minimal-cost-forces-linear-profile mirrors 'canonical temporal profile' of 074.

name: Affine extremal configurations (F): u=J(1-i), b_2=q(i-1) or b_1=c_1(i-1)
statement: Blow-up at a common differentiability point gives affine profiles while preserving extremality and minimal costs.
why: Rademacher + rescaling to tangent profile; standard in branching-function arguments (eps-linear intervals).

name: Rarity transport (Sp): P^j(U)<=s^-o(1) P^i(S)^{2/3}
statement: Power-rare predecessor events stay power-rare at later laws (via tail exponent + Holder).
why: Energy-to-probability transfer specific to this model; variant of 'measure of a rare set of tubes' arguments.

name: Measurable completion events and causal restrictions (Borel/analytic versions)
statement: Analytic projections of Borel path relations are universally measurable; inner/outer Borel versions.
why: Standard descriptive set theory (Lusin/Souslin).

name: Forward flattening of scores
statement: Restrict to subpower classes so prescribed log-probability scores have deterministic limits.
why: AEP-style flattening; standard in multiscale entropy (Hochman).

name: Transfer of conditional profiles
statement: Bidirectional subpower lists transfer conditional scores between laws.
why: Routine.

name: Time prediction (time choice score >= d(j-i))
why: Variant.

name: Recoverable phase names: score >= log(E_i/(kappa_i w)), equality under prediction
why: Variant.

name: Wave-envelope estimate (GWZ Thm 1.3) with Hilbert-valued and weighted extensions
statement: ||F||_4^4 <~ L^eps sum_R sum_tau sum_U |U|^-1 (int_U sum ||F_theta||^2)^2; Hilbert-valued via Gaussian randomisation.
why: Cited theorem; Hilbert extension by standard Gaussian randomisation.

name: Kinetic estimate for parabolic rays (kin)
statement: delta^-1 sum_{t,D} mu{Q_z(t) in D}^2 <~ delta^-eps kappa E under R^3-regularity of ray measure.
why: Direct corollary of GWZ via wave packets (known route: square function/wave envelope -> Kakeya-type collision estimates).

name: Scalar-channel estimate (SC)
statement: sum m^2/f^{1-eta} <= tau^-eta s^-o(1) b_0 e for 1-D normal channel, classical and Schrodinger.
why: 1-D collision counting / L^4 Strichartz-type bound; routine.

name: Memory bound for documented labels (mem) and prediction version
statement: P{X in label's list of delta^-R cells of width delta^L} <= delta^{(1-d+2Gamma+eta(L-1)-R)/2}.
why: New combination; variant.

name: Memory when both costs vanish
why: Special case of P43.

name: Exclusion of a strictly nonclassical zero-cost hybrid case
statement: Hybrid minimisers with Gamma_hyb>Gamma_cl cannot have c_2=c_1=0 (uses GWZ kinetic/crossing estimates).
why: Variant; GWZ used as black box.

name: Discretized planar Furstenberg estimate (RW), probabilistic form
statement: |union P_l|_Delta >= Delta^{-F(a,b)+omega}, F=a+min{1,b,(a+b)/2}, for Frostman probability measures.
why: Ren-Wang Thm 4.1; F(a,b) matches min(s+t,(3s+t)/2,s+1).

name: Likelihood and list comparisons (LP)
why: Standard.

name: Conditional planar incidence bootstrap (cond)->(inc)
statement: Conditional entropy-score version of Furstenberg: i(Q_1|D) >= a+min{1,a+g}.
why: Entropy/score version of a cited incidence theorem; known route (Hochman-style entropy versions of projection theorems).

name: Nested boosted names C(a) and lemma 'Geometric and probabilistic bounds for the boosted names'
statement: C(a)=(x_c,n_c,T_1^(a),position^(a)); profile D(a) Lipschitz with D(1)<=p+d; angular score >=(3-p)v; time score >=dzh.
why: Prototype of canonical names.

name: Exclusion of classical zero costs
statement: Classical extremizer with Gamma>eta/2 cannot have both costs zero; proves D'(a)>=1+3d contradicting D(1)<=p+d=1+3d-2Gamma (uses Ramsey).
why: One-variable version of the entropy-growth contradiction; shares architecture with 074.

name: Curvature displays (quadratic equality / pure linear / strict) and templates l(a,v), w(a,v)
statement: Which rounded shear coefficients R_a,k_a,bar k are recorded and at what precision.
why: Part of P52.

name: Canonical name C(a,v): finite record of time bin, rounded shear frame, derivative cell L, base cells [X]_v,[B]_{a+v},[Y-2[X]B]_{a+2v}, residual normal phase
statement: Finite phase-space record at time depth a and horizontal resolution v, retaining the changing shear frame.
why: Paper names Hochman-Shmerkin local entropy averages as precedent; same-release 074 uses coordinate entropy in two frames. Novel content: the recorded moving shear frame. Candidate F1 if upgraded.

name: Refinement and comparison of canonical names
statement: Finer names determine coarser to bounded lists; Lipschitz dependence.
why: Routine.

name: Canonical entropy excess E(a,v)=H(a,v)-D_0-(p+d)a-W(a,v) >= 0 with endpoint equality / label prediction
statement: Nonnegative entropy excess on the (a,v) domain, vanishing at boundary points v=u(a) / (1,0) / (D,u(D)).
why: No near-equivalent found in quick search: an entropy-excess function on a 2-parameter (depth, resolution) domain with zero boundary trace and nonnegativity, driven to contradiction by transport inequalities. Neighbours (Shmerkin/Orponen branching functions; Hochman entropy porosity; 074 canonical profile) are 1-parameter or same-release.

name: Angular trace m(a,v) and time stationarity (ang),(ng)
statement: Almost-everywhere linear angular score and stationarity.
why: Lebesgue differentiation of Lipschitz profiles.

name: Mixed coefficient trace nu
why: Routine differentiation.

name: Memory consequences (mr): m >= (k_0+2Gamma+eta(L_raw-1))/L_raw
statement: Angular rate lower bound from P43.
why: Variant.

name: Admissible side variables Z (coarse/exact, quadratic/linear) and common phase
statement: Conditioning variables for conditionally independent replicas; measurable common phase F(Z).
why: Conditionally independent copies are standard (entropic sumset, Tao); choice of side is new.

name: Conditional angular dimension (time mark surprise d) and Angular separation (line avoidance)
statement: Conditional marks xi=(theta,r) have time-surprise d and avoid affine lines by a power.
why: Variant.

name: Replica information budgets (vb),(fib) and stationary conditional walks (leg)
statement: Negligible information between replicas' marks and common phase; resampling legs with explicit increments.
why: Conditional resampling (Markov chain/walk on fibres) is a known entropy technique; specific legs new.

name: Score calculus: pathwise score limits, monotone diagonal trace, prefixes with future conditioning, changes of law
statement: Distributional limits of scores with chain rule and Lipschitz increments.
why: Routine.

name: Conditional projection rule
statement: Entropy form of a discretised projection theorem under negligible information budget.
why: Entropy version of Bourgain/Shmerkin-Wang projection theorems: known route.

name: Finite radial exclusion; Radial dichotomy; parent-centred directions; low-exponent pin estimate; pin-product alternatives
statement: Dichotomy e_* in {0} or >= d for radial line concentration; product slope f=(theta_j-theta_i)(r_j-r_i) score >= dp.
why: Radial projection bootstrap of Shmerkin-Wang (SW2025 Sec 5.4) and Orponen-Shmerkin-Wang is the named neighbour in the sibling paper 074.

name: Admissible interior tangent data; radial spreading; crossing
statement: Tangent experiment with common root C_*, side Z, phase F, replicas with marks; hypotheses 'radial spreading' and 'crossing'.
why: Variant.

name: Differential cost (time-rate) and width-rate
statement: d_a H >= d + min(1,c)(w+x) + |1-c|(pi or G); d_v H bounds.
why: Variant.

name: Angular/commutator modes; projection amplification x>=min(1,d+M)
why: Projection-theorem consequence.

name: Basic phase rates, many-leg vertical rate, mark-motion comparison, orientation rates, two time innovations, horizontal width, binary time estimate
statement: Rate inequalities (modes),(Gq),(H-walk),(trans),(cross-q),(mix-q),(double),(e-q),(bin).
why: Variants; many case-specific computations.

name: Admissible local actions (surplus): (d_a - k d_v)E >= 2Gamma
statement: For freezing k=0 or motion speeds k, the entropy excess decreases backwards at rate >= 2Gamma.
why: Together with P54 forms the potential/monovariant; individually an algebraic consequence of P65-P67.

name: Fixed-width line estimate
why: Variant.

name: Stationary equality boundary (radial spreading at q=c_2=1,J=0)
Strict affine boundary: d_a H(a,v_0) >= 2+3d
Finite off-gap motion and off-gap path contradiction
statement: Path in (t,v) domain on which E decreases at rate >=Gamma while staying in the domain of valid inequalities contradicts E>=0, E=0 on boundary.
why: Characteristic-path / comparison argument for first-order differential inequalities is classical; part of the P54 package.

name: Proof of Theorem 2.4 (case analysis over c, J, q, d)
statement: Covers equality curvature, pure linear, strict curvature cases.
why: Assembly.

name: Round experiment (classical rays (B+tA,Y+t|A|^2) and wave with Schrodinger-type evolution in null coordinates; plateau analysis)
why: Null-coordinate (paraboloid/Schrodinger) form of the cone wave is standard (Lorentz/light-cone coordinates).

name: Round regularity: round tests and null-hyperquadric tests F=c+du+alpha.x+beta z+k(uz-|x|^2), discriminant 1, weight r^4 f^{1-eta}
why: Frostman/Wolff-type regularity with conformally invariant hyperquadric tests; hyperquadric family is a new choice (light cones / null planes are its degenerations).

name: Packet locality, enlarged tests, single-time estimate, composition of free gaps, saturation at inserted cuts (CE)
statement: Round analogues of P17, P20, P23.
why: Analogues of cylinder lemmas.

name: Thin endings reduce to cylinders (conformal flattening of null hyperquadric; overlap; conformal wave transport; capacity allocation; weight comparison; classic…
statement: Saturated round experiments with thin terminal shape have Gamma <= cylinder exponents.
why: Change of representation via conformal chart (F5-type). Neighbours: Lorentz rescaling (Ou-Wang, GLMX), cone-to-cylinder at small angular scale (Bourgain-Demeter). Variant.

name: Theorem 8.1 Round-cone bound Gamma_cl,round, Gamma_wav,round <= 100 eta
why: Assembly.

name: Angular uncertainty at saturated wave cut (round-Pl); spatial readout; plane-slab estimates
statement: r_j/d_{l_j}=s^o(1), u(a)=(1-a)/2; plane-slab caps.

name: Round phase name C(a,v) (grid) and profiles D(a,v), J(a,v,w); wave excess E(a,v)=D-4v-(p+d)a >= 0, E(a,u(a))=0
statement: Round analogue of P52/P54.
why: Same as P54.

name: Outgoing entropy (round-out): o_T >= 4d + min(1-d, m/2) via four transverse pins, Gram-Schmidt, projective directions and finite Ramsey colouring
why: Pinning/projection bootstrap of Shmerkin-Wang/OSW type; Ramsey colouring of triples to fix projection directions is a new gadget (borderline N3, F3).

name: Two-direction descent lemma
statement: Locally Lipschitz E>=0 with zero trace on v=t/2 cannot satisfy E_t+E_v/2<=-c where m<=q and E_t<=-c where m>=q (m monotone in t).
why: Elementary comparison/characteristics argument.

name: Annular estimate ||W_H g||_{L^3} <= C_delta H^-delta ||g||_3; null coordinates; uniform packet localisation; volume of physical predecessors; input regularity …
statement: Physical L^3 estimate per frequency annulus from Theorem 8.1 via L^infty-amplitude pieces and synthesis int|v|^3 <~ H^{-1/2} sum m^{3/2}.
why: Standard amplitude/level-set decomposition and wave-packet synthesis.

name: Proof of Theorem 1.1 (Littlewood-Paley summation)
why: Standard.

name: Corollary 9.6 full range 2<p<infty, alpha>max{0,1-3/p}
statement: Interpolation of L^3 with L^2 and L^infty kernel bound.
why: Standard interpolation.

name: Maximal half-wave and a.e. convergence (p>=3, s>1-2/p)
why: Established implication.

name: Maximal Bochner-Riesz bounds and a.e. summation (3<=p<infty, delta>1-3/p); strict nonmaximal BR range; sphere extension r>3; Kakeya maximal L^3
why: Established implication chain LS => BR => restriction => Kakeya.

id: P54 + P68 + P72 (round: P86 + P88): ent…
why: Turns the whole positive-cost case into a first-order differential-inequality problem for one scalar function: E>=0, E=0 on a boundary curve, and (d_a - k d_v)E >= 2Gamma along admissible directions; a characteristic path then forces E<0. Non-analytic: neither the canonical name nor its excess occurs in the goal or in L; the goal is an L^3 inequality. Load-bearing: every positive-cost configuration in Thm 2.4 and the whole round wave case of Thm 8.1 close through it (06:1083-1276; 08:1433-1471)…
Minimising the shear cost among extremizers is a non-obvious second-order extremal choice that pins the geometry (b_2(i)=c(i-1)). Load-bearing for everything after Sec 2.
Changes representation of thin round packets into a parabolic-cylinder model where GWZ (2+1) applies; keeps a 1-D Schrodinger evolution when the normal coordinate stays quantum.
Single inequality that closes the round case; Ramsey colouring to coherently choose projection planes is an unusual gadget.
Avoids any positive phase-space density for masked quantum evolutions; makes 'power-rare predecessor' a transferable notion.

name: Entropy-excess potential with zero boundary trace and transport inequalities
statement: E(a,v)=H(a,v)-D_0-(p+d)a-W(a,v) >= 0 on a 2-parameter (time-depth, resolution) domain, with E=0 at label-recoverable boundary points; admissible local actions give (d_a - k d_v)E >= 2Gamma; following a characteristic path backward from the boundary forces E<0. Round analogue: E=D-4v-(p+d)a, E_t+E_v/2<=-2Gamma or E_t<=-2Gamma, contradicted by the descent lemma.
why: Passes tests 1-3 as far as checked: no human 2-parameter analogue found, non-analytic, load-bearing. Downgrade pressure: (i) the 1-parameter core is standard branching-function/entropy-growth technique; (ii) the same mechanism appears in three sibling model papers of the same release, so this is a cluster-level device (one day after 074); (iii) the transport/descent step itself is elementary. Correctness of the whole package is unverified. Would fall to N2 if an expert identifies the 2-paramete…

name: Lexicographic extremal reduction: minimal mass exponent p, then minimal shear costs c, c1, forcing linear benchmarks and affine width profiles
statement: Among extremizers of the cylinder functional choose minimal p; any exponent-preserving split has kappa_a=kappa s^{pa}, E_a=e s^{-da}; then minimise curvature cost c (and c1); minimality forces b_2(i)=c(i-1); blow up at a differentiability point to affine profiles.
why: Worst-case-exponent paradigm (Wang-Zahl) plus eps-linear profile technique (Orponen-Shmerkin) are close neighbours; the shear-cost lexicographic layer is a variant, not a new concept.

name: Canonical name C(a,v): finite phase-space record with recorded moving shear frame
statement: Records time bin t_a, rounded shear coefficients (R_a,k_a,bar k), derivative cell L, base cells [X]_v,[B]_{a+v},[Y-2[X]B]_{a+2v}, residual normal velocity/position after subtracting the recorded shear.
why: PLAN rule: a precedent the paper names itself caps at N2 (Hochman-Shmerkin). Would be F1 if upgraded.

name: Hybrid classical/quantum cylinder model and thin-shape reduction by conformal flattening of null hyperquadrics
statement: Thin round packets near a null hyperquadric are mapped by a rational conformal chart (Bateman/Kelvin covariance of Box) to a parabolic-cylinder model; if the normal coordinate is below the uncertainty scale it keeps a 1-D Schrodinger evolution (hybrid model), else classical.

statement: Compatible paths (all selected clauses simultaneously violable with rho) prescribe a pattern sigma_P on U_j; c_{U_h} is constant on the cylinder; omega(P) = prod 1/c_h; W = sum_j W_j.
why: Part of I07 cluster (bookkeeping).

name: Reweighting by a full assignment y (E W_j = E_{T,y}[sum over paths violated at y of 2^{|U_j|} prod 1/c_{U_h}(y)])
statement: Sample y uniform, set rho = y outside T; conditional on (T,rho) multiply by 2^{|U_j|} to undo the cylinder probability.
why: Standard reweighting.

name: Backward (reverse) path counting: injective reverse encoding from terminal set R_j, recursion F_s(R) = (1/|V_R|) sum_{i in V_R} sum_{D subset E_i,|D|>b} alpha^…
statement: With alpha = 2p/(1-p), pi(T) 2^{|U_j|} prod 1/c = pi(R_j) prod alpha^{|D_h|}/|V_{R_h}|; one-step weight <= theta; hence E W_j <= theta^j and E W <= 1/(1-theta).
why: Part of I07 cluster; the averaging-instead-of-multiplying device is what removes the clause count and permits arbitrary constant pk.

name: theta = sum_{l=b+1}^k C(k,l)(2p/(1-p))^l
statement: Poisson-like tail; <= sum_{l>b} Q^l/l! with Q = 2pk/(1-p).
why: Tail sum.

name: Lemma sparse-partition: every width-b CNF on m vars is a DISJOINT sum of <= 2^{eta m} width-b CNFs with <= M(b,eta) m clauses each
statement: For every b>=1, eta>0 there is M(b,eta) such that H = sum_{a<=q} H_a pointwise, q <= 2^{eta m}, H_a width <= b with <= Mm clauses, satisfying sets pairwise disjoint.
why: Re-proof of the disjoint sparsification lemma (known, cited); restated with clause count Mm instead of variable-occurrence bounds.

name: sunflower, core, petals
statement: Distinct sets with common pairwise intersection C (core); petals = sets minus C.
why: Erdos-Rado.

name: Lemma sunflower-bound (Erdos-Rado): > s!(r-1)^s distinct s-sets contain an r-sunflower
statement: Classical, with proof by induction on s.
why: Erdos-Rado 1960.

name: eligible sunflower at size i (r_i members, nonempty core); branching state = active antichain + separate unit-clause side condition; branch 0 inserts core C, b…
statement: F = F_0 + 1[C false] F_1 with disjoint supports.
why: IPZ branching with DHMTW side condition; keeping the side condition separate from the active family is a bookkeeping refinement.

name: occurrence bounds e_i, added-clause invariant (<= e_u + 1 per literal), insertion charging N_u <= (e_u+1)(2m + sum_{v<u} N_v), budgets D_i
statement: Bounds the number of steps per path linearly in m.
why: IPZ accounting.

name: leaf counting via per-size decision streams with few ones + binary entropy bound; threshold choice r_i = 2^{q_i}
statement: #leaves <= prod 2^{m F_i h_2(1/r_i)} <= 2^{eta m}.
why: Standard entropy counting as in IPZ01.

name: Definition language: data x (d bits), Hankel/Toeplitz hash seed u, monic modulus P of degree r = ceil(d^{2/3}), t ~ d^{1/6} coefficients beta_j in F_2[Z]/(P); …
statement: d = floor(n/5); r = ceil(d^{2/3}); t = largest even j with j^6 <= d; parameter bits are part of the input; evaluator never tests irreducibility.
why: Close variant of PSZ00 input-index construction + ABI86/IPZ01 polynomial families; parameters r, t tuned to the sqrt(d) live sets.

name: Hankel (Toeplitz) linear hash h_i(x) = sum_s u_{i+s-1} x_s
statement: Universal linear hash; only uniformity of h(w) for nonzero w is used.
why: Toeplitz hashing.

name: Prop polytime: L decided by one deterministic TM in time C(n+1)^a
statement: Integer parameter search, O(rd + t r^2) bit operations; no irreducibility test.
why: Routine algorithmics.

name: Prop good-slices: for fixed b, B and large n there is a setting of non-data bits whose slice g satisfies Pr_{T,rho}[|T| not in [m0/2, 2m0] or corr_b(g_{T,rho})…
statement: Probabilistic method over (u, beta): hash injective on the restricted cube w.p. >= 1 - 2^{m-r}; then signs t-wise independent; t-th moment + union over (C_m+1)^{Mm} sparse tests + sparse partition gives corr_b <= 2^{-m/8}; average over parameter choices.
why: Close variant of IPZ01's random-polynomial depth-3 (bounded bottom fan-in) argument, transplanted to restricted cubes.

name: h(w) uniform for every nonzero w (successive pivots), hence injectivity on a restricted m-cube except w.p. <= 2^{m-r}
statement: Union bound over 2^m - 1 differences.
why: Universal hashing.

name: limited independence from Lagrange interpolation: uniform beta in F^t gives t-wise independent unbiased signs on distinct hash values
statement: Evaluation map surjective for q <= t distinct nodes; lambda balanced.
why: Standard k-wise independence construction.

name: count of sparse tests <= 2^{Mm[1 + b log2(2m+1)]}
statement: Encoding of normalized clauses and lists of <= Mm clauses.
why: Counting.

name: t-th moment bound E Y^t <= t^t 2^{mt/2}, Markov, union bound
statement: Terms with a singleton point vanish; at most 2^{mt/2}(t/2)^t surviving descriptions.
why: Standard moment method for k-wise independent sums.

name: binomial tails of |T| and averaging to fix one parameter setting
statement: Pr[m<m0/2], Pr[m>2m0] <= 2^{-m0/16} each; averaging argument.
why: Chernoff-type.

name: Order of quantifiers and parameters: fix A, s = 3A, B = 64(s+1), p = B/sqrt d, k = ceil(3(s+1) sqrt d), Q = 4B[3(s+1)+1], then choose b = b(A) with sum_{l>b} Q…
statement: pk is a (large) constant depending on A; b is chosen after A so the restriction lemma applies; the slice is chosen after (b, B). "This is the only place where the desired circuit exponent affects the target width."
why: Strategic insight but arithmetically forced given I07 + I26; in Lean exists_final_parameter_width / exists_factorial_tail_width.

name: Correlation transfer to width k: |E g H| <= 2^{-m0/16} E[W_H 1_good] + Pr[not good] <= 6 2^{-m0/16} for every width-k CNF H, no independence needed
statement: Combine I07 (per H) with I26 (good event, uniform over all width-b tests).
why: Direct combination.

name: near-balance: constant-true CNF gives |E g| <= 6 2^{-m0/16}, so Pr[g=1] >= 1/4
why: Trivial instance of I33.

name: Circuit counting: <= S middle CNFs with <= S clauses; delete clauses wider than k (error S 2^{-k} each); gH = H for middle gates of an exact OR; sum over middl…
why: Standard.

name: Lemma field-existence: monic irreducible polynomial of every degree r over F_2
statement: Elementary construction of GF(2^r) and counting of lower-degree elements.
why: Textbook; Lean uses Mathlib GaloisField + primitive element instead (route difference).

name: slice: function of the data bits obtained by fixing the parameter bits
why: Subfunction under a restriction of non-data inputs.

name: Comparator definitions: Circuit3, gateCount = bottomCount + middleCount + 1, FiniteMultiTapeMachine, MultiTapeHaltsIn, runSteps
statement: Self-contained model of depth-3 circuits and multi-tape TMs on top of Mathlib Turing.Tape.
why: Formal renderings of standard models.

name: Multi-tape TM implementation of the evaluator (Tape*.lean, Machine*.lean, LanguageBit*.lean): ~1224 decls, ~7900 lines; machine constants C = 24000*3^8, a = 8
statement: Explicit compilation of hash, polynomial multiply/reduce, Horner loop, parser into a finite multi-tape machine with time bound.
why: Routine implementation (negative control for the load-bearing proxy).

name: Restriction lemma: clause-count-free expansion of a p-restricted width-k CNF into width-b CNF tests with E W <= 1/(1-theta), valid for ANY constant pk (b = b(p…
statement: For H width <= k on [d], b >= 1, theta = sum_{l=b+1}^k C(k,l)(2p/(1-p))^l < 1: exists W(H,T,rho) >= 0 with E W <= 1/(1-theta) and |E_z G H_{T,rho}| <= W corr_b(G) for all G simultaneously. Proof: H_{T,rho} = K + K sum_j (-1)^j sum_{paths} prod v_{i_h}/prod a_{U_h}; each term = omega(P) E[J_P] (marker mixture); count paths backwards from the terminal live set with weight 1/|V_R| averaging over eligible violated clauses.
why: No neighbour found in four searches over the switching-lemma family (Hastad, Razborov, Rossman, SBI, Lovett-Wu-Zhang, GMR, IMP12); the conclusion (clause-count-free L1 expansion into narrow CNFs at arbitrary constant pk) differs from all of them; non-analytic; the knockout shows it is the step that breaks the sqrt n ceiling. Not templated (the IH F_s(R) <= theta^s is incidental). Confidence held at 0.5 because the switching-lemma neighbourhood is dense and expert-heavy, zbMATH/MathOverflow were…

name: Marker mixture: c/(c+w) realised as a convex mixture of conjunctions of the indexed clauses (random order of clauses and c markers)
statement: Uniformly permute a clause objects and c markers; the conjunction of clauses before the first marker holds w.p. c/(c+w) at a point violating w of them. Applied independently per path step, K prod v/prod a = omega(P) E[J_P] with J_P in C_b(T).
why: Classical identity in a new role; graded as part of the C1 cluster. Standalone it is N1-N2.

name: Strategy/quantifier insight: choose b after A so pk may be any constant, with a slice whose restricted correlation exponent (1/8) does not depend on b
statement: Fix A; s = 3A, B = 64(s+1), k = ceil(3(s+1) sqrt d), Q = 4B[3(s+1)+1]; choose b with sum_{l>b} Q^l/l! <= 1/2; then choose the slice for (b, B).
why: Conceptual crux but arithmetically forced by C1 + C4; its novelty is inherited from C1.

name: Prop good-slices: a k-wise independent slice whose random restrictions have corr_b <= 2^{-|T|/8} simultaneously over all width-b CNFs
statement: For fixed b, B and large n, some parameter bits give Pr_{T,rho}[|T| out of [m0/2, 2m0] or corr_b(g_{T,rho}) > 2^{-|T|/8}] <= 4 2^{-m0/16}.

statement: d = floor(n/5), r = ceil(d^{2/3}), t ~ d^{1/6}; accept iff lambda(sum beta_j h(x)^j) = 0.
why: Downgraded from the analyst's N2: a conjunction of L concepts with the paper's own named precedent (PSZ00); parameter tuning only.

statement: Width-b CNF on m vars = disjoint sum of <= 2^{eta m} width-b CNFs with <= M(b,eta) m clauses each.
why: Re-proof of the disjoint sparsification lemma; downgraded from the analyst's N1 because DHMTW14 already states the needed form up to the trivial occurrence-to-clause-count conversion.

why: It is the step that breaks the sqrt n barrier: it allows any constant pk (b chosen after A), while every switching-lemma statement in L needs pk below an absolute constant. Conclusion type (signed CNF mixture with L1 cost, clause-count free, tests stay CNFs) is not a subterm of the goal or of L; the paper itself contrasts it with Hastad. name: Strategy insight I32 + I26: choose b AFTER A so pk may be any constant, and make the slice pseudorandom so its correlation exponent (1/8) does not depend on b
why: Explains why parity/majority cannot work (their corr_b decays like 2^{-m/b}) and why a pseudorandom slice can. The quantifier order is the conceptual crux of omega(sqrt n).

name: I26 Prop good-slices (k-wise independent slices with small corr_b on almost every restriction)
why: Needed with exponent independent of b and simultaneously over all width-b tests; uses sparse partition on the restricted cube.

name: I12 marker mixture (c/(c+w) realised as a convex mixture of conjunctions)
why: Keeps every test a width-b CNF, which is what makes corr_b the right currency.

name: I17 disjoint sparse partition with linear clause count
why: Large Lean share (Sparse* defs ~22% frac_dag_dependents).

name: Indexed IFS Phi=(phi_i), phi_i(x)=r_i x+t_i, 0<|r_i|<1; self-similar measure mu_{Phi,p}
statement: mu = sum_i p_i (phi_i)_* mu; equivalently the law of lim phi_{I_1}...phi_{I_n}(0) with I_j iid ~ p. Repeated (indexed) maps allowed.
why: Hutchinson 1981.

name: Exact overlap (equality of complete affine maps for distinct same-length words)
statement: phi_u=phi_v for distinct words of equal positive length; equality includes signed slope and translation.
why: Standard (Simon 1996, Hochman 2014).

name: Random affine map G_n and random-walk entropy rate h_RW = lim H(G_n)/n = inf H(G_n)/n
statement: P(G_n=g)=sum_{w: phi_w=g} p_w; h=lim H(G_n)/n=inf_n H(G_n)/n by subadditivity; 0<=h<=H(p).
why: Garsia entropy / Varju survey Conjecture 3 uses exactly this quantity.

name: Lyapunov exponent chi=-sum p_i log|r_i|
statement: Base-2 average log contraction.
why: Standard.

name: Lower Hausdorff dimension of a measure
statement: dim_H nu = inf{dim_H E : E Borel, nu(E)>0}.
why: Standard.

name: Exact dimensionality of mu (Feng-Hu Theorem 2.8) and equality of the two measure-dimension conventions
statement: lim log mu(B(x,s))/log s = d for mu-a.e. x; d = dim_H mu.
cited_or_new: cited, not re-proved in paper; RE-PROVED in Lean
why: Feng-Hu 2009. Lean re-derives it via Hopf maximal inequality, Birkhoff/Maker averages and a maximal ball-ratio bound.

name: Theorem 1.1 (main): dim_H mu = min{1, h_RW/chi}
statement: See main_statement.
cited_or_new: new (claimed resolution of Varju survey Conjecture 3)

name: Entropy-rate upper bound d <= min{1,h/chi}
statement: Regroup into n-blocks with alphabet = distinct maps of G_n (same mu), SLLN for prefix probability and contraction, covering argument.
why: Folklore (Feng-Hu, Hochman); merging coincident maps into a new alphabet is standard.

name: Fixed-grid entropy H_s^0, averaged entropy calH_s, window entropy G_{s,t}=calH_s-calH_t, one-bit deficit Delta_s=1-G_{s,2s}
statement: calH_s(X)=int_0^1 H(floor(X/s+u))du; Delta_s measures non-saturation between scales s and 2s.
why: Varju 2019 averaged entropy; Wang 2011 translation averaging.

name: Lemma 2.1 Entropy calculus (smoothing identity, affine invariance, integer-ratio concavity and convolution monotonicity, scale and grid comparisons)
statement: calH_s(X)=h(X+V_s)-log s; calH_s(aX+b)=calH_{s/|a|}(X); for t/s integer, G_{s,t} concave, in [0,log N], and G_{s,t}(X+Y)>=G_{s,t}(X).
why: Re-proof of cited lemmas (signed scaling added).

name: Lemma 2.2 Entropy and dimension: limsup max{calH_s,H_s^0}/log(1/s) <= d
statement: For exact-dimensional compactly supported nu.
why: Standard.

name: Lemma 2.3 Uniform nonsaturation: d<1 implies delta=inf_{v>0} Delta_v(mu)>0, for unequal signed ratios
statement: If Delta_{v_n}->0 then TV bound gives G_{v_n,Kv_n}->log K; stopped self-similarity transfers near-saturation to all smaller scales (loss C_*=log(1/a_*+2)+1), contradicting P11.
why: Named precedent (BV Lemma 13); the extension via a stopping time to unequal signed ratios is routine.

name: Lemma 2.4 Two-point gain: G_{s,t}(X+vJ)-G_{s,t}(X) >= Delta_v(X)-s/v-v/t
statement: Fair pair at distance v raises window entropy by Delta_v minus boundary losses; no integer-ratio needed.
why: Restatement of Varju's fair-pair comparison in the averaged-entropy calculus.

name: Pair capacity c_ell(nu): max total weight of fair two-point laws with separation in [2^-ell,2^{1-ell}) forming a submeasure of nu (an LP / fractional matching)
statement: c_ell(nu)=max sum_e w_e s.t. w_e>=0, (1/2) sum_{e ni x} w_e <= nu({x}).
why: Named predecessor (Varju Prop. 21); the LP/fractional-matching packaging is a natural formalization of 'mass in fair pairs at scale 2^-ell'. Candidate for N3 only jointly with P15.

name: Lemma 3.2 Finite-law pair bound: k(H(nu)-H^0_rho(nu)) <= log|kF| + C_k sum_{2^-ell<=2rho} c_ell(nu), C_k=60000k^4, independent of minimal separation
statement: Exact-minus-grid entropy of a finite law is bounded by the k-fold sumset growth plus pair capacity at all finer bands; separation-free.
why: Quick check found no precedent for a separation-free deficit-to-pair-capacity bound with a sumset term; the paper names Varju Prop. 21 only as a predecessor. Key non-obvious device: conditioning on the k-fold sum Y makes the refinement cost linear (not t log 1/t) in exceptional probabilities, so costs sum geometrically over all finer scales.

name: Randomized nested partitions rho_h=rho 4^-h with independently perturbed internal cuts (density <= 20/rho_h)
statement: Each parent of length in [rho_h/2,2rho_h] split into N in [2,8] pieces, cuts perturbed by +-rho_{h+1}/10; cuts independent of samples; separating depth J exists but is never bounded.
why: Randomized grids are standard; here an auxiliary gadget for P15.

name: One refinement after observing the sum: H(C_{h+1}|Y,C_h=(A_i)) <= 9k sum_i p_i (linear in exceptional probabilities)
statement: On the event that at most one coordinate deviates and the sum is near its mean, all child labels equal the mean's labels; the event B is Y-measurable so carries no binary-entropy cost; h_2(q)<=3sqrt q with q<=t^2.
why: Graded together with P15.

name: Symmetric coupling pi_h=sum_A nu(A) nu(.|A)^{x2} gives feasible pair mixtures; sum over h of 2^-ell/rho_h <= 8/3
statement: Converts mean deviations into band capacities; geometric summation removes J.
why: Routine coupling/geometric series.

name: Block types: words W_h in Lambda^b, type(w)=symbol counts, q_kappa, Q_kappa uniform on type class; type environment omega, signed products R_j, depths sigma_j
statement: Coding = iid types then independent uniform words within types; types fix the signed slope r(kappa).
why: Known disintegration (GSSY; SSS; Kaenmaki-Orponen).

name: Conditional laws nu_{omega,n} (law of sum_{h<n} R_h phi_{W_h}(0) given types) and mu_omega; E mu_omega = mu
statement: Finite random translation laws given the type environment.
why: Conditional laws of the standard disintegration.

name: Parameters alpha, b, A=b alpha, A'=b(chi+alpha)/2, h_b=bh-m log(b+1), gamma=h_b-dA>0, rho_n=2^{-ceil(An)}, E_n={sigma_n<=A'n}, a_n=ceil(An)-1
statement: Fixed constants.
why: Parameter choices.

name: Lemma 4.1 Entropy retained by types: E H(nu_{omega,n}) = H(G_{bn}|Omega_n) >= n h_b; E H^0_s(nu_{omega,n}) <= H^0_s(mu)+1; E[1_{E_n}(H - H^0_{rho_n})(nu_{omega…
statement: Under the dimension-loss hypothesis, conditional translation laws carry linear entropy invisible at scale 2^{-An}.
why: Close neighbours: Hochman's entropy of the full affine map (Thm 1.4), RV Appendix A, Barany-Verma Thm 3.5. The observation that types fix slope so translation entropy = conditional map entropy is a short step.

name: Digit-count sumset bound: |k D_b| <= (k+1)^{m^b}, hence log|kS| <= n m^b log(k+1)
statement: A k-fold sum of block translations is determined by digit counts; fixed types make this uniform in omega and sign-independent.
why: Trivial counting, but essential pairing with P15.

name: Proposition 4.2 Pair mass in finite scale bands: E[1_{E_n} sum_{ell=a_n}^{B_n} c_ell(nu_{omega,n})] >= c n with deterministic finite B_n (no growth bound)
statement: P15 + P22 + P23 with k chosen after b, eps; B_n = max band index among finitely many laws.
why: Assembly of P15/P22/P23; the novelty lives in P15.

name: Suffix laws tau_j = D_{R_j} mu_{theta^j omega} with tau_j = (D_{R_j} nu_{theta^j omega,n}) * tau_{j+n}
statement: Pathwise convolution identity.
why: Standard.

name: Window entropy g_j = G_{r/M, Mr}(tau_j) at target depth L (r=2^-L), with 0<=g_j<=2 log M and g_j nonincreasing in j
statement: A monotone sequence in the block index at each physical scale; its decrements are the per-window gains.
why: Window entropy of partial convolution products is a standard object in this literature.

name: Lemma 5.1 Conditional pair gain: E[g_j - g_{j+n} | F_{j+n}] >= (delta/2) c_{L-ceil(sigma_j)}(nu_{theta^j omega,n})
statement: Pairs from the window, rescaled to distance in [r,4r), each gain Delta_v(tau_{j+n})-5/M; averaging the unobserved future types restores D_{R_{j+n}}mu by Jensen (Delta convex), where nonsaturation gives delta.
why: Natural once P12 and P13 are in place; the Jensen-over-future step is a standard randomization move.

name: Separated band selection: choose n_1<...<n_q successively with a_{n_i}-A'n_i-1 > B_{n_h} (h<i), candidate starts J_i (multiples of n_i), retention events A_{i,…
statement: Adaptive choice of block lengths after earlier (uncontrolled) band endpoints are known; every band contributes delta c T/(4D) while each physical scale's total drop is <= 2 log M; so q <= 8D log M/(delta c), contradiction.
why: No precedent found for a scale-free counting that pits q adaptively separated relative-depth bands against a telescoping bound at each physical scale. Pieces (telescoping, diagonal selection) are standard.

name: Lemma 5.2 Disjoint retained windows: at each target L, retained windows from all bands are pairwise disjoint, so total gain <= 2 log M
statement: x_j=L-ceil(sigma_j) is nonincreasing; a finer-band window ends before any coarser-band window starts.
why: Graded with P28.

name: Completion of proof: no dimension loss (d<1, d chi<h) is possible
statement: Upper bound plus contradiction gives Theorem 1.1.

name: Lemma 6.1 Overlap lengths: an exact overlap of arbitrary lengths yields one of equal lengths
statement: phi_{uv}=phi_{vu}.
why: Known.

name: Corollary 6.2 No exact overlaps: dim mu = min{1,H(p)/chi} (the exact overlaps conjecture for measures on R)
statement: H(G_n)=nH(p) without exact overlaps.

name: Attractor K_Phi (set of coding limits) and similarity dimension s_* (sum |r_i|^s=1)
why: Standard.

name: Corollary 6.3 Attractor: no exact overlaps implies dim_H K = min{1,s_*}
statement: Weights p_i=|r_i|^{s_*} and the cylinder covering bound.

name: Corollaries 6.4-6.5 Homogeneous systems and the three-map family {lambda x, lambda x+1, lambda x+t}
statement: Specializations of P32.

statement: In-house finite information theory (Mathlib at d13f23b has limited Shannon-entropy API).
why: Infrastructure.

name: Typed tag abstraction (tag : alpha -> beta, equal tags => equal ratios)
statement: Generalizes block types to any slope-fixing tag.
why: Formalization generalization.

Separation-free: converts entropy hidden below scale rho into fair-pair mass at arbitrarily fine bands with a constant independent of the smallest gap - exactly what Baker/Barany-Kaenmaki examples showed was needed and what Hochman's fixed-scale inverse theorem cannot give. Non-analytic: neither pair capacity nor the sumset-plus-capacity inequality is a subterm of the goal, of Mathlib, or of the bibliography. Non-obvious device: conditioning on the k-fold sum Y makes the per-level refinement en…

Removes the last need for effective separation: band endpoints B_n can be arbitrarily large because each n_i is chosen after the previous B_{n_h} are known, and a band's contribution delta c T/(4D) is independent of n_i. Monovariant: at each physical scale g_j is nonincreasing and retained windows from different bands are disjoint, so all gains share a 2 log M budget; q bands force q <= 8 D log M/(delta c). Not a subterm of the goal or L.

why: This is where h_RW enters and exact overlaps are absorbed with no arithmetic assumption.

name: Finite-law pair bound with the sum-observation refinement (log-free, separation-free)
statement: For every k>=1 there is C_k (=60000k^4) such that every finitely supported nu on R and every rho>0 satisfy k(H(nu)-H^0_rho(nu)) <= log|kF| + C_k sum_{l: 2^-l <= 2rho} c_l(nu), F = supp nu, with C_k independent of the minimal gap of F. That delta is exactly what the unbounded band endpoints B_n require, and it is the separation-free bridge that Baker / Barany-Kaenmaki make necessary. Against N3: it is a strengthening of a named predecessor in L by a single device; the sum observat…

name: Pair capacity c_l(nu)
statement: c_l(nu) = max sum_{e in E_l(F)} w_e subject to w_e >= 0 and (1/2) sum_{e contains x} w_e <= nu({x}), with E_l(F) the pairs at distance in [2^-l, 2^{1-l}); i.e. the largest total weight of fair two-point laws in band l forming a submeasure of nu.
why: A renaming, as an LP, of the maximal Bernoulli-decomposition mass in Varju's Prop 21 (in L), restricted to one dyadic band. Varju's proof literally minimises the residual, so 148's paper names this predecessor correctly. Not F1: it introduces no new variable beyond Varju's object. Reconciliation with f1_pair_capacity.json/.md (F1 agent, same day): it independently finds the same Varju Sec 4.2.3 identity, the fractional b-matching and sub-coupling forms, and that Kittle-Kogler 2026 replaced c_l …

name: Scale-free separated-band counting with adaptive block lengths and disjoint retained windows
statement: Choose n_1 < ... < n_q successively with a_{n_i} - A'n_i - 1 > B_{n_h} (h<i), using no growth bound on B_n. At each target depth L the retained windows from all bands are disjoint in block index, so their gains telescope to <= 2 log M (g_j is nonincreasing). Summing over L = 1..T, each band contributes delta c T/(4D), independent of n_i, so q <= 8 D log M/(delta c), a contradiction.
why: Telescoping of a monotone multiscale entropy and diagonal parameter choice are standard (Varju's Lemma 27 is the in-L template). The adaptive arrangement is a genuine but modest variant. Would be F4 if raised.

name: Map entropy retained by block types (types fix slopes, so translation entropy = conditional map entropy)
statement: E H(nu_{omega,n}) = H(G_{bn} | Omega_n) >= n(bh - m log(b+1)); E H^0_s(nu_{omega,n}) <= H^0_s(mu) + 1; under dimension loss E[1_{E_n}(H - H^0_{rho_n})(nu_{omega,n})] >= eps n.
why: This is where exact overlaps are absorbed with no arithmetic input. It is a short adaptation of named precedents: GSSY types plus Hochman's full-map entropy.

name: Uniform nonsaturation for signed unequal ratios
statement: If d<1 then delta = inf_{v>0} Delta_v(mu) > 0, for any signed, unequal ratios (stopped self-similarity).
why: A named precedent with a routine extension.

name: Conditional pair gain by Jensen over the unobserved future types
statement: E[g_j - g_{j+n} | F_{j+n}] >= (delta/2) c_{L - ceil(sigma_j)}(nu_{theta^j omega, n}).
why: Prop 20 composed with a standard Jensen-over-environment step (borderline N2).

name: Linear pair mass in a finite band with uncontrolled endpoint
statement: E[1_{E_n} sum_{l=a_n}^{B_n} c_l(nu_{omega,n})] >= c n with B_n finite but with no growth bound.
why: Assembly. Its novelty lives in C1. P23 is a trivial count whose role (sumset sub-linear in k) is the tensor-power-style amplification that C1 needs.

name: leave / terminal edge count F_n
statement: Run uniform triangle removal from K_n until triangle-free; the leave is the set of uncovered edges, F_n its size.
why: Design-theory term (leave of a partial triple system); process from BFL2015.

name: Main theorem: L2 convergence of F_n/n^{3/2} to 1/(2 sqrt 2)
statement: E[(F_n/n^{3/2} - 1/(2sqrt2))^2] -> 0; hence convergence in probability and of E F_n / n^{3/2}.
why: The statement (constant) was conjectured: joosKuehn2025 Conj 16.2; the theorem is new, the concept is not.

name: Fixed parameters eps=1/2000, r0=8000, L=100, B=50, H0=8001
statement: Numerical constants fixing the stopping density, link-cycle length, suffix length and suppression exponent.
why: Parameter choice.

name: Prefix trajectory p_i, stopping step i0, p, D=np^2, m=n^2p/2
statement: p_i = 1 - 1/n - 6i/n^2; i0 chosen so p = n^{-1/2+eps}+O(n^{-2}); D ~ n^{2eps} common neighbours per edge.
why: JK/BFL trajectory.

name: Rooted template (H,I), extension count X_{H,I,psi}, scaling S(H,I), same-root subtemplate, rooted density, balanced
statement: Rooted extension counts with scaling n^{v-|I|} p^{e}; balanced = every same-root subtemplate has rooted density <= that of (H,I).
why: Standard (Spencer counting extensions; JK templates).

name: Good prefix (degrees, codegrees, link-cycle counts up to length 8000, two rooted-extension upper bounds) with failure prob <= exp(-(log n)^{4/3})
statement: There is a prefix-measurable event G_n of probability 1-n^{-omega(1)} on which G_{i0} has (1+-n^{-c}) degrees and codegrees, (1+-n^{-c})D^j labelled j-cycles in every vertex link (3<=j<=8000), and polylog-factor extension upper bounds for all templates on <= 8001 vertices.
why: Cited black box in the paper (C5 invocation). Lean re-proves it by a different route (see L10-L14).

name: Triangle degree d_e and the linear triangle hypergraph T on E(G)
statement: Fix a good G; E=E(G), T=triangles as 3-subsets of E; d_e=(1+-n^{-c})D.
why: Standard.

name: Priority scan; edge "untouched before t"
statement: Independent uniform priorities U_T; scan in increasing order, accept a triangle iff all its edges remain.
why: Standard.

name: Priority representation
statement: The accepted-triangle sequence of the scan has the law of uniform sequential triangle removal from G.
why: Re-proved, standard.

name: Call (focus of one or two edges, threshold, parent); root/non-root calls; candidates; child call
statement: Root call: focus {e}, candidates all triangles at e. Non-root call: focus {f,g} subset T, threshold U_T, candidates all triangles meeting the focus except T; each candidate S has a unique focus edge e(S) and child call on S\{e(S)} at threshold U_S.
why: Close variant of the recursive random-rank oracle for greedy MIS/matching (Nguyen-Onak 2008; Yoshida-Yamamoto-Ito 2009) and of Spencer/Grable backward exploration, specialised to edge-pair foci.

name: Finite paired test with one jointly ordered candidate list and expose-all rule
statement: At a call: expose priorities of all candidates in fixed type order; scan those below threshold in priority order (one joint order across both focus edges); stop false at first true child, else true.
why: Engineering variant of the standard oracle; the paper flags joint ordering as essential.

name: Exact paired test
statement: The finite test terminates; a root call at (e,t) returns true iff e is untouched before t; a pair call returns true iff both focus edges are untouched before U_T.
why: Correctness of a greedy oracle; same induction as Nguyen-Onak style simulations.

name: Independent unfolding (fresh uniform priority at every occurrence in the tree of all possible calls); omitted-parent root variants
statement: Deterministic tree of all possible calls; an independent uniform variable per child occurrence serves as priority and threshold; distinct roots use disjoint trees.
why: Spencer's branching process realised on the graph's computation tree (cf. belief-propagation computation trees). Lean calls the resulting equations "cavity" equations.

name: Finite evaluation of unfoldings (factorial decay of decreasing paths)
statement: Almost surely every call at every threshold has a finite evaluation; P(decreasing path of length j) <= M^j/j!.
why: Penrose-Sudbury 2005 argument re-given.

name: q_e(t), q_{e,T}(t) (omitted-parent survival), I_{e,T}(t) = int_0^t q_{f,T} q_{g,T}
statement: Survival probabilities in the independent unfolding and the message integral.
why: Cavity/message quantities; Spencer f(c) analogue per edge type.

name: Product identities
statement: P(pair true at t) = q_{f,T} q_{g,T}; q_e = prod_{S ni e}(1 - I_{e,S}); q_{e,T} = prod_{S ni e, S != T}(1 - I_{e,S}); all C^1.
why: Exact cavity / belief-propagation recursion on a tree; Spencer1995 eq. for scalar case.

name: Scalar comparison q(t) = (1+2Dt)^{-1/2} (solves q' = -D q^3)
statement: Spencer's branching survival law (1+Qc)^{-1/Q} with Q=2, c=Dt.
why: Cited formula.

name: Log time s = (1/2)log(1+2Dt); z_e(s) = log(q_e/q)
statement: Change of variables making q = e^{-s}; z(0)=0.
why: Standard ODE normalization.

name: Edge-adjacency matrix A (A_ef=1 iff e!=f in a common triangle)
statement: Real symmetric matrix on E(G) with row sums 2d_e.
why: Adjacency matrix of the triangle-hypergraph 2-shadow on edges (standard construction).

name: Exact z-equation and linearized error ||z' + (A/D)z||_inf <= C(n^{-2a}+n^{-c}+log n/D) under bootstrap assumptions
statement: Differentiating the product identities; bootstrap ||z||_inf <= n^{-a}, I_{e,T} <= 1/2.
why: Routine linearization/bootstrap.

name: Link trace estimate tr((M_u/D)^r) = 1 + O(n^{-c*}) from link-cycle counts
statement: Closed walks of even length r=8000 in the vertex link: injective walks are labelled cycles; tree-supported and cycle-supported non-injective patterns are lower order.
why: Quantitative re-proof of a known method.

name: Star approximation ||M_u/D - 11^T/N_u||_2 = O(n^{-gamma})
statement: Leading eigenvalue ~1 and simple; other eigenvalues O(n^{-gamma}); eigenvector close to normalized all-ones.
why: Standard eigenvalue perturbation.

name: Star-average decomposition: P = sum_u 11^T/N_u (extended to E), R = A/D - P with ||R||_2 = O(n^{-gamma}), ||R||_inf = O(1)
statement: A is the sum of the extended link matrices M_u (two edges in a common triangle share a unique vertex); each edge lies in exactly two stars, so the l2 error does not grow with n.
why: Novel use; P = B^T N^{-1} B for the unsigned vertex-edge incidence B is classical (line-graph identity B^T B = 2I + A_line).

name: Vertex-space factorization P = UV, VU = Id + W and max-norm bound ||e^{-sP}||_inf <= 1+2s, ||e^{-sP}||_2 <= 1
statement: (Uy)_{uv} = y_u+y_v, (Vx)_u = average over star; e^{-sP} = Id - U int_0^s e^{-v(Id+W)} dv V; ||e^{-v(Id+W)}||_inf <= 1.
why: Push-through identity (UV)^j = U(VU)^{j-1}V is standard; its use to control an edge-space semigroup by a vertex random walk is the new move. Part of candidate E1.

name: Finite bounded-perturbation (Dyson) expansion with mixed norms: K terms in max norm, remainder in l2 and converted by sqrt(m)
statement: Iterate E(s) = E0(s) - int E0(s-v) R E(v) dv K times, K gamma > 2; terms are polylog in max norm; remainder <= n (Cn^{-gamma})^K (log n)^K/K! = o(1).
why: Cited expansion; mixed-norm remainder trick is standard in analysis (e.g. resolvent expansions in random-matrix local laws).

name: Uniform max-norm semigroup bound sup_{s<=log n} ||e^{-sA/D}||_inf <= C1 (1+log n)^J
statement: For every graph satisfying the degree, codegree and link-cycle conditions.
why: No neighbour found that controls a max-norm heat semigroup of a quasirandom edge-adjacency operator via star averaging; ingredients (trace method, line-graph identity, Dyson expansion) are individually known. Candidate E1.

name: Unfolded probabilities q_e, q_{e,T} = (1+o(1))q(t), I_{e,T} = O(log n / D) uniformly
statement: Bootstrap/continuity argument using I20 and I26.
why: Standard bootstrap once I26 is available.

name: Off-pattern product bound q_{f,T}q_{g,T}/(1-J_n)^2 <= 2q(t)^2
statement: Deleting at most two no-success factors from a pair call increases the product by at most (1-J_n)^{-2}.
why: Direct corollary.

name: Triangle type vs occurrence
statement: A member of T as opposed to its occurrences in an unfolding.
why: Plumbing.

name: k in {1,2} uniformly sampled oriented root edges, all roots executed at threshold 1; collision event C_k = some type exposed twice among all exposed lists
statement: Compares the finite tests (shared priorities) to independent unfoldings (disjoint trees).
why: Standard sampled-root second-moment experiment.

name: Coupling by exposed triangle types: |P(X^fin in H) - P(X^ind in H)| <= P_ind(C_k)
statement: Use U_T at the first exposure of each type and fresh variables afterwards; executions agree until a repeat.
why: First-repetition coupling, standard in local-limit arguments.

name: Formal graph Gamma of visited calls with label map lambda, formal vertices, birth calls, properties (i)-(iv)
statement: Each root adds a formal edge; each visited child glues a new vertex to its attachment edge; the only triangles of Gamma are gluing triangles.
why: Exploration-graph encodings are standard in local analyses (Spencer, Bohman triangle-free), but this gluing graph is tailored.

name: Ancestral call path; Gamma_{a,b}; extra-edge witness
statement: (a,b) distinct, nonadjacent in Gamma, labels adjacent in G, lambda injective on Gamma_{a,b}.
why: "Cycle in the explored neighbourhood" certificate; tailored form new.

name: Geometric witness for a collision: C_k produces an extra-edge witness; P(C_k) <= O(1/n) + P(witness exists)
statement: Case analysis on injectivity of lambda and on the latest vertex of a formal triangle.
why: Tree-likeness certificate; close in spirit to standard "explored ball is a tree unless a cycle is found" arguments.

name: Call forest paths, pattern (h, l1, l2, marks, focus choices), formal graph J, J^+ = J+ab; pattern count C 2^l
statement: v(J) = 2r+l, e(J) = r+2l.
why: Bookkeeping.

name: Embedding an extra edge: #emb(J^+ -> G) <= (2m)^r (2D)^l D^{-B}, via a last-L-births suffix template for long patterns
statement: Short patterns: whole J^+ is a template with all subtemplate scalings >=1, gain p. Long: template on the last L=100 born vertices with backward edges and ab has scaling D^L p < 1 and all completion scalings <= 1, so polylog many extensions; gain D^{-B} independent of path length.
why: Template counting is standard (JK, BFL); the suffix trick to get a length-independent gain is new but routine for experts.

name: Visitation weights b(t) = q(t)^2, C_D = 1+2D, mu = log(1+2D)/(2D)
statement: b is the off-pattern survival factor; mu its integral.
why: Definition.

name: Off-pattern event O_x: every off-pattern candidate at a required call below t_x has a false child, evaluated hypothetically
statement: Necessary for visiting all required calls; O_x independent across x given selected priorities.
why: New device; hypothetical evaluation of subtrees follows Lemma finite-evaluation.

name: Visiting an embedded pattern: P(all required calls visited) <= C_D^3 (2mu)^l / (h! l1! l2!)
statement: Decreasing priorities along each segment give 1/j!; each selected priority carries a factor 2b(u) from O_x; integrating gives mu^j/j!.
why: Decreasing-path 1/l! bounds are standard (Nguyen-Onak 2008; Penrose-Sudbury); weighting by off-pattern failure is the new twist.

name: Uniform collision bound P_ind(C_k) = O(D^{15-B} + n^{-1}) = o(D^{-1})
statement: Pattern count x embedding bound x root probability x visitation bound, summed: D^{-B} C_D^3 exp(24 D mu) = O(D^{15-B}).
why: Cluster I32-I40 delivers o(1/D) coupling error for adaptive paired queries with growing D; no neighbour found achieving sub-1/D local-approximation error in this setting. Candidate E2.

name: Moment identities: P(all k finite roots true | prefix) = E[(F_n/m)^k | prefix]; unfolded = ((1/m) sum_e q_e(1))^k
statement: Sampling roots with replacement turns survival probabilities into moments.
why: Standard.

name: Conditional L2: E[(Y_n-1)^2 | prefix] = o(1) uniformly on G_n; normalization a_n = mq(1)/n^{3/2} -> 1/(2sqrt2); removal of bad prefixes
statement: Y_n = F_n/(m q(1)); bad prefix contribution <= Cn P(G_n^c) = o(1).
why: Routine.

name: Scope remark: no claim for arbitrary starting graphs, general hypergraph removal, or fluctuations
statement: Scope limitation.
why: Not a mathematical item.

name: ExposureTree: a free monad of priority exposures with "fresh" (independent) and shared interpretations
statement: Inductive tree of exposure queries over keys K with values V; fresh interprets every exposure with an independent copy; product PMF gives the shared one.
why: Formalization device (free monad / decision tree); corresponds to Grable's adaptive exposure decision trees.

name: Discrete-grid priorities: priorities in Fin N, depth-bounded grid queries, grid->continuum error
statement: All probabilities are finite PMFs on Fin N; errors from ties and grid are shown to vanish as N -> infinity.
why: Formalization device.

name: Cavity operator, cavityDepth (Picard iteration) and cavityLimit in a space of bounded continuous functions
statement: cavityOperator H q e parent t = prod_{T in candidates}(1 - int_0^t prod q); cavityDepth k = k-fold iterate; Cauchy in BCF; limit = solution of the product identities.
why: Cavity method / belief propagation (statistical physics) plus Picard iteration: transfer. The Lean naming makes the import explicit.

name: Moving star average: movingStarMean/movingStarLift on a shrinking active edge set; movingResidualForcing; trajectorySeminorm; activeLinf/activeL2
statement: Time-dependent version of P = UV for a nested family of active edge sets, with seminorms along trajectories.
why: Moving (discrete-time, shrinking-support) variant of the paper's star-averaging device I23-I24.

name: movingStar_mixed_stability and moving_perturbation_mixed_norm_absorb
statement: Mixed l2/l_inf stability of x_{k+1} = x_k - a_k(P_k x_k + R_k x_k) + forcing on a nested active set.
why: Discrete-time analogue of I25-I26.

name: Self-contained prefix: centred codegree vector recurrence with star drift; edge-barrier improvement; degree/wheel/balanced-template tracking; rooted upper boun…
statement: For triangle removal from K_n up to density n^{-1/2+1/2000}: codegrees (1+-n^{-c}), degrees, link-cycle counts (via wheels as 2-balanced templates), polylog^{3*8001+2} rooted upper bounds, with failure <= exp(-(log n)^{4/3}). Proved from Freedman (re-proved) and the moving-star stability, without Joos-Kuhn.
why: Replaces the paper's only black box (JK, 87 pp.) with a triangle-specific proof in which codegree self-correction is a linear max-norm stability statement for the same star-averaged operator; no human neighbour found (BFL2015 needed triangular extensions; JK chains/branching families). Lean-only, no prose exposition; see novelty pass.

name: Freedman inequality for finite Markov histories (two-sided and maximal forms)
statement: P(sum of bounded martingale increments >= r and predictable variance <= V) <= exp(-r^2/(4(V+cr))).
why: Freedman 1975 (transfer from probability).

name: Rooted-count moment bound from intact-survival: E[X^q] <= U((2((q+1)k)+1)^k M)^q if P(F intact) <= U p^{|F|}
statement: Spencer-type extension-count moment bound transferred to the removal process.
why: Standard moment method.

name: Max-norm semigroup stability via star averaging (A/D = P + R, P = UV, VU = I + W, mixed-norm Dyson expansion)
why: Named by the paper as one of the two new continuation estimates (introduction.tex:130-133). The naive bound loses e^{O(D)} (stability.tex:100-103); this device is what makes the D -> infinity regime work. Not a subterm of the goal or of L; the decisive object P = sum of star averages appears nowhere in BFL/JK/Spencer. Reused in Lean (moving-star version) to give a self-contained prefix proof replacing JK: evidence of payoff beyond its own theorem.

name: o(1/D) collision bound: extra-edge witness + suffix-template D^{-B} gain + off-pattern-weighted visitation (2mu)^l/l!
why: Paper flags the sub-1/D precision as new and necessary for the second moment (introduction.tex:116-118; witnesses.tex:4-7). Lean canonical_collision_sum dominated share 0.317 (passes 20% proxy). Weighting each step of a visited path by the off-pattern failure factor b(t)=q(t)^2 converts D^l path counts into poly(D) total, a non-obvious quantitative move.

name: Lean-only self-contained prefix via moving-star codegree stability
why: Removes the paper's only black box (JK, 87 pp.) with ~7k lines of a triangle-specific proof; dominated share 0.269. BFL2015 needed carefully designed triangular extensions to pass the n^{7/4} barrier; the Lean route controls the whole codegree vector by a linear max-norm stability statement plus link spectral control from wheel counts.

name: Paired-focus finite test with one jointly ordered list and expose-all rule
why: Paper says joint ordering is "essential to the later visitation estimate"; full exposure makes collisions detectable.

name: Independent unfolding and exact product (cavity) identities
why: Load-bearing: all continuation probabilities live here.

name: Max-norm semigroup stability via star averaging
statement: If G has (1+-n^{-c}) degrees and codegrees and (1+-n^{-c})D^j labelled j-cycles in every link (j <= 8000), then sup_{0<=s<=log n} ||exp(-sA/D)||_inf <= C(1+log n)^J, where A is the edge-adjacency matrix of the triangle hypergraph. Mechanism: each link matrix is l2-close to its averaging projection; the sum P of star averages factors as UV with VU = I + W (W = neighbour random walk), so ||e^{-sP}||_inf <= 1+2s; the l2-small remainder R is handled by a K-term Dyson expansion whose remainder is co…
why: No near-equivalent found anywhere; non-analytic; knockout-essential and reused (Lean prefix) beyond its own proposition. Confidence is low because each step is one move from a classical tool; Test 4 may well show it is discoverable once l_inf stability is identified as the bottleneck.

name: o(1/D) collision bound for adaptive paired queries (extra-edge witness + suffix template + off-pattern-weighted visitation)
statement: P_ind(some triangle type exposed twice) = O(D^{15-B} + 1/n) = o(1/D): a repeat yields two visited ancestral call paths plus an extra G-edge; embeddings of such path unions are <= (2m)^r (2D)^l D^{-B}; visiting a prescribed embedded pattern has probability <= C_D^3 (2mu)^l/(h! l1! l2!) with mu = log(1+2D)/(2D).
why: Load-bearing and non-analytic, but each component has a close precedent (Nguyen-Onak/Penrose-Sudbury decreasing paths, Spencer/local-limit tree-likeness, JK extension bounds). The new content is quantitative (off-pattern weights, length-independent D^{-B}), which the codebook grades as a variant. Upgrade to N3 only if Test 4 shows models fail to reach sub-1/D precision.

name: Lean-only self-contained prefix via moving-star codegree stability
statement: For triangle removal from K_n up to density n^{-1/2+1/2000}, with probability >= 1 - exp(-(log n)^{4/3}): codegrees, degrees and link-cycle counts are (1 +- n^{-1/80000})-accurate and rooted extension counts are at most polylog^{3*8001+2} times scaling. The centred codegree vector x_k obeys x_{k+1} = x_k - a_k (P_k x_k + R_k x_k) + martingale forcing (moving star average P_k, link-spectral remainder R_k), and its max norm is kept below a barrier by mixed-norm stability; Freedman controls the fo…
why: As an item it is a variant of C1 inside the same family (templated reuse). Its real significance is as evidence for C1: the same device yields, within this release, a new proof of a BFL/JK-type prefix theorem for triangles that humans needed 40-90 pages and different machinery for. That is the downstream-speedup signature PLAN step 9 asks for, but it is produced by the same model on the same problem, so it is not a held-out test. Lean-only and without prose; the reconstruction is from signature…

name: Paired-focus recursive test with a single jointly ordered candidate list and expose-all rule
statement: Edge e survives to threshold t iff no triangle S at e with U_S < t has both other edges surviving to U_S; for a pair focus the two edges' candidates are scanned in one priority order and all candidate priorities are exposed.
why: Standard oracle with an engineering refinement (joint ordering, expose-all) that the paper needs for C2.

name: Independent unfolding with exact product (cavity) identities
statement: Give every occurrence in the tree of possible calls a fresh priority; then q_e = prod_{S ni e}(1 - int_0^t q_{f,S} q_{g,S}).
why: Transfer: Spencer's branching process, made exact per edge type (cavity equations).

name: Two-random-root moment experiment and first-repetition coupling
statement: P(k sampled roots survive | prefix) = E[(F_n/m)^k | prefix]; finite vs independent answers differ by at most P(repeat).
why: Standard.

name: Incidence criterion
statement: Let ell be an odd prime, K a finite field of characteristic 2 containing a primitive ell-th root of unity, kappa = ell^2. Given an (ell+1)-regular finite set system (V,F) of incidence girth >= 12 and x_v in K^m with sum_V x_v x_v^T = -I_m, sum_{v in f} x_v x_v^T = 0 for every f, and 0 < m < |V| <= m*kappa, there are a finitely presented G with ell-torsion and a,b in K[G] with ab = 1 != ba.
why: The only item in the family with no neighbour found in any field and no retrieval trigger in the trace. Its content is a finite certificate that beats the sofic rank bound (t < m*kappa) by exploiting D = ell+1 = 0 in K. That is exactly why it cannot exist in characteristic 0 and why it forces nonsoficity. Against: every component is standard (averaging idempotents, glued finite groups, HNN character twists, augmentation specialization, DJ transfer). It emerged incrementally from the model's own…

name: Glued subgroup averages give a rectangular one-sided identity
statement: With P_v the averaging idempotent of K_v = F_ell^2 and the partition of K_v \ {1} by its ell+1 lines L_f: sum_{u in K_v} u = 1 + sum_{f ni v}(L^_f - 1). Hence U_{-,v} = -kappa x_v P_v and T_{v,-} = P_v x_v^T satisfy UT = I_m once the local Gram sums vanish and the total is -I_m.
why: Standard averaging device. The new use (subgroup averages weighted by rank-one Gram matrices) is the mechanism of C1 and is graded there.

name: Punctured polynomial pairing
statement: For q = 2^h, holes O in the lower set S_{(q-2)/2} of F_q^n, and x_v = (f_o(v))_{o in O} with f_o the degree-<=(q-2)/2 interpolant of the indicator of o on S: sum_{v in line} x_v x_v^T = 0 for every full affine line, and sum_{v notin O} x_v x_v^T = -I_m.
why: A retrieval-triggered transfer from coding theory, built on a classical line-sum fact. The punctured-hole trick is a new arrangement, not a new concept. It is graded N2 because the paper's named precedents (GL, DLZ) supply the decisive features (products and line restrictions).

name: Exactly regular girth-12 affine-line system with holes
statement: For large h there are holes O in S with 2N/D^2 <= |O| <= 7N/D^2 and a family of full affine lines avoiding O, D-regular on V = A \ O, with incidence girth >= 12.
why: Heavy but technique-standard (random slabs, LLL, trades, Linnik). It dominates proof length, not novelty, so it is a budget sink rather than a cut.

name: Character packing and the specialization certificate of the reverse defect
statement: Twist via HNN letters tau_v so that conjugates of eP_v become orthogonal character idempotents eQ_{alpha_v}. Pack t coordinates into m slots (t <= m*kappa), and detect b_mat*a_mat != 1 via J_0 Delta C = e(TU - P), which specializes to X^T X - I_t != 0 because rank X <= m < t.
why: A conjunction of standard tools (HNN, character idempotents, specialization, rank). It is borderline N2 only because the 'sandwich back into the embedded subgroup algebra' trick is neat. The trace graded it N2, and I downgrade it because no step needs an idea absent from L.

name: Planar balance (Euler) embedding of the local groups
statement: If the incidence graph has girth >= 12, each F_ell^2 embeds in the glued group N. A minimal balanced planar diagram yields black degree >= 3, white degree >= 2 and faces of length >= 12, contradicting Euler's formula.
why: Standard small-cancellation counting, replacing an imported theorem (Haefliger). Insight-driven in the trace, but the origin is constructed from known counting, and the simplification ratio is about 1:1.

name: Explicit Dykema-Juschenko finite-factor matrix units
statement: Embed Mat_m(K[L]) in a corner of K[L x F], F = (Z/ell)^m semidirect S_m, and add the complementary idempotent.
why: Named precedent in L; made explicit only.

name: Linnik prime ell = -1 mod q^100
statement: Least prime ell = -1 mod q^100 with ell <= c q^{100L}.
why: Imported number theory (transfer).

name: Group-algebra to cellular-automaton transfer (Gottschalk corollary)
statement: T_b is injective with left inverse T_a; a nonzero coefficient of ba-1 gives a delta configuration outside the image.
why: Standard transfer; the paper says 'this standard transfer'.

name: Parity criterion for a one-sided inverse
statement: For finite loopless graphs immersed in a rose, coned to give G = pi_1(X), with |S_x cap S_x'| odd for (x,x') != (x_A,x_A), |S_{x_A}| even, |S_x cap S_y| odd across A'xB', and root protection: a = sum g_x, b = sum g_x^{-1} (= a*), c = sum h_y^{-1} satisfy ab = 1, ac = 0, c != 0 in F2[G].
why: An explicit adaptation of a model-produced precedent in L ('We adapt those arguments'). The original parity mechanism belongs to family 196 and should be graded there, against pre-release literature (Mineyev, Rips-Segev).

name: Fano-complement extra letters (balanced types with one parity exception)
statement: T = points of PG(2,128) plus 7 extra letters identified with the Fano plane. Extra parts are complements of Fano lines (4-sets, pairwise meeting in 2), plus the full 7-set at x_A only. With m = 1 mod 4 the label counts balance exactly and all intersections are odd except S_{x_A} cap S_{x_A}.
why: The paper's self-declared change relative to ZD. A neat but small design gadget; borderline N1.

name: Word-weight decay and bounded-pattern exclusion with multiplicity stages
statement: sum_{W in T^h} P(W)^2 <= exp(-2 delta h), and with probability 1-o(1) there is no bounded system of almost completely paired paths. Counts are organized by edge multiplicities and nearly aligned subdivisions.
why: Re-derivation of a model-produced precedent in L, with new constants.

name: Planar-separator extraction and cone-surgery asphericity/root protection
statement: Every reduced spherical arrangement contains a bounded nearly paired pattern (Lipton-Tarjan separator, parameters fixed in the right order). Hence X is aspherical, G is torsion-free with a finite 2-dimensional K(G,1), and paths from the roots have nontrivial labels.
why: Inherited from ZD. Whether the separator-based arrangement exclusion is new relative to pre-release literature is a question for family 196.

name: From a binary DF defect to a determinant below one (trace-gap projection + modular lifting + block shears)
statement: From a2*b2 = 1 != b2*a2 over K2[H2] (char 2), build in (bigoplus C3) x| H2 a rational orthogonal projection P of trace d+theta whose mod-2 reduction factors through d columns. Lift the factorization mod q = 2^k and form an integral matrix A invertible over Q[G] with det_FK(A) = q^{-theta} in (0,1).
why: Borderline N3. No prior statement of 'char-2 DF failure => DC failure' was found, so this is a new bridge.
