Each component, though, has a named precedent (Dicks-Schick projections, FK derivative, idempotent lifting), and the model reached the composite idea early and unprompted. Graded N2 per the PLAN's named-precedent rule. It moves to N3-provisional if an expert confirms the implication is unknown and the components are judged non-equivalent.

name: Triangular compression from a low-rank fit of a triangle-free graph
statement: If F_ij = sum_T alpha_i(T) beta_j(T) fits a graph (F_ii = 1, F_ij = 0 off edges), F_ij P_i P_j = 0 for i < j, and Y_i J_i = I_d, J_i Y_i = P_i I_w, then D_sharp C_sharp = I_{md} with C_sharp in Mat_{wt x md}, by inverting the unipotent triangular part. With wt < md this gives a one-sided inverse with a visible defect.
why: An architectural sibling of C1 (model-produced, in L) instantiated by a TCS minrank transfer. The new bridge (minrank to DF) is notable, but the item is a variant.

name: Large modular idempotents with ordered two-sided annihilations
statement: For H built from P = (Z/p)^3 and cyclic Fourier data, there is an idempotent e in K[H] with (u(s)-1)^ell e = 0 and e (v(s)-1)^ell = 0 for all s, and regular rank d/w > 1/96. It comes from the top-degree Jennings filtration plus a nonsingular diagonal weighted pairing (Schwartz-Zippel).
why: Known tools assembled to a new specification; borderline N1.

name: Incidence criterion (PV3): regular set system with incidence girth >= 12 and rank-one Gram weights vanishing on every member with total -I_m, m < t <= m*ell^2 …
why: Reduces an infinite group-algebra question to finite incidence + linear-algebra data; the whole paper is organized around it (load-bearing well above 20%). No retrieved antecedent; no literature is cited for it in the trace or paper; the model reached it only after 9 strategy switches. Non-analytic: neither 'hypergraph', 'girth' nor Gram identities occur in the goal statement ab=1, ba!=1. Arrived with no visible trigger at the final re-entry (L402).

name: Punctured low-degree polynomial pairing (PV4): interpolation polynomials at holes of F_q^n; products of degree <= q-2 sum to zero on full lines; retained total…
why: Supplies the only known instance of EC1's hypotheses; characteristic two enters exactly here (D = ell+1 = 0 in K). Not a coding theorem: the paper uses no result from GL/DLZ; the 'holes' trick is specific.

name: Glued subgroup averages -> rectangular one-sided factorization with faithful embeddings and character projections (PV2).
why: Core algebraic mechanism; necessary. Constructed early, with no retrieval.

name: Reverse-defect certificate by specialization on an embedded subgroup algebra: X^T X - I_t != 0 because rank <= m < t (PV7).
why: Clean certificate that avoids the word problem; essential for 'rigorous certificate' demanded by the prompt.

name: Planar balanced-diagram Euler embedding argument (PV6).
why: Self-contained; replaces an imported theorem (insight-driven).

name: Vertical-component structure theorem for the fixed-support coefficient scheme (a36).
why: Correct, clean structural statement that any counterexample is intrinsically positive characteristic.

name: Shifted target tree S^+ with charging of fresh splits (relative absolute-cost bound)
statement: Move every internal branching depth of the target topology S one level later (S^+). For large L and eta-regular depths, the shifted target branching depths avoid all branching depths of the old two-copy tree, so each of the 2b target branching vertices must be created by a fresh split at a unary vertex, each with coefficient m_{e+1}-m_{e+2} = -delta. Hence sum_E |c_E| <= C_{q,k} delta^b for b charged vertices, and (1/|J|) sum_E |c_E| <= C_{k,eta} with J = kappa(S^+)^2 ~ delta^{2b}: errors survi…
why: No neighbour found for the shift-plus-charging device in the stochastic-stability, RPC, diluted-cavity, Bayesian strong-RS or sparse-graph (Coja-Oghlan et al.) literatures. The paper names no precedent for it, while naming antecedents for everything around it. It is non-analytic and knockout-essential, with a qualitative error-budget drop. Against: it sits one inference from clause C10, which the trace states three times, and 'move to general position' is a generic habit. Its value is local to …

name: Finite-tree insertion calculus: tree density, canceled-anchor expansion, reference totals kappa(S)
statement: For power-mean iterated kernels, inserting a path factor A changes the tree law by the density prod_a A^a prod_beta Y_beta^{gamma_beta}. Differentiating gives signed sums over extension histories (an old leaf with coefficient 1, or a fresh path at beta with coefficient gamma_beta). The total coefficient over extensions realizing a prescribed shape S is kappa(S) = prod_v prod_{j<a_v} (m_{d_v} - j m_{d_v+1}).
why: A load-bearing new packaging of a known power-mean/cascade calculus, which the paper itself attributes to MP01/PT04/Ruelle. Near-analytic in the goal's own recursion.

name: Depth-selecting Rademacher marks and identities on prescribed colored trees
statement: A countable family of bounded marked Poisson perturbations: signs sampled at assigned depths of auxiliary paths, rational test functions g and g_0, and a spin or marker anchor. Their concentrated scores give, via Palm insertion, Taylor-coefficient vanishing (u_nu in [j^{-j},2j^{-j}], t_nu = 1/j) and polarization, sum_E c_E E[f R_E] - E f sum_E c_E E[R_E] -> 0 for every prescribed colored shape. The sign products select split depths exactly.
why: A clean new device inside a well-known genre whose precedents the paper names.

name: Conditional-decorrelation induction on squared conditional covariance v_N(S,d), with three-copy positivity
statement: Induct on the number of leaves, using the depth-averaged quantity v_N(S,d) = N^{-2} E sum_{ij} Cov(A_{S,i},A_{S,j} | F_d)^2. The three-copy inequality turns signed identities into a nonnegative bound.
why: A templated strengthening (carry an extra tracked quantity + all substructures), so capped at N2. Barbier-Panchenko is a close neighbour for the induction shape.

name: Marker anchor variance identity
statement: With S_0 = 1 and a full copy of S added fresh at e-1, both sides of the prescribed-tree identity carry the same coefficient. This gives Var(E[R_S|F_{e-1}]) -> 0 at fixed L.
why: Overrides the trace's N2. It is an instance of the paper's own identity (C3) with the trivial anchor, with no independent content beyond C3.

name: Random-tree law Q_k for the logarithmic power-mean expansion
statement: log Y_0 = sum_k (-1)^{k-1} t^k/k E_{Q_k} E_T prod D^a, where Q_k grows a tree by adding a fresh child at internal vertex beta with probability (n_beta m_{d+1} - m_d)/n.
why: Overrides the trace's N1-N2. A reorganization of a known expansion whose tree law matches the standard RPC replica-sampling rule. N0 if the equivalence is confirmed for all k.

name: Concentration on average over separated branching depths, with martingale-energy depth continuity
statement: Prove multioverlap concentration only after averaging over eta-regular branching depths. Undo the one-level shift using sum_d E|mu_{d+1}-mu_d|^2 <= 1 (a bounded martingale), so the average one-step change is O(1/L). Exceptional trees have vanishing Q_k probability.
why: The averaged target is the enabling choice for C1, but its mechanism (martingale energy, N0) and its genre (parameter averaging) are both known.

name: Perturbed cavity reservoir with a built-in finite auxiliary hierarchy (uniform mesh m_d = d/L)
statement: Compare sizes N and N+1 through a common reservoir whose Gibbs measure is iterated by L-1 auxiliary power-mean levels, with sublinear bounded perturbations, and select sizes and parameters with near-minimal increments.
why: Transfer of the ASS/RPC cavity frame, which the paper attributes.

name: Recursive law encoding of a uniformly sampled reservoir site, and independent-message comparison
statement: Encode the site's whole finite hierarchy by successive conditional laws (a trial law in M_L). Multioverlap concentration then lets distinct site labels be replaced by independent copies in the cavity insertion.
why: Applies a known representation idea to the built-in finite hierarchy.

name: Upper bound with all-plus normalization and convexity remainder; reduction to first moments
statement: Reproduce the PT04 interpolation bound with a normalization by the all-plus configuration and the remainder A^p - pAB^{p-1} + (p-1)B^p >= 0; truncate to reduce to first moments.
why: A minor technical variant of PT04.

name: Shifted target tree S^+ with charging of fresh splits (relative absolute-cost bound)
against: It is one step from the learned clause C10: once one knows that each fresh unary split costs delta and that the normalizer has one delta per branching vertex, forcing target splits to be fresh is a natural move. It is general position applied to tree depths. It needs the model's own tree calculus (PV3) and a standard martingale averaging (PV6), so its value is local to this framework. The downstr…
why: No precedent is named in the trace or in the paper (the paper names antecedents for the perturbation identities but none for the shift). It is reached after a visible run of six failures, three of them explicit small-denominator failures, so the obvious variants (coarse partitions, equal-exponent refinements) were tried and failed. Syntactically tiny (add 1 to every internal depth) yet it changes the proof budget qualitatively: without it, errors after division by kappa(S)^2 ~ delta^{2b} are un…

name: Marked-perturbation identities on prescribed colored trees (insertion calculus, canceled-anchor expansion, depth-selecting marks, Palm + analytic extraction)
against: Stochastic-stability identities (GG98, AC98), their diluted multioverlap versions (Barra-De Sanctis 2007) and Panchenko's invariance identities (Pan13) are close neighbours named by the paper itself. Power-mean computations with cascades are in MP01 and PT04.
why: Exact finite-tree identities for arbitrary kernels with explicit signed coefficients gamma_beta = m_d - n_beta m_{d+1} and kappa(S); marks that select split depths are a clean new device. The trace reaches it by construction after a failed transfer (Bayesian), not by retrieval.

name: Conditional-decorrelation induction on squared conditional covariance v_N(S,d)
against: Templated strengthening ('carry an extra tracked quantity' + 'all substructures'), so capped at N2 by the codebook. Conditional covariance / three-copy arguments are standard in spin-glass concentration proofs.
why: A non-obvious choice of inductive quantity (squared conditional covariance at every depth, all topologies) that makes three-copy positivity available.

name: Marker anchor variance identity
against: A one-line variant of the spin-anchor identity (S_0 = 1 instead of sigma_i); division only at fixed L.
why: Converts conditional decorrelation into ordinary concentration with a coefficient C(S,e) = -delta kappa(S) identical on both sides; neat.

name: Random-tree law Q_k for the logarithmic power-mean expansion (telescoping coefficients)
against: Power-mean expansions are known (MP01, PT04); the representation is a reorganization.
why: Elegant probabilistic representation that makes coefficient magnitudes 1/k automatically.

name: Averaging over branching depths as the notion of concentration (no uniform-in-depth concentration needed because the insertion expansion itself averages over t…
against: Averaging over a perturbation parameter to get concentration is the classic GG/Talagrand/Panchenko device; averaging over levels mirrors the pinning-lemma pigeonhole.
why: Weakening the target to exactly what the cavity expansion consumes is a strategic insight, and the paper emphasizes it.

name: recursively enumerable set
statement: S subset N^n is r.e. if a deterministic computation accepts exactly its members.
why: Textbook notion; Mathlib REPred.

name: Diophantine representation
statement: P in Z[A,W] with a in S iff P(a,w)=0 for some w in N^m.
why: Classical (DPR/MRDP).

name: single-fold / finite-fold representation
statement: Single-fold: the complete auxiliary tuple w is unique when it exists; finite-fold: finitely many tuples. All auxiliary variables are counted.
why: Matiyasevich 1974 notion.

name: single-fold polynomial system / single-fold graph
statement: A finite list of integer polynomial equations F_i(a,z)=0 whose set of complete tuples z is a singleton for a in R and empty otherwise; a single-fold graph of f:D->N^e is such a system for {(a,f(a))}.
why: Abbreviation of Matiyasevich's single-fold notion for relations and graphs.

name: unique slacks and sign codes
statement: F>=G is F-G=s with fresh s in N (strict: F-G=1+s); an integer z is z+ - z- with z+ z- = 0; polynomial arguments are named by fresh variables.
why: Folklore in Diophantine coding.

name: Composition and disjoint cases (lem:composition)
statement: Conjunctions with separate auxiliary tuples, compositions of single-fold graphs, and finite unions with pairwise disjoint argument sets are single-fold; disjoint cases use Boolean selectors e_i, gate each equation as e_i F = 0, and force every case-local variable to zero via (1-e_i) z = 0.
why: Re-proof of known closure operations; precision about zeroing inactive variables is the only addition.

name: sum-of-squares conversion
statement: F_1=...=F_r=0 over N iff sum F_i^2 = 0; no new variables.
why: Folklore.

name: the curve E: y^2 = x^3 - 25x
statement: Projective closure of y^2=x^3-25x with chord-tangent group law; the congruent-number curve for n=5.
why: Known curve; choosing a rank-one curve is part of candidate E1, not novel by itself.

name: Rank one and torsion (prop:rank-one)
statement: E(Q) has rank one and torsion {O,(0,0),(5,0),(-5,0)}; every rational point is uniquely nP+t.
why: Known; re-proved by standard descent.

name: six-coordinate rational code with shifted inverse
statement: (p,n,d,t,s,q) with pn=0, d=1+t+s, (p+n)t+d=1+qd; value (p-n)/d; t is the inverse of p+n mod d restricted to [0,d-1], and the shift by d handles d=1 without a case split.
why: Variant of the bounded-Bezout-coefficient trick in cco2024; the shift is a minor convenience.

name: Unique rational codes and arithmetic (lem:rational-codes)
statement: Every rational has exactly one valid code; any fixed finite sequence of rational field operations and comparisons has a polynomial implementation with unique outputs and auxiliaries.
why: Routine.

name: point code with identity flag
statement: Two valid rational codes and a flag o in {0,1}; o=1 forces both numerators zero (represents O), o=0 imposes the curve equation after clearing denominators.
why: Routine encoding.

name: Single-fold point arithmetic (lem:point-arithmetic)
statement: Addition of coded points has a single-fold implementation via seven disjoint cases with a case-local slope code; the same holds for fixed addition chains and multiplication by a fixed positive integer.
why: Routine single-fold transcription of the group law.

name: naive x-height, canonical height, uniform comparison
statement: H(a/d)=max(|a|,d), h_x(Q)=log H(x(Q)); hat h(Q) = (1/2) lim 4^{-N} h_x([2^N]Q); hat h([j]Q)=j^2 hat h(Q), hat h>0 on nontorsion, and |log H(x(Q)) - 2 hat h(Q)| <= c_E.
why: Cross-field transfer of Neron-Tate theory.

name: height constants kappa, m_*, a_E
statement: kappa > e^{6 c_E} integer; m_* even with a_E = 2 m_*^2 hat h(P) satisfying a_E > 2c_E and 2a_E - 6c_E > log kappa: 'A fixed scalar multiplication enlarges the quadratic coefficient while leaving the uniform error bound unchanged.'
why: Parameter tuning inside candidate E1; by itself a routine choice.

name: W(Q) = H(x([m_*]Q)) and the quadratic sequence W_j
statement: W(Q)=H(x([m_*]Q)) (1 if [m_*]Q=O); W(nP+t) depends only on j=|n|; log W_j = a_E j^2 + eps_j with |eps_j|<=c_E; (W_j) strictly increasing and unbounded.
why: Component of candidate E1; the ingredients (heights of multiples, Poonen's denominator growth) are known, the use as a single-fold integer sequence is new.

name: representative point; Lemma representatives
statement: Q is a representative if Q != O, y(Q)>=0, W(Q)>1 and x(Q) >= x(Q+t) for all t in T; for each j>=1 exactly one point of (jP+T) u (-jP+T) is a representative.
why: Simple normalization device (max x in a torsion coset, nonnegative y).

name: index bracket at input scale
statement: Require a representative Q with W(Q) <= u + W_1 < max{W(Q+P), W(Q-P)}; the neighbour maximum equals W_{k+1}, so exactly one k>=1 (and one Q) qualifies.
why: Standard bracketing of a strictly increasing sequence; neighbour-max trick avoids sign of the index.

name: square window: multiplicative test of r = k^2
kind: key construction / lemma (proof paragraph; Lean lemma)
statement: With L_0 = W([2]Q) W(R) W_1 and D_0 = W(Q)^2 max{W(R+P),W(R-P)}, log(L_0/D_0) = 2a_E(k^2 - r) + e with |e| <= 6c_E (from the identity (2k)^2 - 2k^2 - ((r+1)^2 - r^2) + 1 = 2(k^2-r)); hence L_0 <= kappa D_0 and D_0 <= kappa L_0 iff r = k^2.
why: Passes a quick test 1 (no precedent found for using quadratic Neron-Tate growth to test a quadratic index relation by a bounded number of multiplicative comparisons); non-analytic; logically load-bearing for the whole elliptic branch. Syntactically tiny (one identity), Cook-like.

name: single-fold growth function (prop:growth)
statement: There are a total g: N->N with single-fold graph (output and all auxiliaries unique), delta>0 and u_0>=4 such that delta (log u)^2 < log g(u) < u log u for u >= u_0; concretely g(u) = W_{k^2} where k is the bracket index of u.
why: Head of candidate cluster E1: a single-fold Diophantine JR-type function did not exist in the literature (the obstruction is the periodicity of Pell-based constructions); built from a rank-one curve via I16-I19.

name: Pell sequences (lem:pell-sequences)
statement: For a>=2: positive solutions of x^2-(a^2-1)y^2=1 are exactly (x_i,y_i); y_i == i mod (a-1); (2a-1)^{i-1} <= y_i <= (2a)^{i-1}; and b^n <= y_{n+1}(bu)/y_{n+1}(u) <= b^n (1+1/(2u-1))^n.
why: Classical; the ratio bound via R_i(bu) >= b R_i(u) is a short induction.

name: index cutoff u^u < (2u-1)^{u-1}
statement: For u>=4, u^u < (2u-1)^{u-1}; combined with g(u) < u^u it forces Pell indices below u.
why: Routine.

name: single-fold power graph from a growth function (prop:power)
statement: If g has a complete single-fold graph and delta(log u)^2 < log g(u) < u log u for u >= u_0, then Pow(b,n,c) <=> (b>=2 and c=b^n) has a complete single-fold representation, using two Pell equations with parameters bu and u, cutoffs 0<F,H<g(u), residues F == H == n+1, and integer quotient F = cH + r.
why: Close variant of the paired-Pell single-fold construction of mati1974/cco2024 with a different cutoff.

name: self-referential Pell scale u = (c+1)^l (n+1)(b+1) + u_0
statement: u is a fixed polynomial in the output c and the inputs; once indices are pinned, c >= b^n from the lower ratio bound, so the error c n/(2u-1-n) < 1 is controlled by the output itself; l > 3/(delta log 2) ensures the intended Pell coordinates lie below g(u).
why: Small, clever variant; a free-scale removal of this kind is the standard aim of single-fold constructions (mati1974 Sec.4).

name: binary containment x <= y (bitwise)
statement: x \bits y iff every binary 1-digit of x is a 1-digit of y.
why: Known.

name: single-fold binary containment (prop:subset)
statement: x \bits y has a single-fold representation: B=2^{y+1}, H=B^x, N=(B+1)^y, N = sBH + dH + r with d<B, r<H, d = 2t+1 (digit = binom(y,x), odd iff x \bits y by Lucas mod 2).
why: Known construction re-checked for uniqueness.

name: counter machine model (INC / TESTDEC, single halt state)
statement: Deterministic machine with finitely many states and counters, instructions INC(j) and TESTDEC(j), and a unique halt state with no instruction.
why: Minsky machines.

name: counter-machine universality for tuple inputs (lem:counter-universality)
statement: For every r.e. S subset N^n there is a counter machine that, with the first n counters initialised to a, halts iff a in S (simulation of a Turing machine by two base-D stacks).
why: Classical.

name: bound constant C and arc set
statement: C = 1 + s + sum d_j; counters at time t are below C+t; arcs labelled +j, 0j, -j with destinations.
why: Routine.

name: run encoding system (state, branch and counter masks)
statement: B=2^w=4b, J=B^{k-1}, M=sum B^t; I_q \bits M with sum_q I_q = M; Z_q+N_q=I_q, Z_q+V_q=M; I_q = 1_{q=q*} + B sum E_a; R_j \bits (2b-1)M (top bit reserved), R_j = rho_j J + eta_j, R_j = d_j + B(R_j - rho_j J + sum E^+ - sum E^-); zero test R_j \bits (B-1)V_q.
why: Known method; the exact-halt identity I_h = J (derived from summing state equations), final-digit removal and top-bit reservation are small single-fold-specific modifications.

name: clock register and dyadic scale window
statement: R_0 = C + B(R_0 - rho_0 J + M - J) forces rho_0 = C + k - 1; b <= rho_0 and 2 rho_0 < B force 2(C+T) < B <= 4(C+T), which contains exactly one power of two, so the base is a function of the run.
why: Named precedent (Chaitin 1987); the dyadic window is a clean but small device.

name: machine compiler (prop:machine-compiler)
statement: For a fixed deterministic counter machine with input initialisation, a finite polynomial system in a and natural auxiliaries has exactly one complete solution when the machine halts and none otherwise.
why: Single-fold variant of the Jones-Matiyasevich register-machine proof.

name: no-carry coefficient argument
statement: If sum_{t<k} c_t B^t = 0 with |c_t| < B then all c_t = 0; used to read off counter updates without carries or borrows.
why: Folklore.

name: unique power of two in (2L,4L]
statement: For L>0 the interval (2L,4L] contains exactly one power of two.
why: Elementary.

name: Main theorem (thm:main)
statement: Every r.e. S subset N^n (n>=1) has P in Z[A_1..A_n, W_1..W_m] (m>=1) with #{w : P(a,w)=0} = 1 if a in S and 0 otherwise.
why: Headline result, not an item to grade.

name: undecidability under an at-most-one-solution promise (cor:unique-h10)
statement: There exist m, D such that no algorithm decides solvability over N of degree-<=D polynomials in m variables promised to have at most one solution.
why: Immediate reduction from a nonrecursive r.e. set.

name: 2-isogeny descent: phi, psi, squareclass homomorphism alpha, ker alpha = psi E'(Q), index bound
statement: Standard descent via 2-isogeny; [E(Q):2E(Q)] <= |im alpha| |im alpha'|.
why: Textbook descent.

name: image computations; [2] not in im alpha' (mod 5)
statement: im alpha subset {+-1,+-5}; im alpha' subset {1,2,5,10} and omits [2] by a mod-5 descent on N^2 = 2m^4 + 50e^4; hence index <= 8.
why: Standard.

name: nontorsion point (-4,6); torsion via Nagell-Lutz
statement: [E(Q):2E(Q)] = 2^{r+2}, so r <= 1; (-4,6) is nontorsion by Nagell-Lutz (36 does not divide 62500); affine torsion has y=0.
why: Standard.

name: complete witness ledger
statement: Explicit recursive specification of every auxiliary coordinate (rational codes, addition tuples, height tuples, growth tuple xi, power tuple, containment tuple, computation tuple); counts s+3tau+r+1 containment calls and r+5 slacks.
why: Bookkeeping.

name: Semi: R and not-R both single-fold
statement: Semi R := SF R and SF (not R); closed under and/or/not/all; used to build guarded case splits whose guards and negated guards are both single-fold.
why: Abbreviation; the paper's disjoint-cases lemma is implemented via complements instead of explicit selectors.

name: rational / point / scalar functional compiler
statement: FractionPoly and Expr compile rational expressions to integer polynomial (in)equalities on rational codes; MapSF/PointSF/ScalarSF express single-fold graphs of maps to tuples, points and scalars, with comp/pair/pullback.
why: Plumbing.

name: Tate-limit canonical height from Mathlib Weil heights
statement: Generic: if h(P+Q)+h(P-Q) = 2h(P)+2h(Q)+O(1), the limit 4^{-n}h(2^n P) exists, is within C/3 of h, satisfies the parallelogram law and is quadratic; instantiated with h = logHeight of xRep using Mathlib's addSubMap height bound and a symmetric-height bound proved here.
why: Transfer (formalized).

name: Mordell-Weil for E via height descent
statement: HeightDescent.finitely_generated: a Northcott, nonnegative quadratic height plus finite index of 2A gives finite generation; instance AddGroup.FG E.Point from the 8-element cover of E(Q)/2E(Q).
why: Classical (the paper cites Silverman VIII 4.1).

name: full 2-descent via the Kummer map
statement: alpha_e(P) = class of x - e (adjusted at x=e) for e in {0,5}; kummer = alpha_0 x alpha_5; kummer P = 0 iff P in 2E(Q) (explicit halving formula); local mod-5 obstructions give mod_two_cover with G=(25/4,75/8) and torsion representatives.
why: Classical.

name: duplication height growth and small-point enumeration
statement: height(x)^4 <= 6250000 * height(dupX x); bounded_points enumerates 19*20*13 = 4,940 candidate x with height < 185 by `decide +kernel`, finding only x in {0,+-5,-4,45,25/4,-5/9}; hence H strictly increases under doubling for y != 0, so torsion = E[2].
why: Routine; the only kernel-level finite enumeration in the family.

name: abstract rank-one structure
statement: index formula [A:2A] = 2^n |A[2]| for A = Z^n x T; exists_rank_le_one; 2-adic valuation of x drops by 2 under doubling (vx_double, vx_dyadic) so G is nontorsion; rank_one gives E(Q) = Z x T.
why: Standard.

name: macro machine and TM2 simulation
statement: Macro instructions (div by radix 2 or 5, muladd) compiled to counter programs; Mathlib's PartrecToTM2 stacks encoded base 5; finite-state restriction of the label set.
why: Classical.

name: packed base-B digit library
statement: digit, pack, ones, bits_mask, digit_sum, division_last, update_coefficients/update_identity.
why: Plumbing.

name: Elliptic-height square window producing a single-fold growth function
why: Supplies exactly the object the 1974 problem lacked: a Diophantine relation of super-polynomial, sub-u^u growth whose graph is single-fold. Pell/Fibonacci relations fail because their solution sets are periodic in the index. Key idea is tiny and non-obvious: because log W_j is quadratic in the hidden index with bounded error, a fixed product of heights at Q, 2Q, R, R+-P, P tests the quadratic relation r = k^2 exactly ((2k)^2 - 2k^2 - ((r+1)^2 - r^2) + 1 = 2(k^2 - r)). With linear log-growth (Pe…

name: Square-window lemma as a standalone device (second difference of quadratic heights)
why: Formalized as a self-contained lemma (HeightWindow.square_window) with clean hypotheses: any integer sequence with log W_j = a j^2 + O(c) and log kappa between 6c and 2a-6c admits the exact test. Reusable beyond this curve: any quadratically growing Diophantine sequence would do.

name: Self-referential Pell scale u = (c+1)^l (n+1)(b+1) + u_0 with cutoff g(u)
why: Removes the free large parameter of classical exponentiation definitions by letting the output bound its own error; the lower ratio bound c >= b^n makes this consistent. Uses the two growth bounds for two distinct jobs (upper: index pinning; lower: admitting the intended solution).

name: Clock register with dyadic scale window (and exact halt mask I_h = J)
why: Pins the encoding base as a function of the run (B in (2(C+T),4(C+T)]), which is exactly what the classical Jones-Matiyasevich encoding lacks for uniqueness. The halt identity B I_h = H derived by summing the state equations rules out padded records without extra variables.

name: Complete-witness discipline: shifted-inverse rational codes, zeroed inactive cases, canonical representatives
why: Necessary for uniqueness of every auxiliary coordinate; done carefully and verified in Lean.

name: Elliptic-height single-fold growth function (index bracket + square window on a rank-one curve)
statement: On E: y^2=x^3-25x with E(Q)=ZP+T, put W(Q)=H(x([m_*]Q)), so log W_j = a_E j^2 + O(c_E). On input u, the unique representative Q with W(Q) <= u+W_1 < max W(Q+-P) has index k ~ sqrt(log u); the unique representative R with kappa^-1 <= W(2Q)W(R)W_1 / (W(Q)^2 max W(R+-P)) <= kappa has index k^2. g(u)=W(R) has a single-fold graph and delta(log u)^2 < log g(u) < u log u.
why: No construction of a single-fold (or any) Julia-Robinson-type relation from archimedean height comparisons was found. It supplies the object missing since 1974 by a mechanism Pell cannot provide: a bounded multiplicative window tests only linear index relations when log-growth is linear, but tests k^2 = r when log-growth is quadratic. Downgrade pressure: the bridge was explicitly posed (Pheidas Q9, c. 2005), and Poonen 2002 (in L) already squares indices on rank-one curves p-adically. The eurek…

name: Square-window lemma as a standalone device
statement: If log W_j = a j^2 + O(c) for j >= 1 and 6c < log kappa < 2a - 6c, then for k,r >= 1: kappa^-1 <= W_{2k}W_rW_1/(W_k^2 W_{r+1}) <= kappa iff r = k^2.
why: Given a quadratic sequence with bounded error, finding a bounded-window test for r=k^2 is an elementary exercise. Its value lies in C1's decision to have such a sequence in a single-fold system.

name: Single-fold power from a quasi-polynomial growth function (self-referential Pell scale u = (c+1)^l (n+1)(b+1) + u_0 with cutoff g(u))
statement: If g has a complete single-fold graph and delta(log u)^2 < log g(u) < u log u eventually, then Pow(b,n,c) <=> b>=2 & c=b^n is single-fold, via the paired Pell system with u = (c+1)^l (n+1)(b+1)+u_0, l > 3/(delta log 2), cutoff F,H < g(u), residues n+1 and quotient c = F div H.
why: A close variant of Matiyasevich's univocal Thm 5. It matters because it lowers the target from the exponential growth the literature expected (CCO Sec. 7, (++)) to quasi-polynomial Julia-Robinson growth, which is what makes C1's elliptic growth enough. If an easy Pell-only quasi-polynomial single-fold function exists, then this lowering, not C1, is the real key step; see open questions.

name: Single-fold machine compiler: clock register, dyadic base window, exact-halt identity
statement: A Minsky run is encoded in base B=2^w; a clock register forces B in (2(C+T),4(C+T)], which contains exactly one power of two, and summing state equations gives B*I_h = H (halt exactly at the last step), so each halting input has exactly one complete witness.
why: Named precedents (Chaitin; Jones-Matiyasevich), and the reduction it serves is mati1974's theorem. Borderline N1.

name: Complete-witness discipline: shifted-inverse rational codes, zeroed inactive cases, representatives, Semi
statement: Every auxiliary (slacks, selectors, reduced numerators/denominators, inactive-branch variables) is forced to a unique value.
why: Careful bookkeeping; necessary but routine.

name: Rank one and torsion of y^2 = x^3 - 25x (2-isogeny descent / Lean full 2-descent, Nagell-Lutz or duplication-height enumeration)
statement: E(Q) = ZP + E[2] with P nontorsion (congruent-number curve for n=5).
why: Cross-field transfer; the choice of curve is arbitrary among rank-one curves.

name: Neron-Tate quadraticity and uniform comparison log H(x(Q)) = 2h^(Q) + O(1)
why: Transfer of a textbook theorem.

name: Single-fold binary containment via Lucas's theorem mod 2
statement: x is bitwise contained in y iff binom(y,x) is odd, read as a digit of (B+1)^y in base B = 2^(y+1).
why: Known construction re-checked for uniqueness.

name: Thompson's group F
statement: Increasing PL homeomorphisms of [0,1], finitely many pieces, dyadic breakpoints, slopes in 2^Z; multiplication hg = h∘g; discrete group.
why: Textbook definition (CFP 1996).

name: amenable / invariant mean
statement: G amenable iff there is a positive normalized left-invariant mean M on ℓ∞(G;ℝ): M(1)=1, M≥0 on φ≥0, M(φ(h·))=M(φ).
why: Classical definition.

name: Følner criterion, amenable ⇒ Følner sets
statement: If G is amenable then for every finite S and ε>0 there is nonempty finite A with |hA△A|/|A|<ε for all h∈S.
cited_or_new: cited, not re-proved in paper; RE-PROVED in Lean
why: Følner 1955 / Namioka. Lean re-proves it by Hahn–Banach separation (Day's trick) plus a finite coarea/layer-cake argument (Namioka).

name: Thm main: F is not amenable
statement: Thompson's group F is not amenable.
why: Headline theorem, not an item to grade.

name: Lemma displacement (Benyamini–Sternfeld)
statement: There are a real Hilbert space H, a Lipschitz f:B→B on its closed unit ball and δ>0 with ‖f(x)−x‖≥δ for all x∈B.
why: Known theorem (1983), imported from nonlinear functional analysis: cross-field TRANSFER.

name: basic dyadic interval
why: Standard.

name: basic partition; mesh
statement: Finite partition of [0,1] into basic dyadic intervals (cells may share endpoints); mesh = largest cell length.
why: Standard (finite binary trees).

name: T respects I
statement: I is a union of cells of T.
why: Tree-node membership renamed.

name: affine chart s_I and product I·J
statement: s_I:[0,1]→I increasing affine; I·J = s_I(J); s_{I·J}=s_I∘s_J.
why: Standard dyadic address concatenation.

name: normalized restriction T_I
statement: T_I = {s_I^{-1}(K) : K∈T, K⊆I}, defined when T respects I.
why: Subtree of a binary tree at a node.

name: restriction composition (dyad:restriction)
statement: If T respects I and I·J then T_I respects J and (T_I)_J = T_{I·J}.
cited_or_new: new statement of a standard fact
why: Trivial tree fact.

name: uniform partition T^(n) and image partition gT^(n)
statement: T^(n) = uniform depth-n partition; gT^(n) = images of its cells under g.
why: Standard tree-pair / forest encoding.

name: Lemma dyad:eventual
statement: For each g∈F, gT^(n) is basic for large n, with mesh→0; for finite K⊂F and finite family J of basic intervals there is n0 with gT^(n) basic and respecting every member of J for g∈K, n≥n0.
why: Standard (CFP Lemma 2.2).

name: I<J (strict separation), internal interval
statement: I<J iff max I < min J (positive gap); internal iff both endpoints in (0,1).
why: Abbreviations.

name: Lemma dyad:transport (affine pair transport)
statement: If I<J and I'<J' are pairs of internal basic intervals, some h∈F carries I affinely onto I' and J affinely onto J'.
why: Standard folklore for F (transitivity on ordered dyadic tuples with affine control).

name: exact covariance (dyad:covariance)
statement: If h carries I affinely onto I', and gT^(n), (hg)T^(n) are basic and respect I, I' respectively, then ((hg)T^(n))_{I'} = (gT^(n))_I.
why: One-line consequence of the definitions; the choice to look at it is part of candidate EC1/EC3.

name: Lipschitz/displacement constants L, δ and branching D > 4L²/δ²
statement: Fix f, L, δ as in Lemma displacement; choose integer D≥2 with D > 4L²/δ².
why: Parameter bookkeeping.

name: parent intervals I_1<...<I_D
statement: Internal basic intervals I_j = [(2j-1)2^{-r}, 2j 2^{-r}] with 2^r>2D (Lean: depth 2D, index 2i+1).
why: Trivial choice.

name: recursive coloring p(T) (color:recursion)
statement: p(T) = f( (1/D) Σ_j p(T_{I_j}) ) if T respects every I_j, else 0; well founded on the number of cells; p(T)∈B.
why: Provisional: no near-equivalent found (Moore's Ramsey characterisation uses finite scalar colorings of trees, not recursively defined Hilbert-ball colorings; Akhmedov uses a height function; Day/Følner fixed-point theorems are for affine actions on compact convex sets). Syntactically tiny, like Cook's extension variables.

name: p(T^(r)) = f(0), p(T^(2r)) = f(f(0))
statement: Uniform partitions get iterated values of f.
why: Illustrative computation.

name: interval family 𝓘 (parents and descendants)
statement: 𝓘 = {I_i} ∪ {I_i·I_j}: D parents and D² descendants, all internal.
why: Finite bookkeeping set.

name: admissible (n,g)
statement: gT^(n) is a basic partition respecting every member of 𝓘.
why: Conjunction of L-notions.

name: global colors X_I^(n)(g) with zero extension (color:global)
statement: X_I^(n)(g) = p((gT^(n))_I) if (n,g) admissible, else 0; B-valued functions on all of F.
why: Pullback along Moore's tree-pair encoding; new only through I19.

name: scalar correlations φ_{I,J}^(n)
why: Inner products of I23.

name: fixed transport set S = {h_{I,J}}
statement: For each ordered separated pair I<J in 𝓘 choose h_{I,J}∈F carrying I,J affinely onto I_1,I_2; S is fixed before the test set A.
why: Instances of a standard transitivity lemma; the order-of-quantifiers design is a modest new device.

name: finite translation inequality (eq:finite-translation)
why: Standard.

name: Prop avg:boundary (uniform boundary bound)
statement: For every nonempty finite A⊂F, max_{h∈S} |hA△A|/|A| ≥ (δ²/L² − 4/D)/(4(1−1/D)) > 0.
why: Statement = 'Følner condition fails for S', an L-notion. Novelty sits in the proof.

name: correlation comparison / pair exchangeability (avg:correlation)
statement: For all strictly separated I,J∈𝓘: |E_A⟨X_I,X_J⟩ − α| ≤ η where α=E_A φ_{I_1,I_2}, η = max_{h∈S}|hA△A|/|A|.
why: Follows mechanically from I16+I26 once I23 exists; idea of approximate pair-invariance is classical (exchangeability).

name: parent mean m(g) and child means z_i(g)
statement: m = (1/D)Σ_k X_{I_k}; z_i = (1/D)Σ_j X_{I_i·I_j}.
why: Averages.

name: exact recursive identity X_{I_i}=f(z_i) (avg:recursive-identity)
statement: For admissible g, X_{I_i}(g) = f(z_i(g)).
why: Direct unfolding of I19; inherits its novelty.

name: displacement–energy inequality (avg:displacement)
statement: δ² ≤ ‖m−f(m)‖² = ‖(1/D)Σ(f(z_i)−f(m))‖² ≤ (L²/D) Σ‖z_i−m‖²; uses m = mean of f(z_i).
why: Elementary estimate; the observation 'm is itself the mean of f(z_i), so f(m)≈m if z_i≈m' is the hinge of the argument.

name: parent and child energy bounds (avg:parent-bound, avg:child-bound)
statement: E_A‖m‖² ≤ (1−1/D)(α+η)+1/D and the same for z_i.
why: Expansion of squared norm.

name: mixed-term bound; nested pairs are a 1/D fraction (avg:mixed-bound, Fig. mixed-pairs)
statement: E_A⟨z_i,m⟩ ≥ (1−1/D)(α−η) − 1/D: only column k=i pairs a descendant with its own parent.
why: Counting argument; mild new device (nested pairs are negligible).

name: variance estimate (avg:variance)
statement: E_A‖z_i−m‖² ≤ 4/D + 4(1−1/D)η; α cancels, no sign assumption.
why: Nearest neighbour: finite exchangeability / de Finetti (Diaconis–Freedman) style 'equal pair correlations force concentration of means'.

name: proof of Thm main
statement: Prop avg:boundary contradicts the Følner criterion.
why: Contrapositive of Følner.

name: Cor nonunitarizable (uniformly bounded non-unitarizable reps of F)
statement: For every ε>0, F has a uniformly bounded representation with sup‖π(g)‖≤1+ε that is not unitarizable.
why: Corollary via a cited (model-produced) theorem.

name: Cor percolation (p_c<p_{2→2}≤p_u, infinitely many clusters)
statement: For every finite symmetric generating set: ‖T_{p_c}‖_{2→2}<∞, p_c<p_{2→2}≤p_u, nonuniqueness phase.
why: Corollary via a cited (model-produced) theorem.

name: Prop aux:map (explicit Hilbert B–S map)
statement: On H=L²([0,1];ℝ²) there is a globally Lipschitz f:B→B with ‖f(x)‖=1 and ‖f(x)−x‖≥1/2.
why: Hilbert case of a 1983 theorem (and of Lin–Sternfeld 1985).

name: curve γ(t)=a(t)v(t) with v(t)(w)=(cos θ(t)w, sin θ(t)w); profiles a, θ
statement: Straight ray for t≤1, bounded oscillating tail in the 5/16-ball whose points stay uniformly separated (sinc inner products).
why: Variant of the classical Kakutani / Benyamini–Sternfeld curve-in-infinite-dimensions constructions.

name: Lemma aux:tube (unique nearest point, Lipschitz parameter)
statement: γ injective, ‖γ'‖≥1/8, uniform separation σ(d)>0, tube of radius ρ<1/32 with unique nearest point and |t(x)−t(y)|≤16‖x−y‖.
cited_or_new: new statement of standard tube facts
why: Standard differential-geometric estimates.

name: uniform separation σ(d) (aux:separation)
statement: inf_{|t−s|≥d}‖γ(t)−γ(s)‖>0 via sinc(q)<1.
why: Compactness/sinc estimate.

name: Lemma aux:rotation (R_t u(t)=v(t), Lipschitz in t)
statement: R = Id + A + A²/(1+κ), A h = v⟨u,h⟩ − u⟨v,h⟩.
why: Standard plane-rotation formula.

name: correction G and cutoffs β, χ (aux:G)
statement: G(x)=x+β(r)q(t)v(t)+χ(r)(R_t−Id)e on the tube, identity elsewhere; Lipschitz, ‖G‖≥ρ/4, G(x)=x for ‖x‖≥1/2.
why: Routine cut-off construction.

name: f(x) = −G(x)/‖G(x)‖
statement: Negative radial normalisation; ‖f(x)−x‖ ≥ 1/2.
why: Standard retraction-to-sphere trick.

name: comparator model: IntervalHomeomorph, IsDyadic, DyadicPLWitness, F, BoundedReal, leftPull, InvariantMean
statement: F = {f : [0,1]≃ₜ[0,1] // StrictMono f ∧ ∃ finite dyadic knots with slopes 2^e}; InvariantMean = positive, normalized, left-invariant ℝ-linear map on lp ∞.
why: Faithful formalisation (checked: textually identical to the comparator).

name: standardPLEquiv / intervalHomeomorph_standardPL_iff
statement: The model carrier equals the textbook finite-breakpoint dyadic PL condition (coverage derived).
why: Sanity equivalence.

name: Day/Hahn–Banach approximation by finite probabilities
statement: An invariant mean forces 0 into the closure of the ℓ¹ defect set of finite probabilities (geometric Hahn–Banach), giving finitely supported probabilities with total defect < ε.
why: Day's argument.

name: Namioka layer-cake/coarea: probability with small defect ⇒ Følner set
statement: Exact finite coarea identities for mass and translations; some superlevel set has small total boundary.
why: Namioka's trick.

name: exists_fixed_boundary (generic core)
statement: For ANY real inner product space E and Lipschitz f on its unit ball with displacement ≥δ, and D≥2 with D>4L²/δ², there is a fixed finite S⊂F with uniform boundary constant for every nonempty finite A.
why: Same content as I27.

name: Recursive Hilbert-ball coloring of dyadic partitions driven by a fixed-point-free Lipschitz map
why: A one-line definition that occurs nowhere in the goal or in L; with it the 50-year-open problem falls to ~2 pages of Hilbert-space algebra (the Cook–Reckhow profile: syntactically tiny, hard to find, huge budget drop). It converts approximate left-invariance of finite averages of SCALARS into an approximate fixed point of a NONLINEAR map on an infinite-dimensional ball, which classical fixed-point characterisations of amenability (Day: affine actions on compact convex sets) never do. It exploit…

name: Approximate pair-exchangeability ⇒ child means ≈ parent mean ⇒ approximate fixed point of f
why: The hinge observation that m is simultaneously the parent mean and the mean of f(z_i), so concentration of z_i near m forces m≈f(m). The Lean core theorem exists_fixed_boundary is generic over any Hilbert space and any displacement map: a reusable criterion.

name: Fixed transport set S chosen before A, single level n after A, exact covariance of normalized restrictions
why: Makes correlations comparable EXACTLY, so only the Følner defect enters; the quantifier order avoids any dependence of S on A.

name: Nested pairs occupy a 1/D fraction (only the own-parent column is uncontrolled)
why: Removes the need for any control on nested (ancestor–descendant) correlations, which the transports cannot compare.

name: Explicit Lipschitz displacement map on L²([0,1];ℝ²)
why: Self-contained, fully formalized; ~34% of the Lean DAG.

name: Recursive Hilbert-ball coloring of dyadic partitions driven by a fixed-point-free Lipschitz map
statement: Fix f: B->B Lipschitz with ||f(x)-x|| >= delta on the unit ball of an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space, and D separated internal dyadic intervals I_1<...<I_D. For a basic partition T, p(T) = f((1/D) sum_j p(T_{I_j})) if T respects every I_j, else 0 (well-founded on cell count). Pull back to F by X_I(g) = p((gT^(n))_I).
why: Survives Tests 1-3. It is not a templated induction strengthening, so the N2 cap does not apply. It is syntactically tiny and occurs nowhere in the goal or L. With it, a 47-year-old problem with at least six failed claims (Shavgulidze 2009, Akhmedov 2009/2013, Beklaryan 2011, Moore 2012, Wajnryb–Witowicz 2014) reduces to about two pages of Hilbert-space algebra. The recursion is forced once the strategy is fixed: the same f must act at every scale so that parent and child pair-correlations shar…

name: Pair-exchangeability => concentration of child and parent means => approximate fixed point of f
statement: If D-tuples x_k (parents) and y_{ij} (descendants) in B satisfy x_i = f(mean_j y_{ij}) and all separated-pair correlation averages are within eta of a common alpha, then delta^2 <= L^2 (4/D + 4(1-1/D) eta). Lean: FiniteBoundary.lean exists_fixed_boundary / boundaryConstant_le_of_correlations (generic over any real inner-product space).
why: Known L²/exchangeability computation applied to C1's objects. It belongs to the C1 cluster and is not separately eureka.

name: Fixed transport set S before A, single partition level after A, exact covariance of normalized restrictions
statement: For each separated pair I<J in the interval family choose h_{I,J} in F carrying I,J affinely onto I_1,I_2. Then ((hg)T^(n))_{h(I)} = (gT^(n))_I, so phi_{I,J}(g) = phi_{I_1,I_2}(h_{I,J} g) at any level n admissible for g and hg.
why: family.json's provisional N2 is lowered: the design is the standard Følner quantifier order plus standard tree-pair covariance, with nothing beyond L.

name: Nested pairs occupy a 1/D fraction (only the own-parent column is uncontrolled)
statement: In <z_i, m> = D^{-2} sum_{j,k} <X_{I_i·I_j}, X_{I_k}>, the D(D-1) terms with k≠i pair separated intervals; the remaining D terms (descendant vs own parent) are bounded by -1.
why: Lowered from provisional N2. The observation matters, but it is the textbook diagonal absorption once D is a free parameter.

name: Explicit Benyamini–Sternfeld map on L²([0,1];R²) with delta = 1/2 (appendix), and its use as the displacement input
statement: There is an L-Lipschitz f: B->B on the unit ball of L²([0,1];R²) with ||f(x)-x|| >= 1/2.
why: Cross-field transfer of a 1983 theorem. The explicit construction is at most N1. The NOVELTY OF USING it for amenability is recorded under bridge_novelty, not here.

name: Lean-only re-proof of the forward Følner criterion (Day separation + Namioka layer-cake)
statement: An invariant mean yields, for every finite S and eps, a finite A with |hA△A| < eps|A| for h in S.
why: Classical.

name: Main theorem
statement: Exists finite connected 2-dim aspherical simplicial K with linear combinatorial filling and pi_1 K with no geometric action on proper complete CAT(0) spaces; corollaries hyperbolicity, no locally CAT(0)/CAT(-1) finite models.
why: target, not graded

name: geometric action
statement: proper, cocompact action by isometries.
why: Standard (BH).

name: Incidence template Gamma (doubled Fano incidence graph with omitted edge Y_D-CD)
statement: Bipartite graph with vertices X_i for the 7 points of PG(2,F2), extra Y_i for i in {A=e1,B=e2,C=e3,D=e1+e2+e3} (no three collinear), and the 7 lines; both representatives joined to each incident line except the edge Y_D-CD is omitted. 18 vertices, 32 edges, cycle rank 15.
why: Tiny finite gadget, not a subterm of the goal or L, whose specific shape (which points doubled, which incidence omitted) is tuned so that (a) all fans stay connected with cycle-rank budget compatible with hyperbolicity and (b) the limiting metric configuration is contradictory. Cook-like profile. Risk: once one decides to use a near-critical random model with a finite template, searching small templates for a metric contradiction may be routine (could be N2).

name: loose edge e_0 = X_D-CD
statement: The incidence edge at D whose Y-counterpart is omitted; it belongs to no fan.
why: Part of P03; credited there.

name: fan F_i
statement: Edges over point i other than the loose edge; K_{2,3} at A,B,C, K_{2,2} at D, 3-star elsewhere; k_i=(6,6,6,4,3,3,3), sum 31.
why: A partition of P03's edges; the idea it serves is in P08.

name: field, assignment
statement: A field is an edge position in a template or polygon word; an assignment gives a signed letter to each field.
why: Bookkeeping.

name: core hexagon
statement: Six-cycle from three noncollinear points, their joining lines, one representative per point with all six incidences present; any three successive edges contain at most two fields of each fan.
why: Standard 6-cycles of the incidence graph, restricted by representative choice.

name: Nested independent Bernoulli tables (fans, top marks, 90 square decorations, six-letter table)
statement: Alphabet S_n of N=2n signed letters; parameters f=2-α, p=3-β, 0<α,δ<1, 7α<β<1. (i) fan tuples included w.p. N^{f-k_i}; (ii) full core tuples marked w.p. N^{p-gf-1}, a top occurrence = marked tuple all of whose 7 fan restrictions are included; (iii) for each of 90 two-edge core paths a 4-field square table w.p. N^{-2-δ}; (iv) a six-letter table w.p. N^{-3-δ}. Expected counts N^{2-α}, N^{3-β}, N^{2-δ}, N^{3-δ}.
cited_or_new: new (model); components are variants of known random models
why: The idea of operating at near-critical density (just below the 1/2 collapse threshold) so that hyperbolicity survives while metric constraints become exact in the limit, combined with nested occurrences whose shared costs are counted once, is the conceptual core. Neighbours: square/hexagonal models (Odrzygozdz), Gromov graphical random groups. Could drop to N2 if a neighbour with nested tables exists.

name: fan occurrence, top occurrence (a->b), decorations
statement: Included fan tuple with its type; marked core tuple whose fan restrictions are included; included square/six rows.
why: Names for P08's parts.

name: Two-complex P: letter bouquet + cones on fans, cone on the subdivided Fano macro graph B for each top, decoration polygons
statement: Cones on labelled graphs instead of one 2-cell per relator; B = Fano incidence graph with D-CD subdivided (15 vertices, 22 edges, cycle rank 8 = 15-7).
why: Standard cone-off device adapted to the two-level occurrence structure.

name: Presentation equivalence + C2 quotient
statement: pi_1 P equals the letter presentation group; it maps onto C_2 (all relators have even length).
why: Routine van Kampen.

name: Occurrences, not words
statement: A fan shared by several tops is coned once; each top and decoration has its own cell.
why: Remark.

name: Master pattern M and matches
kind: definition (inline \emph) master pattern M; match; Omega_n
statement: M = one top with its 7 fans + one square row for each of 90 two-edge paths (212 fields, 98 entries); a match is an assignment with all required entries present; Omega_n the random set of matches with uniform law mu_N; E|Omega_n| = N^{3-β-90δ}.
why: Pattern-count object, new for this model, standard in random-graph theory.

name: Admissible field sets
statement: Either <=3 distinct core fields with <=2 from each fan (loose field exempt), or <=2 fields of one square decoration.
why: Tailored definition; content is a computation of where the critical exponent stays positive.

name: occurrence, field positions, unsigned coincidence rank R
statement: R = #positions - #distinct underlying generators; fan fields counted once even if the fan sits in several tops.
why: Ollivier's decorated abstract diagrams / AFL constraint counting, adapted with shared fans.

name: Coincidence-rank bound R <= (p-7f)s + fu + sum(h_e - δ)
statement: W.h.p., simultaneously for all collections of <= M distinct occurrences containing all fan slots of their tops.
why: Standard first-moment argument with the new shared-fan exponent.

name: Elementary (spherical/disk) pictures; existence with exact lifted chain
statement: Pictures with side pairings; every null word has a disk picture; every nonzero 2-cycle of the universal cover is the chain of a finite collection of spherical pictures (via Hurewicz, general position).
why: Standard.

name: top polygon, ports
statement: Grouping cone triangles at a top-apex instance into a polygon tracing a macro walk; ports = radial labels of a fan (exceptional port X_D at D).
why: Bookkeeping.

name: Normal pictures: simple macro cycles, no same-side adjacency, fan-apex links without repeated radial labels
statement: Lexicographic minimal pictures satisfy the three properties; the radial-label switch preserves genus zero and the lifted chain.
why: Standard reduction moves adapted to cones.

name: fragment, partial instance, multiplicities r_b, m_b, S_b and fan weight w_b = max{r_b, m_b}
statement: Fragments are arbitrary face selections; fan weight dominates both the represented-apex count and the largest multiplicity of a top using the fan.
why: Multiplicity weighting is a known technique; the specific domination rule for shared prerequisites is a tuned variant. Candidate for 'shared-cost-once' idea (see P21).

name: Weighted contact bound I <= pT + f·sum_b(w_b - S_b) + sum_e (h_e - δ) t_e
statement: Layer-cake: apply the rank bound to positions of weight >= j for each j and sum; charge each internal contact to a non-maximal endpoint in its value class.
why: Named precedents; adaptation to shared fan prerequisites.

name: Local apex inequality with dominant top + partial-link bound 2 sum J_b <= B_rad
statement: sum_z d_z + 2(w_b - S_b) <= (sum q_z + P*_b)/2 + 2 J_b; dominant/nondominant turn counting in cyclic links; loose-side payments at the exceptional port.
why: Local combinatorial estimate specific to the template; standard genre.

name: Fragment isoperimetry A <= B/κ, κ = min{β-7α, α/5, δ}
statement: Every fragment of area A has boundary B >= κA when the rank bound holds for <= 8A occurrences.
why: Assembly of P21+P22; the margins β-7α, α, δ are the deficits of the model.

name: Bounded-piece partition of planar bounded-degree multigraphs
statement: Recursive Lipton-Tarjan separators: parts of size <= K(D,η) cutting <= η·#vertices edges.
why: Standard corollary of Lipton-Tarjan.

name: Linear filling and asphericity w.h.p.
statement: For fixed small α,β,δ with β>7α, w.h.p. P is aspherical and the letter presentation has a linear isoperimetric inequality (area <= 60 C_0 ℓ).
why: Assembly; local-to-global via separators is standard.

name: Conditional test (I, e, t)
statement: I subset of fields, e outside I, I∪{e} admissible, t a positive integer (number of coupled branches).
why: Tailored definition.

name: Critical exponent h(W) = |W| - sum_{E_rho ⊆ W} c_rho; budget h(W) >= min{2,|W|}, h(W) >= |S| for admissible S ⊆ W

name: Closure U: inclusion-maximal U ⊇ I with h(U)=|I|; gap h(U∪V)-h(U) >= 1

name: Stars: t copies of M glued along U, injective in each field; overlap types; variance rule C_t N^{-q+C}

why: Variant of standard extension counting.

name: Concentration of extension counts A_sigma and leaf counts B_b
statement: Means a_N, b_N independent of sigma/b; relative variances o(1) uniformly.
why: Variant.

name: Star coupling: law on t matches agreeing on I, each branch ~ mu_N in TV, leaves ~ iid uniform letters in TV

why: Technique is standard probabilistic combinatorics; its role is credited to P43.

name: Six-letter pair counts uniformly ~ N^{1-δ}
statement: For all positions r<q and letters u,v, Q_rq(u,v)/N^{1-δ} -> 1 uniformly w.h.p.

name: Sampling proposition (finite families of tests)
statement: For any finite family of tests and small parameters: |Omega_n| ~ N^{3-β-90δ}, single-field marginals uniform, all couplings exist, six-letter counts uniform.

name: Energy minimizing basepoint with zero tangent barycenter and variance inequality
statement: For a geometric action of an infinite f.g. group on a proper complete CAT(0) space, E(x)=avg d(x,sx)^2 attains a positive minimum; sum <h,v_s> <= 0.

name: Uniform displacement bound max_s ||v_s||^2 <= 25(1+ε)/(1-ε) from the six-letter table

name: Concavity of <h,·> in CAT(0) cones; inductive mean E||m_t||^2 <= 1/t
statement: Sturm's inductive mean bound (unit variance) and Gigli-Nobili concavity, re-proved.
why: Cited results.

name: Uniform conditional test: limsup_nu E_mu <h_I, v_{sigma(e)}> <= 0 for bounded h_I depending only on labels in I
statement: Couple t matches agreeing on I; average ⟨h_I, v_{e_j}⟩ <= ⟨h_I, m_t⟩ <= B||m_t||; leaves near iid uniform so E||m_t||^2 <= 1/t + error; let ν->∞ then t->∞. Uniform over actions chosen after the tables.

Risk: an expert in Sturm/IKN might regard it as a natural combination (N2).

name: Limiting configuration: L2-product of orbit realizations over Omega_nu, pointed ultralimit
kind: construction (Gamma-hat, product over matches, ultralimit Z)
statement: Orbit realizations of the core graph + square closing paths, product metric averaged over matches, nonprincipal ultralimit; complete CAT(0) (BH I.5.53, II.3.10).
why: Standard construction applied to the matches.

name: Edges length 1; admissible k-paths have squared endpoint distance >= k
statement: Via log comparison and the uniform conditional test at each step.
why: Direct application of P37.

name: CAT(0) quadrilateral inequality d13^2 + d24^2 + 4 d(m,n)^2 <= sum of side squares
statement: Midpoint convexity.
why: Known inequality (re-derived).

statement: For admissible I∪{e} and any h_I with values in T_{x_ν}X_ν depending only on the labels on I, ||h_I|| <= B: limsup_ν E_{μ_ν} <h_I, v_{σ(e)}> <= 0, uniformly over actions chosen after the tables. Proof: couple t matches agreeing on I with near-iid uniform e-leaves; concavity gives avg <h_I, v_{e_j}> <= <h_I, m_t> <= B||m_t||; barycenter + Sturm give E||m_t||^2 <= 1/t + O(η); let ν->∞ then t->∞.

statement: Bernoulli tables over a growing alphabet of N letters: fan tuples at N^{f-k_i} (f=2-α), full core tuples marked at N^{p-gf-1} (p=3-β, top = marked tuple whose 7 fan restrictions are present), 90 four-letter tables at N^{-2-δ} closing every nonbacktracking two-edge core path, and an independent six-letter table at N^{-3-δ}. The decoration layer is a known model (square/hexagonal) in its known hyperbolic regime, and labelled-graph relations are Gromov's graph model; what is new is the nesting (fans then tops) with shared costs paid once, which is an engineering variant serving C3's template and C4's counting. No equivalent nested model found (searches above), so not N0/N1; but with named close neighbours it does not clear test 1 as a standalone concept. Its genuinely creative content…

In the limit every edge has length 1, every two-step path length sqrt2, every admissible three-step path >= sqrt3; hence each core hexagon is the 6-vertex skew hexagon of a unit cube about a common center c (adjacent directions at arccos(1/3), two-step at arccos(-1/3), opposite antipodal). Doubling forces fan identities M_i = x_i ⊕ y_i = h_H ⊕ h_H'; the omitted incidence plus the ternar…

Non-analytic, tiny, and its carriers are used by >40% of the DAG. F3: auxiliary finite gadget built only to drive the proof. Downgrade risk: chain depth 2 means it may be easy to find once C1/C2 are given (arm D o…

name: Shared-cost-once diagram counting with multiplicity weights w_b = max{r_b, m_b}
statement: Fan fields carry weight w_b dominating both represented-apex counts and the largest multiplicity of any top using the fan; layer-cake application of the distinct-occurrence rank bound to positions of weight >= j; local apex inequality with a dominant top; fragment isoperimetry A <= B/κ, κ = min{β-7α, α/5, δ}.
why: Paper names Ollivier 2004 and AFL 2017 as related precedents; the domination rule for shared prerequisites is a tuned variant, not a new concept.

name: Six-letter displacement bound
statement: An independent table of length-6 relators at density just below 1/2 has near-uniform pair counts; each row gives a^{-1} = s2...s6, so ||v_a||^2 <= 5 sum ||v_{s_k}||^2 and averaging over rows starting with a bounds every displacement by 25(1+ε)/(1-ε) times the normalized mean energy.
why: A short Cauchy-Schwarz once one decides to add a dense auxiliary table; the pair-coverage fact at density ~1/2 is standard. Could be argued N3-lite as an F3 auxiliary table built only for the proof, but its discovery cost appears low.

name: Critical-exponent closure U and star (extension) counts
statement: Inclusion-maximal U ⊇ I with h(U) = |I| so that every further extension raises the critical exponent by >= 1; t copies glued along U; second-moment concentration of extension and leaf counts; uniform law on stars is the coupling.
why: Transfer of Spencer-style extension counting (closure + second moment) from random graphs to random presentations; cross-field transfer is N0 by rule. Confidence limited because I did not verify the exact form of Spencer's closure statement online.

name: Stable exchange symbol E prod_i (x_i + y_pi(i))
statement: For any law of a permutation pi that is a limit of finite products of independent Bernoulli transpositions and deterministic permutations (incl. Poisson exchanges and uniform permutations of subsets), E prod_{i in V}(x_i + y_pi(i)) is stable.
why: It is exactly the Borcea-Branden algebraic symbol of the interchange/exclusion transition operator, and its stability is equivalent (BB Thm 1.1) to BBL's theorem that symmetric exclusion preserves stability, which is in L. The model writes it without citation in the trace; the paper calls it a 'symbol' and credits BBL Thm 4.20 for the proof step. Transfer, not invention.

name: Splicing to the cycle-weighted next-pin symbol (loop weight 2 for free)
statement: Layer the exchange picture at the pin times; eliminate each non-pin vertex q by x_q = y_q = t and taking the coefficient of t. The result is the stable polynomial F_P = E_b[2^{n_P(pi)} prod_{i in P}(x_i + y_sigma(i))], sigma the next-pin permutation and n_P the number of pin-free cycles. Hence the output set sigma(T) has a stable generating polynomial under the Heisenberg (theta=2) cycle-weighted pin law P_P.
why: The only item with no neighbour found. It is the bridge that carries BBL negative dependence from theta=1 to the theta=2 Heisenberg loop weight: the splice composes known closure operations, but noting that it splices cycles and charges each closed loop exactly 2 is not in any source found. Against: every ingredient is N0 (BB symbol = C1, closure operations, BBL presence bound). The mechanism (contraction = trace, giving loop weight 2) is classical in Asano/Suzuki-Fisher Lee-Yang theory for thi…

name: Simultaneous pin test P_E(T in B_E) <= (2r)^|T|
statement: {T in B_E} = {sigma(T)=T}; m r = E_P|T cap sigma(T)|; presence product + AM-GM gives P_P(T subset sigma(T)) <= r^m; the weight comparison w_P <= w_E <= 2^m w_P transfers this to P_E with the factor 2^m; dense-boundary limit.
why: This is the consequence that makes C2 load-bearing. As in 287 (C2+C4), the N3 meaning attaches to the cluster C2+C3, but C3 alone is a short derivation from C2 plus BBL's presence bound.

name: Presence probabilities for stable subset laws
statement: If a random subset has a stable generating polynomial then P(J subset A) <= prod P(j in A), also conditionally.
why: BBL Thm 4.9, cited by the paper.

name: Exterior moments E[wedge^k Pi] = wedge^k E[Pi]
statement: For Bernoulli-transposition products and limits, all minors of the random permutation matrix have mean equal to the minors of the mean.
why: Constructed in the trace (PV2), but equivalent to DLM 2020's determinant-preserving property, which the paper cites. Retrieval after construction is still N0.

name: Conditional next-pin first moment (all-hit determinant + Schur complement)
statement: Conditioned on every cycle meeting J, the mean next-visit matrix equals the first-hitting kernel of a Markov chain with fresh independent steps.
why: A real generalization (arbitrary W, conditioning on G_J, exposure) of a known determinant route for interchange cycles. The precedents are named in the paper.

name: Downward induction over pin sets with sparse multi-point tests
statement: For all grid pin sets E containing D0, all sparse single-time tests T: P_E(T subset B_E) <= p^|T|, by induction on the number of missing grid pins.
why: A templated strengthening (all superset pin sets, multi-point) is capped at N2 by the PLAN rule. Bloch's law re-runs it with a quantitative rate.

name: Return-energy inequality, local Nash, routed flows around hulls, two-end leakage
statement: Reduce r <= eps(p)=o(p) to a quadratic loss bound for the one-period kernel, controlled by a local Nash inequality near regular anchors and finite-energy flows routed around obstacle hulls.
why: Heavy, careful engineering of known diffusive tools in a random repeated environment. Analytically the hardest part, but no new concept.

name: Spin-S slot loop representation, pin law, factorial domination
statement: Toth's random-stirring representation for spin S via 2S symmetric slots, with cycles forced up at pins (weight 1 instead of 2).
why: Known representation plus a natural conditioning (the pin law).

name: Surface cost -> vanishing-field selection -> KMS state
statement: Boundary colouring costs exp(O(|boundary|)); with the pin estimate this gives a macroscopic magnetization tail, selected by a field h_L -> 0, then translation averaging and KMS limits.
why: Griffiths' route. This is the negative control.

name: [Spherical companion] Disk symbol and zero-free layered traces
statement: Via a Cayley transform of C1, E prod(1 + x_i y_pi(i)) is zero-free on the open unit polydisk; cyclic products of admissible permutation layers and single-slot disk-contracting matrices have nonzero trace (contraction A+Bx+Cy+Dxy -> A+D), giving Z(z) != 0 for Re z > 0.
why: Reuses C1 in Lee-Yang form, which is a known route for this model. Interesting as evidence that C1/C2 have more than one use, but the use is in-family.

name: [Bloch companion] One-pin identity d_E(i)=r/(1+r) and the return route to the Bloch coefficient
statement: The down probability of an unpinned slot equals r/(1+r), r = one-pin return probability; returns are compared with an ideal magnon walk whose heat kernel gives kappa sum n^{-3/2} -> zeta(3/2)/(8 pi^{3/2} sqrt(det D)); long returns are controlled by a spread-source flow energy C(K beta)^{-1/2}.
why: A new and effective route to Bloch's coefficient that rests on the Sep 24 machinery. Its components are standard (weight identity, heat-kernel asymptotics, flows). Graded at low confidence because this analyst read only the intro and Sec. 2 closely.

name: [Spherical companion] Weak exponential estimate for zero-sum tests + replica / harmonic pressure-tangent selection
statement: log<exp(theta_R D_f)> <= C b_R V for zero-sum cell tests; replicas plus random zero-free functions select harmonic limits of log|Z|, excluding coexistence of ergodic states with different magnetization lengths; then J_L/V -> m gives the sinh(m|t|)/(m|t|) law.
why: Not analysed in depth. Graded N2 provisionally as a new combination of known principles in a new setting.

against: Griffiths 1966 field selection; standard KMS limit arguments; the paper names Griffiths.

name: normal map
statement: A linear map between vN algebras is normal if it is ultraweakly continuous.
why: Textbook definition.

name: free family of unital subalgebras
statement: Voiculescu freeness: alternating products of centered elements from different subalgebras have trace zero.
why: Voiculescu freeness.

name: freeness passes to vN closures and to groupings
statement: Freeness of *-algebras implies freeness of the generated vN algebras, and freeness is preserved under grouping components.
why: Standard free-probability facts.

name: freely generating Haar d-tuple
statement: Unitaries U_1..U_d generating M as a vN algebra, with tau(U_g)=0 for every nonidentity reduced word g in F_d.
cited_or_new: new name for a standard notion
why: A conjunction of standard concepts in L: free Haar distribution plus W*-generation.

name: Identification by a generating Haar tuple (lem:haar-identification)
statement: A freely generating Haar d-tuple U in M gives a trace-preserving normal *-isomorphism L(F_d)->M with lambda(x_j) mapped to U_j.
why: Standard: the trace on words determines the GNS representation.

name: L(F_d) is a II_1 factor
statement: ICC argument for d>=2.
why: Murray-von Neumann.

name: bounded Borel logarithm S=arg(C) and its conjugates S_g=A_g S A_g^*
statement: Take the Borel logarithm of the free Haar generator C, with values in (-pi,pi], so that S is self-adjoint, centered, ||S||<=pi and e^{iS}=C. Then conjugate S by the group words in A.
cited_or_new: functional calculus cited; use is new to this argument
why: The bounded log of a free Haar unitary, giving C^t=exp(itS), is exactly the ingredient of Popa's free malleable deformation (Ioana-Peterson-Popa 2008). The conjugate family is the free Bernoulli field of F_n.

name: Freeness of the conjugate components (lem:conjugates)
statement: The algebras A_g W*(C) A_g^*, g in F_n, are free. Hence each S_g is free from W*(S_b : b != g).
why: The standard free Bernoulli decomposition L(F_n)*L(Z) = (*_g W*(S_g)) x F_n.

name: group label of a monomial
statement: The product in F_n of the group letters of a monomial in A_j, A_j^*, S, ignoring S.
why: The F_n-grading of the crossed product. Plumbing.

name: Group labels and traces (lem:labels)
statement: A monomial with nonidentity label has trace 0. A monomial with identity label is a polynomial in the S_g.
why: The grading of the crossed product, plus the vanishing of the conditional expectation onto the group-algebra-free part.

name: free sum s(k)=sum_g k(g) S_g
statement: A real-linear, F_n-equivariant map from finitely supported real functions on F_n to self-adjoint elements of M, with A_g s(k) A_g^* = s(lambda(g)k).
why: The analog of the free Gaussian functor field X(xi), realized by the free Bernoulli field S_g instead of semicirculars. It repackages known concepts.

name: Norm of a free sum (lem:free-sum), K=3*pi
statement: ||s(k)|| <= 3 pi ||k||_2. More generally, ||sum z_j|| <= 2 (sum ||z_j||_2^2)^{1/2} + max ||z_j|| for free, centered, self-adjoint z_j.
why: The Ricard-Xu / Voiculescu free Khintchine inequality (Haagerup-type), applied to the scalar self-adjoint case.

name: coefficient cocycle D (Fox derivative form)
statement: Given real finitely supported h_j, the unique cocycle D: F_n -> R^(F_n) with D_{x_j}=h_j and D_{gb}=D_g+lambda(g)D_b.
why: A 1-cocycle into the left regular representation, i.e. the Fox derivative. Named by the paper.

name: formal algebra P, evaluation ev_0, derivation delta (delta z=0, delta a_j = i sigma(h_j) a_j)
statement: On the universal *-algebra of n unitaries and one self-adjoint z, the *-derivation driven by the conjugated-log fields sigma(h_j).
why: A close variant of Voiculescu's cyclomorphy setting: trace-preserving derivations on algebraically free generators. The specific field is the free analog of the Gaussian cocycle deformation derivation (Peterson; Sinclair).

name: word derivative = cocycle value: delta a_g = i sigma(D_g) a_g, delta z_g = i[sigma(D_g), z_g]
statement: Because a_g sigma(k) a_g^* = sigma(lambda(g)k), the derivation acts on every group word through the cocycle value D_g.
why: The noncommutative analog of alpha_t(u_g)=omega(t b(g)) u_g for Gaussian cocycle deformations (Sinclair 2011; Peterson-Sinclair 2012), which the paper does not cite.

name: Universal initial trace identity (lem:flow-trace-identity)
statement: tau(ev_0(delta^r p))=0 for all p in P and r>=1. Proved by label preservation, plus a first-variation argument: conjugating S_g by exp(iuY_g), with Y_g in W*(S_b : b != g), preserves the joint law by freeness.
cited_or_new: new proof of a cyclomorphy-type criterion
why: Its content (tau composed with delta is 0, so the flow is trace preserving) is the cyclomorphy criterion. The first-variation-by-free-conjugation proof is a neat variant.

name: conjugation by a unitary of B preserves freeness from B
statement: If A is free from B and U is a unitary in B, then UAU^* is free from B, and the joint law with B is unchanged.
why: Folklore.

name: polynomial vector field V_j(X)=i H_j(X) X_j, H_j(X)=sum_g h_j(g) X_g S X_g^*
statement: The ODE dA_j/dt = i s_t(h_j) A_j, where s_t uses the time-t conjugates of the fixed S.
why: With h_j=delta_e it reduces to Popa's free malleable deformation A_j -> C^t A_j. For general h_j it is a time-ordered (free) version of the Gaussian cocycle deformation. Close neighbours exist.

name: Global solvability in a generated subalgebra (lem:flow-global-ode)
statement: The polynomial ODE has a unique global smooth solution in any C*-subalgebra E containing S, and the solution stays unitary.
why: Picard-Lindelof in Banach spaces.

name: Moment invariance (lem:flow-moments)
statement: tau(ev_t(p)) = tau(ev_0(p)) for all t, by a uniform factorial bound on iterated derivatives, real analyticity, and I16.
why: Standard analytic-continuation step in cyclomorphy-type exponentiation.

name: operator norm from moments
statement: ||b|| = lim tau((b^*b)^k)^{1/2k} in a faithful tracial vN algebra. So moment preservation gives an isometry.
why: Folklore.

name: Polynomial flow and displacement bounds (prop:flow)
statement: There is a one-parameter group beta_t of trace-preserving normal automorphisms of M fixing S, with ||beta_t(A_j)-A_j|| <= |t| K ||h_j||_2 and ||beta_t(A_w) - e^{itS} A_w|| <= |t| K ||D_w - delta_e||_2.
why: The leaning is N3. Its parts have close precedents: cyclomorphy (named), Popa's free malleable deformation and Sinclair / Peterson-Sinclair Gaussian cocycle deformations (not named). What appears new is the word-displacement bound in operator norm, inside M itself, with no ambient dilation.

name: Small coefficients with a prescribed word value (lem:small-cocycle)
statement: For n>=3 and eta>0 there are a word w and a finitely supported real h with h_1=h, h_j=0 for j>=2, ||h||_2<eta and ||D_w - delta_e||_2 < eta.
why: Weak N3. Posing the problem (generator values small in ell^2 while one word value approximates delta_e) is non-analytic and seems new. Once posed, the solution is textbook free probability: circular law and spectral cutoff. So the pivot is one step from L, and a judge may grade it N2.

name: free prefix words a=x_1, b_j=x_2^j x_3 x_2^{-j}, p_j=(a b_1)...(a b_j), w_m=p_m a, T_m=1+sum lambda(p_j)
statement: A word whose Fox derivative in x_1 is a sum of m+1 group elements that are free, apart from the identity term.
why: Routine engineering of free subgroups and Nielsen moves. The trick that D vanishes on the b_j (h_j=0 for j>=2) is small.

name: Free prefixes and the cocycle value (lem:cocycle-prefixes)
statement: p_1..p_m freely generate a free subgroup, and D_{w_m} = T_m h.
why: Nielsen transformations plus the Fox chain rule.

name: Q_m = T_m T_m^*, mu_m = spectral law of Q_m/m
statement: Spectral measure of the normalized prefix-sum operator.
why: Abbreviation.

name: Spectral limit of the prefix sums (lem:cocycle-spectrum)
statement: mu_m converges weakly to the free Poisson (Marchenko-Pastur, rate 1) law, which has no atom at 0.
why: Free central limit theorem: (1/sqrt m) times a sum of free Haar unitaries tends to a circular element c, and cc^* is free Poisson.

name: spectral cutoff inverse E_m, R_m=f_m(Q_m), h^(0)=T_m^* R_m delta_e
statement: A truncated pseudo-inverse gives ||h^(0)||^2 = tau(R_m) <= 1/(dm) and ||T_m h^(0) - delta_e||^2 = mu_m([0,d]).
why: Spectral-cutoff (regularized) least-squares inverse.

name: reality of h^(0) and finite truncation
statement: Complex conjugation J commutes with real functions of Q_m, so h^(0) is real. Approximate it by a finitely supported real h.
why: Routine.

name: completion of A
statement: C is a completion of A=(A_1..A_n) if (A,C) is a freely generating Haar tuple.
why: A renaming.

name: Approximating the extra generator in one step (prop:perturbation)
statement: For every eps>0 there are a trace-preserving automorphism alpha and a word w with ||alpha(A_j)-A_j||<eps and ||alpha(A)_w - C||<eps. The new completion is C' = C A_w^*. The proof sets alpha = gamma^{-1} o beta_1, where gamma is the Nielsen automorphism C -> C A_w.
why: It looks non-analytic and new: a norm-small automorphism of L(F_{n+1}) that makes a long word in the first n generators approximate the (n+1)-st. It turns the known non-uniformity of free/cocycle deformations on long words, usually used for rigidity, into a constructive absorption device. The risk is the unverified shlyakhtenko2026 precedent.

name: Nielsen automorphism gamma: A_j -> A_j, C -> C A_w
statement: The basis change c -> cw of F_{n+1} induces a trace-preserving automorphism, via I05.
why: Aut(F_{n+1}) acts on L(F_{n+1}).

name: tuple distance d_2 and word-polynomial Lipschitz constant L(F)
statement: ||F(U)-F(V)||_2 <= L(F) d_2(U,V), by telescoping.
why: Abbreviation of a telescoping bound.

name: adaptive error-budget iteration (F_{j,k}, eps_k, alpha_k, w_k, G_{j,k}, L_k, r_k; dense sequence y_j)
statement: At each stage, approximate y_1..y_k in the current tuple, choose eps_k, perturb, substitute the witness word, and only then fix the future budget r_k.
cited_or_new: new instance of a standard scheme
why: A standard diagonal Cauchy-limit construction with tracked budgets. The paper describes shlyakhtenko2026 as using 'a limiting generation argument', so the template has a named precedent.

name: the limit tuple is free Haar and generates M
statement: Norm convergence preserves the word traces. L^2-density of the word algebra plus the conditional expectation give W*(A^(inf))=M.
why: Routine.

name: Isomorphism of consecutive ranks (thm:rank-step)
statement: L(F_n) is isomorphic to L(F_{n+1}) for n>=3.
why: Results are not graded as machinery.

name: only the first n generators need to converge
statement: The completions C^(k) may fail to converge; the targets are approximated in L^2.
why: Commentary.

name: amplification Q^t and induced map Theta^t
statement: The normalized corner p(Q (x) B(l^2))p with trace t. Tracial isomorphisms amplify.
why: Murray-von Neumann.

name: L(F_2) is isomorphic to L(F_3) (thm:main)
statement: Compose N_3=N_4=N_5 and amplify by sqrt 2. Dykema gives N_3^{sqrt2}=N_2 and N_5^{sqrt2}=N_3.
why: Checked arithmetic: 1+(3-1)/2=2 and 1+(5-1)/2=3.

name: fundamental group F(Q)
statement: F(Q) = {t>0 : Q^t is isomorphic to Q}.
why: Murray-von Neumann.

name: all interpolated free group factors are isomorphic; fundamental group R_{>0} (cor:all-interpolated)
statement: Combine Thm main with Radulescu's dichotomy (including infinity) and the amplification formula.
why: C5 transfer.

name: free entropy dimensions depend on W*-generators (cor:entropy-dimensions)
statement: Transport semicircular tuples (for delta, delta_0) and group tuples (for delta^*, delta^star) from L(F_n) into L(F_2). Then each of the four dimensions takes every value n>=2.
why: Transport by distribution-preserving isomorphisms. N1-level argument.

name: transported tuples X^(n)=theta_n(S^(n)), Y^(n)=theta_n(G^(n)); G^(n)=(Re u_j, Im u_j)
statement: Self-adjoint generating tuples with prescribed entropy dimensions.
why: Standard tuples.

name: One-step absorption of a free generator
statement: For a freely generating Haar (n+1)-tuple (A,C), n>=3, and every eps>0, there are a trace-preserving automorphism alpha and a word w in F_n with max_j ||alpha(A_j)-A_j|| < eps and ||alpha(A)_w - C|| < eps.
why: Its form is precedented in L by a model-assisted preprint and in ergodic theory, and it is close to analytic in the goal. Its non-trivial content is inherited from I22+I23. The provisional N3 in paper.json is withdrawn.

name: Small cocycle with a prescribed word value
statement: For n>=3 and eta>0 there are a word w in F_n and a finitely supported real h with ||h||_2 < eta such that the Fox cocycle D with D_{x_1}=h, D_{x_j}=0 (j>=2) satisfies ||D_w - delta_e||_2 < eta.
why: The only item with no neighbour found and no retrieval trigger in the trace. It is where non-amenability enters: it fails for Z (Dirichlet kernel) and for property (T) groups. The eureka content lies in posing the problem: small generator values, a word value near delta_e, coupled to absorption. Solving it is textbook once posed, and Lean found a second elementary proof.
