If Test 4 is decided at pivot level (prop:flow given), expect N2. The N3 claim really attaches to the cluster C2+C4.

name: Cocycle-driven polynomial flow
statement: dA_j/dt = i s_t(h_j) A_j with s_t(k) = sum_g k(g) A_g(t) S A_g(t)^*, which generates trace-preserving automorphisms beta_t fixing S, with ||beta_1(A_j)-A_j|| <= 3pi||h_j|| and ||beta_1(A_w) - C A_w|| <= 3pi||D_w - delta_e||.
why: A free/internal analogue of known cocycle deformations. Neither Popa/IPP nor Sinclair/Peterson-Sinclair is cited by 287, but both are standard in the field.

name: Word derivative equals cocycle value (exact operator-norm word displacement)
statement: delta a_g = i sigma(D_g) a_g, hence ||beta_1(A_w) - C A_w|| <= 3pi ||D_w - delta_e|| exactly (no BCH error).
why: The expected noncommutative analogue. It matters as the coupling that makes C2 meaningful, so grade C2+C4 together for the cluster test.

name: S = Arg(C): bounded Borel logarithm as flow driver
statement: Replace the semicircular driver by S = arg(C), so e^{iS} = C and any flow fixing S fixes C. The discontinuity of the logarithm sidesteps the K_1 obstruction in C*_r(F_{n+1}).
why: Retrieval and transfer of IPP's deformation device. The insight backtrack it triggered has origin 'retrieved', not 'constructed'. The trace analyst's N2 and the paper analyst's N1 are overridden (alt N1 if the representational use is credited).

name: Adaptive error-budget iteration with L2 generation
statement: Iterate C1. Fix eps_k before the witness word w_k and the future budget r_k after it. The A^(k) converge in norm to a free Haar tuple whose word algebra is L2-dense, so it generates M via E_N.
why: A standard diagonal template whose same-problem-area precedent is in L. 287's own Lean proof swaps it for a Baire argument, so the explicit forward-budget ordering is dispensable. Borderline N2 only if that ordering is credited.

name: Nielsen correction (gamma: C -> C A_w, alpha = gamma^{-1} beta)
statement: Compose the flow with the inverse of the free-basis change c -> cw, so that beta(A_w) ~ C A_w becomes alpha(A_w) ~ C.
why: A known object used one step from its standard role.

name: Universal initial trace identity (first-variation proof of tau o delta = 0)
statement: tau(ev_0(delta^r p)) = 0 for all p in the free formal algebra and r >= 1. Analyticity then gives moment invariance.
why: A new proof of a known criterion.

name: Free sum s(k): l2_R(F_n) realised inside M through the free complement
statement: s(k) = sum_g k(g) A_g S A_g^*, with the S_g free, so l2 cocycle values become operators in M.
why: A repackaging of the free Bernoulli field. It has an F5 flavour but is not new.

name: Support-independent free-sum bound (K = 3 pi)
statement: ||sum_j z_j|| <= 2 (sum ||z_j||_2^2)^{1/2} + max ||z_j|| for free centred self-adjoint z_j.
why: Known inequality, re-proved.

name: state / pure state
statement: Positive functional of norm one; pure = extreme point of the state space.
why: Textbook.

name: GNS representation and equivalence h~k of pure states
statement: h~k iff the GNS representations are unitarily equivalent.
why: Textbook.

name: tracial algebra
statement: Unital C*-algebra with a faithful tracial state, extended normally to B**.
why: Renaming of 'C*-algebra with faithful tracial state'.

name: property (U): every pure state of B has exactly one state extension to C
statement: Inclusion B in C such that each pure state of B has a unique state extension.
why: Established notion in the cited literature.

name: peaking sequence ((P_n) peaks to h)
statement: A decreasing sequence of projections peaks to h if h is the only state with h(P_n)=1 for all n.
why: Projection specialisation of AAP excising nets / closed projections; Tanaka2026 (model-produced) also uses projections q_n with tau(q_n)=2^-n excising a product state.

name: support projection r_h in B**
statement: Least projection of B** on which the normal extension of h is one; minimal when h is pure.
why: Textbook.

name: conditional expectation; faithful
statement: UCP map C->B fixing B, B-bimodular; faithful if E(a*a)=0 implies a=0.
why: Textbook.

name: reduced word in A and the stable unitary v
statement: a_0 v^e1 a_1 ... v^em a_m with E_1(a_t)=0 at (+,-) turns and E_2(a_t)=0 at (-,+) turns.
why: Ueda's HNN words.

name: centered element
statement: x in ker E.
why: Textbook.

name: continuous chain
statement: B_gamma = closure of union at limit ordinals.
why: AW04.

name: base algebra A_0 = CAR = (x) M_2 and p_n = e_11^{(x)n}
statement: UHF(2^infty) with product vector state peaked by p_n, tau(p_n)=2^-n.
why: Classical CAR algebra; same base as Tanaka2026.

name: active index / bridge iteration (X_beta)
statement: Continuous chain from A_0 adjoining at active j the bridge for (p_n),(q_n^j) with tau(q_n^j)=2^-n.
why: AW04-type chain with T16 as step.

name: A[T] = C*(A_0, v_j : j in T active)
statement: Subalgebra generated by A_0 and a subset of stable unitaries.
why: Abbreviation.

name: dependency sets I_j and dependency-closed T
statement: Countable I_j subset j with q_n^j in A[I_j]; T is closed if j in T implies I_j subset T.
why: As a definition it is a closure-under-a-function abbreviation; its value lies in T21.

name: schedule sigma: kappa x kappa -> kappa injective with sigma(beta,eta) >= beta, kappa = c^+
statement: Bookkeeping fixed before the construction; replaces diamond's guessing.
why: Folklore bookkeeping (e.g. Kunen-style iterations of length c^+).

name: unique extension of a pure state is pure
statement: If h pure on B has unique extension to C, the extension is pure.
why: Folklore.

name: equivalent pure states are unitarily conjugate; unique lifts of equivalent states are equivalent
statement: Kadison transitivity gives u in B with k = h o Ad(u*).
why: Classical. Lean re-proves Kadison self-adjoint transitivity.

name: peaking under restriction
statement: If (P_n) in B peaks to H on C, it peaks to H|B in B and H is the unique extension of H|B.
why: Elementary observation.

name: decreasing excision (AAP)
statement: Pure h admits a decreasing net of positive contractions x with h(x)=1, x -> r_h strongly, ||x(a-h(a))x|| -> 0.
why: AAP86.

name: projection excision
statement: A peaking sequence excises its state; ||P_n a P_t|| -> 0 when h(a)=0.
why: Specialisation of AAP86.

name: cross-excision (Akemann-Weaver Lemma 1)
statement: h not~ k: ||x_lambda a y_nu|| -> 0 on the product net.
why: AW04 Lemma 1.

name: trace-null supports
statement: No f.d. irreps + tracial tau => tau(r_h)=0 for every pure h.
why: Short folklore fact; key role but easy.

name: at most one trace-preserving expectation; it is faithful
statement: Uniqueness and faithfulness of trace-preserving conditional expectations.
why: Folklore.

name: peaking expectation onto D=C*(p_n)=C(N_0 u {infty})
statement: E(a)(n)=tau(d_n a d_n)/tau(d_n), E(a)(infty)=h(a) is a trace-preserving conditional expectation when traces strictly decrease to 0.
why: Atomic diagonal expectation is standard for c_0-type masas; the twist (value h(a) at infinity, continuity via excision, trace has no mass at infinity) is new but short.

name: (U) + faithful expectation + simple base => simple extension
statement: Simplicity is inherited without ideal analysis.
why: Short, folklore-level.

name: reduced HNN adjunction H(A) with stable unitary and expectation; uniqueness by reduced-word trace vanishing
statement: For trace-preserving theta:D_1->D_2 with expectations, there is a faithfully tracial H(A)=C*(A,v), v d v*=theta(d), E_A killing reduced words; unique up to iso.
why: Ueda's reduced HNN extension; re-proved with the needed expectations.

name: reduced amalgamated free product Z=F*_D G with E_D, E_F, traces
statement: Hilbert D-module free product; E_F kills a_0 b_1 ... b_m a_m words; trace faithful.
why: Standard reduced amalgamated free product. Lean builds it differently: a scalar l^2 Fock space over the atoms of D (AtomicTraceData), possible because D=C(N u infty) with no trace mass at infinity.

name: restriction: C*(A',v) = H(A') for D_1,D_2 subset A'
statement: HNN commutes with shrinking the base.
why: Routine.

name: reordering two adjunctions: H_k(H_j(O)) = H_j(H_k(O))
statement: Two HNN adjunctions with data in a common base O commute, fixing O, v_j, v_k.
why: Symmetric multi-letter HNN extension.

name: HNN commutes with inductive limits of bases
statement: R = closure of union of H(O_beta) is H(O).
why: Routine.

name: the selective bridge (HNN along two matched peaking sequences)
statement: A faithfully tracial, no f.d. irreps; (p_n^1),(p_n^2) peak to f_1 not~ f_2 with equal traces strictly decreasing to 0. The reduced HNN extension along theta(p_n^1)=p_n^2 gives (U) for ALL pure states of A, and h~ ~ k~ iff h~k or {[h],[k]}={[f_1],[f_2]}; H(A) faithfully tracial, simple if A is.
why: No equivalent in L or found elsewhere; it supplies what CF22 Sec. 8 asked for, in a form that works for nonseparable bases.

name: peak transfer through stable letters and the two-ended endpoint criterion
statement: ||dP_G|| <= ||E_D^F(d*d)||^{1/2}; a word decays under x..y if both endpoint expectations decay; matched endpoints are split as phi(a)1 + a^0 and the scalar term moves the peak through the letter, P_n^{l(b)} b = b P_n^{r(b)}, exposing a centered internal coefficient.
why: Inseparable from T16; graded with it.

name: (U) along a continuous chain; unique lifts of equivalent states equivalent
statement: Transfinite composition of (U).
why: AW04.

name: inequivalence persists at limits
statement: Inequivalent on a tail => inequivalent on the limit.
why: Routine.

name: base peak: A_0 separable simple, p_n peaks, tau(p_n)=2^-n; no f.d. irreps above A_0
statement: Properties of the CAR base.
why: Classical.

name: inherited iteration: A[T cap beta] is a bridge iteration for dependency-closed T
statement: Sub-iterations over closed index sets are again bridge iterations; A[T] simple, tracial, separable if T countable.
why: Forcing-iteration analogue; C*-proof routine given C13 and L03.

name: closed-subiteration theorem: A[S] subset X_delta has (U) for every dependency-closed S
statement: Postpone each omitted active step j past the retained ones: R_beta = H_j(O_beta) by P14 and L15, and the omitted pair stays inequivalent on O_beta by T16's no-other-join clause; then T16 gives (U) for A[S u j] subset A[S u (j+1)], and L17 composes.
why: Structural pattern exists in set theory (sub-iterations over adequate index sets are complete suborders) and AWW10 has the free-group special case; the C*-mechanism (reordering HNN adjunctions + no-other-join) is new.

name: countable determination
statement: Every pure h on X_delta has a countable dependency-closed S with h|A[S] pure and h its unique extension.
why: Pure-restriction half is AWW10; uniqueness half is T21.

name: state count: |delta| <= c => X_delta has <= c pure states
statement: Counting via countable determination.
why: Routine.

name: Kishimoto-Ozawa-Sakai homogeneity
statement: Pure states of a separable simple C*-algebra are automorphism-conjugate.
why: KOS03; Lean re-proves it by a quasicentral Krylov-row argument (dominated share 0.111).

name: q_n^j = gamma(p_n) via KOS on separable A[S], with tau(q_n^j)=2^-n from uniqueness of the trace on gamma(M_{2^n})
statement: A matched-trace peaking sequence for the target state, supported on a countable dependency-closed set.
cited_or_new: new here; close variant in model-produced Tanaka2026
why: Close variant exists in Tanaka2026 (model-produced).

name: ZFC recursion of length kappa=c^+ with a state-independent schedule
statement: Build X_beta by bridges scheduled by sigma; countable determination + regularity of c^+ catch every final pure state.
why: Standard bookkeeping once L22 and T16 exist.

name: moment-norm formula ||x|| = lim t((x*x)^r)^{1/2r} for faithful tracial t
statement: Faithful traces determine norms from moments.
why: Folklore.

name: atomic Fock-space model of the amalgamated free product
statement: Replaces Hilbert C*-modules by l^2 over reduced paths through the atoms of D.
why: Formalization device.

name: KOS re-proof via near-central rows (Krylov band averages)
statement: Quasicentral Cesaro averages of Krylov projection chains give near-central row isometries; with Kadison transitivity this yields same-class control and an intertwining limit automorphism.
why: Known theorem, known technique.

name: Selective bridge: reduced HNN extension along a partial isomorphism of two matched peaking-projection algebras
why: Replaces the global automorphism of AW04/FH17 crossed products (which needs separability via KOS and cannot give (U) for all pure states; CF22 Q8.2 is open) with a partial isomorphism of two copies of C(N u infty). The data are countable, so the step works over nonseparable bases. Gives (U) for ALL old pure states and exactly one join; CF22 Prop 8.3 shows this property is what a diamond-free construction needs. Small and non-obvious: matched trace values make theta trace-preserving; trace-null …

name: Closed-subiteration theorem: (U) from every dependency-closed sub-iteration by postponing omitted adjunctions
why: Converts the bridge's no-other-join clause into a global statement; this is the step that removes diamond (introduction.tex:104-105). No C*-algebraic precedent found; dominated share ~0.11.

name: Countable determination replacing diamond; schedule of length c^+
why: Bounds the pure states by c at every stage and supplies a separable determining subalgebra for KOS; highest substantive dominated share (0.153-0.156).

name: Peaking expectation E(a)(n)=tau(d_n a d_n)/tau(d_n), E(a)(infty)=h(a)
why: Makes the HNN data available from a peaking sequence alone; no formula of this form found.

name: Matched-trace peaking sequence q_n = gamma(p_n) via KOS on a separable determining subalgebra
why: Avoids needing gamma to preserve the trace: uniqueness of the trace on gamma(M_{2^n}).

name: Selective bridge: reduced HNN extension along matched peaking-projection algebras (T16 with I20, L09, L07)
statement: A faithfully tracial, no finite-dimensional irreps; (p_n^1),(p_n^2) peak to inequivalent f_1,f_2 with tau(p_n^1)=tau(p_n^2) strictly decreasing to 0. Adjoin v with v p_n^1 v* = p_n^2 as Ueda's reduced HNN extension over D_i = C*(p_n^i). Then every pure state of A has a unique state extension, and the extensions of h,k are equivalent iff h~k or {[h],[k]} = {[f_1],[f_2]}.
why: No construction in any searched source gives an extension that preserves unique extension for all pure states and joins exactly one prescribed pair. The crossed-product precedents (AW04, FH17) need a global automorphism and separability, and the global version of the property is open as CF22 Q8.2. Downgrade pressure: CF22 Sec. 8, which is in L, explicitly suggests a 'partial crossed product' amalgamation for the same goal. The ingredients (Ueda HNN, AAP excision, AW cross-excision, AWW free-pro…

name: Closed-subiteration theorem: (U) for A[S] in X_delta for every dependency-closed S (T21 with L20, I14)
statement: In a bridge iteration with countable dependency sets I_j, every dependency-closed S gives an inclusion A[S] in X_delta with property (U). Proof: postpone each omitted active step past the retained ones (reordering), keeping its pair inequivalent by the bridge's no-other-join clause, then apply the bridge.
why: Templated strengthening: (U) is proved for every closed substructure ('strengthen to all subsets/substructures'), and the induction carries an extra tracked invariant, so it is capped at N2. Close variants exist: the AWW10 special case, and the set-theoretic complete-sub-iteration pattern. The C*-mechanism (postponing adjunctions by HNN reordering while no-other-join keeps the pair apart) is new and is the step that removes diamond, so N3 is plausible if the cap is waived.

name: Countable determination and the c^+ schedule replacing diamond (L22, C23, T25, I15)
statement: Every pure state of X_delta is the unique extension of its pure restriction to a separable A[S] with S countable dependency-closed; hence at most c pure states when |delta| <= c, and a fixed injective schedule kappa x kappa -> kappa with kappa = c^+ treats every pure state.
why: Assembly of AWW10's restriction argument, C2 and standard bookkeeping. The idea is posed in CF22 Sec. 8.

name: Peaking expectation E(a)(n)=tau(d_n a d_n)/tau(d_n), E(a)(infty)=h(a) (L09)
statement: For a peaking sequence with traces strictly decreasing to 0, D=C*(p_n)=C(N u infty) and the displayed map is the trace-preserving conditional expectation onto D.
why: New formula; the only novelty is the value h(a) at infinity, and continuity follows from excision.

name: Matched-trace peaking sequence q_n = gamma(p_n) by KOS on a separable determining subalgebra (I25)
statement: gamma from KOS on A[S] carries g to the reference state on A[S]; q_n = gamma(p_n) peaks to g and tau(q_n) = 2^-n because gamma(M_{2^n}) is a unital matrix subalgebra.
why: Close variant in Tanaka2026 (model-produced). It would be N0 if Tanaka's device is confirmed equivalent from the PDF.

name: Reordering of two HNN adjunctions over a common base (P14)
statement: H_k(H_j(O)) = H_j(H_k(O)) fixing O, v_j, v_k, when both data lie in O.
why: Corollary of the multi-letter HNN or free-product associativity.

name: Trace-null supports: tau(r_h)=0 without finite-dimensional irreps (L07)
statement: If B has no finite-dimensional irreps, every tracial state vanishes on the support projection of every pure state.
why: Folklore; its role in C1 is what matters.

name: Lean-only re-proof of KOS homogeneity via near-central rows (I28)
statement: Kishimoto-Ozawa-Sakai homogeneity, proved with Krylov projection chains and Cesaro-averaged quasicentral rows.
why: Re-proof of a cited theorem.

name: faithful action
statement: An action is faithful when its kernel is trivial; stabilizers need not be trivial.
why: Textbook.

name: almost periodic homeomorphism
statement: f is almost periodic if the closure of {f^j} in Homeo(M) is compact.
why: Standard dynamics notion.

name: almost-periodic corollary
statement: For M as in Thm cor:lie, every almost periodic homeomorphism has an iterate f^m on a continuous R-flow.
cited_or_new: new proof of a conjectured consequence (Pardon Conj 1.4)
why: Immediate corollary: compact abelian Lie group, torus exponential.

name: Thm main (p-adic exclusion)
statement: Every jointly continuous Z_p-action on a connected Hausdorff second-countable n-manifold without boundary has nonzero kernel, hence factors through a finite quotient.
why: The statement itself is the classical p-adic formulation; novelty is in the proof.

name: Thm cor:lie (Hilbert-Smith)
statement: A locally compact second-countable Hausdorff group acting faithfully and jointly continuously on a connected Hausdorff second-countable n-manifold without boundary is a Lie group.
cited_or_new: new (claimed resolution of a famous conjecture)
why: The conjecture statement.

name: test space
statement: Locally compact, finite-dimensional, separable metrizable space: a finite polyhedron, a space homeomorphic to one, an open subset of one, or finite products.
why: Conjunction of standard classes.

name: test categories T(X), T^0(X), P(X), P^0(X)
statement: T^0(X): smallest full replete triangulated subcategory of D^b(Sh_R(X)) containing Rf_* R_B for every continuous f from a compact finite polyhedron B; T(X): its closure under direct summands. P, P^0: same with semialgebraic f.
why: Close neighbours: Woolf's Witt groups of perfect and constructible complexes; Ranicki-Weiss local chain category generated by continuous simplices (paper names both). The variation (generated by proper images of arbitrary continuous maps, not constructible) is new but small.

name: Simplex generators and summands
statement: Closed simplices suffice as sources; every object of T is a summand of an object of T^0; summand closures are thick.
why: Standard skeletal filtration.

name: Duality and compact support on T
statement: Verdier duality restricts to a triangulated duality on T^0, T, P^0, P; biduality is invertible; objects and duals have compact support.
cited_or_new: new in this generality (proof via proper pushforward of simplex duality)
why: Direct consequence of standard Verdier duality (Kashiwara-Schapira) for proper maps; a known technique.

name: Direct images and open extension
statement: Allowed maps induce exact duality-compatible pushforwards Rg_! = Rg_* on T; open extension j_! is fully faithful.
why: Standard sheaf theory.

name: Symmetric cone
statement: The cone of a symmetric morphism u: L -> #L carries a neutral nonsingular symmetric form for the translated duality.
why: Balmer 2000 / Woolf 2008 Lemma 2.1 (delta = +-1 version re-proved).

name: Products with the interval
statement: External products B x A stay in T(I x X); the external duality comparison is an isomorphism and compatible with traces.
why: Standard Kunneth/duality.

name: Two endpoint forms
statement: There is a neutral form on (i_0)_*A + (i_1)_*A with diagonal parts c(i_0)_*alpha and -c(i_1)_*alpha.
why: Woolf 2008 Prop 3.11 transplanted.

name: Homotopy invariance of E_r = W_r(T)
statement: Homotopic maps of test spaces induce equal maps on E_r; contractible test spaces have point Witt groups.
why: Woolf's argument; the only new content is that it runs inside T.

name: Cutoff
statement: For K closed inside O open, every A in B^0(X) admits s: A' -> A with A' compactly supported in O and s invertible near K.
why: Ranicki-Weiss Lemma 4.14 / Cor 4.15 is the named precedent; the sheaf version via polyhedral neighbourhoods of f^{-1}K is routine.

name: Objects supported in an open set
statement: The essential image of j_!: B(U) -> B(X) is the objects with cohomology supported in a compact subset of U; thick and duality-stable.
why: Routine from cutoff.

name: Germ description of the Verdier quotient
statement: Hom in B(X)/B(U) equals colim over neighbourhoods N of X\U of Hom_{D(N)}(A|_N, B|_N).
cited_or_new: new proof of an expected statement
why: Standard style (Verdier quotient by objects supported in U = germs near the complement); proof routine given cutoff.

name: Witt localization (Balmer-Walter)
statement: Long exact sequence W_r(B(U)) -> W_r(B(X)) -> W_r(B(X)/B(U)) -> W_{r-1}(B(U)), natural in maps and in P -> T.
why: Balmer-Walter 2002 Thm 2.1, invoked.

name: Open cover gives a dense inclusion
statement: For X = U cup V, extension gives a fully faithful duality functor B(V)/B(U cap V) -> B(X)/B(U) with dense image.
why: Excision via germs; routine.

name: Dense doubling (cofinality with exponent 2)
statement: For a dense full duality-stable triangulated inclusion A in C, there is d: W(C) -> W(A) with i d = 2 and d i = 2.
why: Hornbostel-Schlichting Appendix A Thm A.2; the doubling D(q)=q+q+H(x[1]) is an explicit proof.

name: Point calculation
statement: E_r(pt)=F_r(pt)=Z (signature) for r = 0 mod 4, else 0.
why: Witt groups of R.

name: Finite diagram chases with exponents
statement: Five-lemma and square chase with explicit annihilating exponents q^3 and 4q.
why: Quantitative five lemma.

name: Bounded comparison F_r(S^j) -> E_r(S^j)
statement: Kernel and cokernel of the semialgebraic-to-continuous comparison on S^j are killed by 2^{e_j}, uniformly in r (e_j = 3(9^j-1)/4).
why: A Mayer-Vietoris induction comparing two homology theories, made integral; standard technique (comparison of homology theories on spheres), new application. Induction carries 'uniform in r' (templated).

name: Rational sphere calculation
statement: G_r(S^j) tensor Q = G_r(pt)_Q + G_{r-j}(pt)_Q for G = E or F; so E_d(S^d)_Q and F_d(S^d)_Q are one-dimensional (d odd).
why: Suspension iso for a homology theory.

name: Signature on a finite semialgebraic relation
statement: Semialgebraic objects are generically locally constant; local signature on a small ball respects any finite Witt relation; hence im F_d(S^d) in F_d(S^d)_Q is exactly Z u_F.
why: Generic local signature is a standard idea (Witt-space / constructible theory).

name: Fixed sphere lattice
statement: For odd d >= 3 there is L_d = 2^{e_d} with E_d(S^d)_Q = Q u_d and im E_d(S^d) in L_d^{-1} Z u_d.
why: If one accepts that E is a homology theory with coefficients W(R), this is E_d(S^d) = Z up to bounded 2-torsion: expected. The novelty is proving it for the non-constructible category T.

name: Action of degree
statement: A degree-s map f: S^d -> S^d acts as multiplication by s on E_d(S^d)_Q; same for pushed orientation forms of closed oriented triangulable d-manifolds.
why: Local-degree computation.

name: Contractible quotient is an integral isomorphism
statement: For d odd and U a nonempty contractible open subset, E_d(X) -> W_d(T(X)/T(U)) is an isomorphism over Z (both d = 1, 3 mod 4).
why: Two-line consequence of localization plus homotopy invariance; the choice of odd d is the design decision.

name: Invariant chart subset (Newman reduction)
statement: There is an open subgroup G = Z_p acting faithfully and orientation-preservingly on a connected invariant open subset O of a chart.
why: Pardon 2013 Section 4.1.

name: odd stabilization W = O x R^{d-n}, d odd > n
statement: Stabilize to an odd dimension d >= 3, with trivial action on the extra factor.
why: Stabilization by R^k is standard; the choice of an odd d is a small design decision.

name: Collapse and compactification
statement: c: S^d -> W^+ is continuous; the action extends to W^+ fixing infinity; orbit spaces are compact metrizable.
why: Routine.

name: Averaged degree-one test
statement: After shrinking G to an open subgroup H that moves points less than the pinch scale, the Haar average of a ball pinch P_{z,r}, normalized, descends to a: Y -> S^d with deg(aqc)=1.
why: Averaging maps/metrics over a compact group is classical (Bochner-Montgomery, Repovs-Scepin averaged metric, Palais). Applying it to a pinch to get an integral degree-one class on the orbit space is a small new twist.

name: Rational orbit pullback injectivity
statement: For a compact G-space E, Rr_* k = r_* k and Q -> r_*Q splits by Haar averaging; so Cech H^j(E/G;Q) -> H^j(E;Q) is injective.
why: Classical rational transfer (Borel, Bredon, Montgomery-Zippin).

name: Killing a rationally trivial map to an odd sphere
statement: For d odd >= 3, K compact metrizable, v: K -> S^d with v^* gamma = 0 rationally, some degree-s map D_s makes D_s v nullhomotopic.
why: Rationalization of odd spheres is K(Q,d) (Serre); DFW 2003 use the same telescope.

name: Finite quotient sheets
statement: For every k there is a nonempty open V in Y on which W/p^kG -> W/G is m = p^k disjoint sheets, with a locally constant multiplier beta: q^{-1}V -> mu_m, beta(gw) = zeta^{g} beta(w).
why: Elementary consequence of faithfulness and the subgroup classification of Z_p.

name: Extending a homotopy from a closed subset
statement: Homotopy extension for maps into S^d from closed subsets of compact metrizable spaces.
why: Borsuk homotopy extension for ANR targets.

name: Moving a test into a prescribed open set
statement: For any nonempty open V in Y \ {y_inf}, some D_s a is homotopic to h with h constant on Y \ V.
why: Combines a rational transfer with odd-sphere rationalization; each piece is standard, the combination on a wild orbit space with no dimension bound is new.

name: Source of a restricted test
statement: Over X \ {b}, the source of f = tqc is an oriented open subset of W and f is proper there, so duality is only ever used on manifolds and test spaces.
why: Observation.

name: orbit sheaf H and eigensheaves H_lambda
statement: H = q_* C_{W^+} (C = real plane), T = action of 1 in G, H_lambda = ker(T - M_lambda), H_D = sum over D, Lambda = mu_{p^infty}.
why: Isotypic decomposition of a smooth representation of a profinite abelian group.

name: Character coproducts
statement: Rq_*C = q_*C = direct sum of H_lambda; Rt_* commutes with these (infinite) sums for compact targets.
why: Standard soft-sheaf argument.

name: Real orthogonality
statement: Distinct character subsums are orthogonal for the pushed orientation form, so character projectors are self-adjoint.
why: Standard.

name: Character classes z_i(t)
statement: For a finite partition of Lambda and a compact test t with contractible neighbourhoods at b_t, z_i(t) in E_d(X) is the unique lift of [A_t, alpha_t] + [A_t, alpha_t(2e_i - id)] under the integral localization iso; e_i is the germ of the character projector near X \ U.
why: No near-equivalent found in a quick search. Neighbours: G-signature / isotypic Witt classes for finite groups (Atiyah-Singer, Neumann, equivariant Witt groups); Witt groups of sheaves (Woolf). Using the 'twice the summand' trick [A,a]+[A,a(2e-1)] plus localization to avoid splitting idempotents at the fixed point is new as far as checked.

name: Sum of character classes
statement: Sum_i z_i(t) = 2 [A_t, alpha_t] integrally, via an explicit isometry S = sum E_j P_j.
why: Elementary matrix identity.

name: Covariance of character classes
statement: g_* z_i(t) = z_i(g t) for maps g of compact tests.
why: Naturality.

name: Homotopy invariance of character classes
statement: Homotopic tests t_0, t_1: Y -> S^d have equal z_i, even though b_t moves; proved through the close-pair test space C_d in S^d x S^d.
why: The close-pair trick (subdivide the homotopy, test with pairs in C_d) is a neat device, but standard in spirit.

name: Equal parts for a concentrated test
statement: If h is constant off a finite-sheet region V, multiplication by beta is an isometry cycling the parts D_i = zeta^i D_0, so z_0(h) = ... = z_{m-1}(h).
why: The sheet-label multiplier twisting characters is the standard Fourier/induction picture for a cyclic cover; the transversal partition is the new touch.

name: Contradiction on the invariant chart
statement: No faithful orientation-preserving Z_p-action on a connected open subset of R^n: z̄_i(a) = (4/p^k) u_d, contradicting the lattice once p^k > 4 L_d.
why: Assembly.

name: Suspending the first product input (signs)
statement: Sign comparison (-1)^r for the external product under suspension.
why: Sign conventions.

name: equal-parts-in-a-fixed-lattice strategy
statement: Fix an integral lattice L_d^{-1} Z u_d first, then for every k produce p^k integral classes with equal rational images summing to 4 u_d; contradiction for p^k > 4 L_d.
why: Divisibility/counting contradictions are classical (Smith theory, transfers, Yang's dimension raising), but using Witt-group integrality of real-coefficient signatures to defeat the Haar-measure 'fractional degree' of a p-adic action is new as far as a quick search shows. Real coefficients are needed to split characters; Witt groups restore integrality that C-coefficient homology loses.

name: Integral character classes z_i(t)
statement: For a compact test t: Y -> X and a finite partition Lambda = D_0 u ... u D_{m-1} of the p-power roots of unity, z_i(t) in E_d(X) = W_d(T(X)) is the unique integral class with l_U(z_i) = [A_t, alpha_t] + [A_t, alpha_t(2e_i - 1)] in W_d(T(X)/T(U)), where e_i are the self-adjoint character projectors on the punctured target and l_U is the integral localization iso for a contractible U around b_t (d odd).
why: A close variant exists: isotypic signature classes for finite group actions (Atiyah-Singer, Gilmer, CSW), including the identity [b] + [b*sigma] = 2[b|V+] for an involution. 304's contribution is to make this work for a profinite group with infinite-dimensional character parts and a non-manifold orbit space. It does so by germ-localizing projectors on the punctured target, lifting integrally through a contractible quotient with d odd, and taking 2x the summand to avoid splitting idempotents. Th…

name: Equal parts in a fixed lattice (organising strategy; L_d fixed before k)
statement: A faithful Z_p action yields, for every k, p^k integral classes in E_d(S^d) whose rational images are equal and sum to 4u_d. Each is then (4/p^k)u_d, contradicting im E_d(S^d) in L_d^{-1}Z u_d once p^k > 4L_d, where L_d is fixed before k.
why: The counting is the classical (and, per the F1 agent, also the Izumi/Rokhlin K-theoretic) free-action signature divisibility (|G| equal isotypic parts of an integer), run with |G| = p^k growing against a lattice fixed beforehand. What is new is the coupling: signature integrality on a finite test polyhedron, reached from a wild orbit space by the averaged degree-one test (C4) and the move-test (C5). This is the first such bridge for Hilbert-Smith that our searches found, but bridge novelty plus…

name: Equal parts for a concentrated test (sheet multiplier beta)
statement: If h: Y -> S^d is constant off a region V where W/p^kG -> W/G has p^k labelled sheets, multiplication by a locally constant beta with beta(gx) = zeta beta(x) cyclically permutes the parts D_i = zeta^i D_0, so z_0(h) = ... = z_{m-1}(h).
why: Once the character classes and the finite sheets exist, the multiplier is the standard trivialisation of a character local system. N1 (borderline N2).

name: Averaged degree-one test a: Y -> S^d
statement: After shrinking G to a small open subgroup H, the Haar average of a ball pinch, normalised, descends to a: Y = W^+/G -> S^d with deg(aqc) = 1.
why: A one-step application of classical compact-group averaging. The idea of a degree-one map out of the wild orbit space is a neat use of it, with close neighbours in L.

name: Moving a multiple of the test into a prescribed open set
statement: For any nonempty open V in Y \ {y_inf}, some D_s a (deg D_s = s > 0) is homotopic to h constant off V.
why: A composition of named known techniques. The family analyst's N2 is lowered to N1, borderline N2, because DFW's telescope is cited and used identically.

name: Test categories T(X) generated by Rf_* of arbitrary continuous maps from compact polyhedra
statement: T(X) is the thick subcategory of D^b(Sh(X;R)) generated by Rf_* R_B for continuous f: B -> X with B a compact polyhedron (non-constructible in general). E_r(X) = W_r(T(X)). Verdier duality restricts to it, and E_r is homotopy invariant.
why: An adaptation of Woolf / Ranicki-Weiss that the paper names. It is technically necessary because the action forces non-constructible images.

name: Fixed sphere lattice via bounded 2-power comparison with the semialgebraic subcategory
statement: Comparison F_r(S^j) -> E_r(S^j) has kernel and cokernel killed by 2^{e_j}, uniformly in r, with e_j = 3(9^j - 1)/4. Hence im E_d(S^d) -> E_d(S^d)_Q lies in L_d^{-1} Z u_d with L_d = 2^{e_d}.
why: A uniform-exponent strengthening of a standard comparison (templated strengthening: uniform/quantitative version), so it is capped at N2 regardless. It is technically the crux for correctness, and the family analyst's gap 1 sits here.

name: Cutoff lemma and germ description of the Verdier quotient T(X)/T(U)
statement: Morphisms in T(X)/T(U) are germs near X \ U, realised by cutting off the finite polyhedral sources. This lets projectors defined on the punctured target act in the quotient.
why: A new proof of an expected statement in a new category, with named antecedents. N1, borderline N2.

name: Homotopy invariance of character classes via the close-pair space C_d
statement: z_i(t) depends only on the homotopy class of the test map, shown by pushing through a close-pair space C_d of pairs of nearby test maps.
why: An expected property with a technical device. The analyst's provisional N2 is lowered.

name: Integral character classes z_i(t) (localization-lifted 'twice the isotypic summand')
why: It is hard to anticipate an invariant that is (a) integral, (b) defined for each character part of a profinite action with infinite-dimensional stalks, and (c) homotopy-invariant in the test map even though the decomposition fails at the fixed point at infinity. The trick [A,a] + [A,a(2e-1)] avoids splitting idempotents, and odd d makes the localization lift integral. It is not a subterm of the goal or of L, and every step of the contradiction runs through it. Rational or C-coefficient homology…

name: Equal parts in a fixed lattice (fix L_d before k)
why: It reformulates the profinite 'Haar fractional degree' as p^k equal integral classes summing to 4, against a lattice fixed in advance. The order of quantifiers (L_d before k) is the crux. No precedent found for Hilbert-Smith.

name: Moving a positive multiple of the degree-one test into any open set of the orbit space
why: It works on orbit spaces with no dimension bound (the known theory says dim is n+2 or infinity), avoiding the classical obstacle. It bridges a global degree with local sheet symmetry.

name: Averaged degree-one test
why: It is the only use of small subgroups: an integral degree-one class on the wild orbit space, which is impossible for any finite group.

name: Bounded (2-power) comparison F -> E on spheres; T categories generated by arbitrary continuous images
why: It extends sheaf Witt homology integrally to non-constructible objects, which the action forces on us. Rational equivalence alone would lose the denominator bound.

name: Lip_0(M) and the Lipschitz-free space F(M)
statement: Lip_0(M) = real Lipschitz functions vanishing at o with the Lipschitz constant as norm; F(M) = closed span of the evaluations delta_x in Lip_0(M)^*; ||delta_x - delta_y|| = d(x,y).
why: Arens-Eells / Godefroy-Kalton free space.

name: AP, lambda-BAP, BAP, MAP; proper metric space
statement: AP: finite-rank T with sup_{u in C}||Tu-u||<eps on every compact C; lambda-BAP adds ||T||<=lambda; BAP = lambda-BAP for some lambda; MAP = 1-BAP. Proper = closed bounded balls compact.
why: Grothendieck approximation properties.

name: approximable separable Banach space (Kalton)
statement: X is approximable if there are equi-uniformly continuous psi_n: X->X with relatively compact ranges and psi_n(x)->x for all x.
why: Kalton 2012.

name: Thm main (thm:main): countable uniformly discrete M with F(M) AP but not BAP
statement: There is a countable, unbounded, nonproper pointed metric space with d(x,y)>=1 for distinct points such that F(M) has AP but fails lambda-BAP for every finite lambda>=1.
why: Results are not graded as machinery.

name: Thm blocks (thm:blocks): finite anchor obstruction in a bounded 1-separated block
statement: For each integer p>=1 there are a bounded countably infinite pointed space M_p, 1-separated, diam <= B_p = 300p^2+150p+5, and a finite A_p containing o such that every finite-rank T_0 on F(M_p) with ||T_0||<=p has max_{a in A_p}||T_0 delta_a - delta_a|| >= 1/2.
why: Result; the strongest machinery is I31-I34.

name: Cor renorming (cor:renorming): equivalent norms on real ell_1 with 2B_p-BAP but not p-BAP; for p=1 not MAP
statement: For each p>=1, ell_1 has an equivalent norm with (1/2)||c||_1 <= ||c||_p <= B_p||c||_1, having 2B_p-BAP but failing p-BAP; for p=1 it fails MAP.
why: Transport of structure.

name: finite-block reduction of the problem (blocks + wedge strategy)
statement: Reduce the infinite problem to a sequence of bounded blocks, each with its own finite anchor obstruction at level p, glued by a metric wedge; each block individually has BAP.
why: Decomposing via contractive retractions onto pieces is a standard device (ell_1-sums of free spaces, Kalton 2004); the novelty is the content of each block, not the reduction.

name: metric wedge M of the blocks, d(x,y)=d_p(x,o)+d_q(y,o) across blocks
statement: Identify basepoints; cross-block distance is the sum of distances to o. M is countable, 1-separated, unbounded (Thm blocks + Prop coefficients or Lemma block-geometry (iii)), nonproper (M_1 is infinite 1-separated in a ball).
why: Standard pointed metric sum; F of a wedge is the ell_1-sum of the F(M_p).

name: Prop coefficients (prop:coefficients): bounded 1-separated N has F(N) ~ ell_1(N\{o}) with (1/2)||c||_1 <= ||Jc|| <= B||c||_1, and 2B-BAP
statement: J c = sum c_x delta_x is an isomorphism; coordinate truncations S_m = J q_m J^{-1} give 2B-BAP.
why: Cited by the paper to AACD20 Thm 4.14 and Cuth-Kalenda Lemma 3.4.

name: linearization of pointed 1-Lipschitz maps; inclusion/retraction contractions I_p, P_p with P_p I_p = Id
statement: Pointed 1-Lipschitz u: N->N' induces a norm-one linear map F(N)->F(N'); inclusion and retraction onto a block give P_p I_p = Id, so I_p is an isometry.
why: Godefroy-Kalton linearization.

name: failure of lambda-BAP for the wedge via compression P_p U I_p
statement: If F(M) had lambda-BAP, choose integer p>=lambda; compress an approximating U to P_p U I_p, contradicting Thm blocks at the anchors.
why: Routine complemented-subspace argument.

name: finite-block projection R_N = sum_{p<=N} I_p P_p and AP of the wedge
statement: R_N is the linearization of the retraction keeping N blocks; R_N u -> u uniformly on compacta; then compose with per-block 2B_p-BAP operators; norm sum_{p<=N} 2B_p is finite but grows with C, eps.
cited_or_new: new (routine); Kalton's general AP theorem cited as alternative
why: AP itself is Kalton's theorem; the direct proof is a standard exhaustion.

name: nonlinear corollary: F(M) is not approximable (Kalton's Problem 1)
statement: Extend {delta_x} to a maximal 1-separated net N_X; Kalton's net characterization would give uniformly Lipschitz maps g: N_X->N_X with finite range fixing any finite set of evaluations; their linearizations T_F give Lambda-BAP, contradiction.
why: C5 transfer: Kalton12 Thm 4.4 + Kalton04 Lemma 3.2.

name: graph conventions: oriented incidences e, e-bar; nonbacktracking walk; rooted radius-r colored ball type
statement: Multigraph with distinct edge instances, two oriented incidences per edge (loops count twice); a walk is nonbacktracking if it never immediately takes the reverse incidence.
why: Standard.

name: Lemma local-limit (lem:local-limit): deterministic Delta-regular multigraphs G_m whose colored neighborhoods converge to the independently uniformly colored De…
statement: Permutation model (Delta/2 uniform permutations) + independent uniform k-colorings; exploration gives collision probability O(N^{-1}); two-root exploration gives variance -> 0; choose realizations N_m with all radius<=m frequencies within 1/m.
why: Local weak convergence of random regular (permutation-model) graphs to the regular tree, with iid marks; textbook (Bordenave's notes; Benjamini-Schramm).

name: scale parameters L=10p, R=3L, K=10p(R+1), D=K+2L+5, B=4R+D, V=1+4pB; Delta even with V/Delta<1/20; Q=Delta^{2L+1}, H=Delta^{D+1}; k>2 Delta Q H colors
statement: Chosen so that R>2L (small balls stay in one source graph), (2pR+1)/K<=1/5 (bump loss), K+2L+1<D (compatibility below cap), Delta dilutes the one-exceptional-direction loss, k makes Delta*Q*H/k<1/2.
why: Parameter budget; checked arithmetically (B = 300p^2+150p+5).

name: source vertices and capped color-distance labels h(x) in {0..D}^k
statement: h_i(x) = min{D, dist_{G_m}(x, color class i)}; labels vary by <=1 along edges; own-color coordinate is 0; at most H coordinates are below the cap.
cited_or_new: new use of a classical device
why: Truncated distance-to-random-colour-class coordinates = Frechet/Bourgain-style random-set embedding into ell_infinity; capping is routine. Transfer (N0/N1), not a eureka step by itself.

name: anchors a_v (one per realized label v), attachment edges of length R, anchor-anchor edges of length 2R+||v-w||_inf, metric d_p = weighted path metric; basepoin…
statement: Join every source vertex to the anchor of its label by length R; join anchors by 2R + label sup-distance. Finitely many labels => finitely many anchors; the block becomes bounded (diam <= 4R+D) while small balls (radius 2L<R) stay inside one source graph.
why: Leaning N3 as a component of the block. Hub/cone attachments to make a metric bounded are generic, and the label-indexed choice is natural once labels exist; graded N2 on its own. It is load-bearing only together with I17 and I23.

name: Lemma block-geometry (lem:block-geometry): separation 1, diam <= B_p, h 1-Lipschitz, d(x,a)>=R, |ball(2L)|<=Q, <=H uncapped label coordinates
statement: Integer edge lengths give separation and attained infima; diameter via attachment-anchor-attachment; label differences sum along paths; short paths use only source edges; walk counts bound balls and uncapped colours.
why: Routine verification.

name: colour restriction: compatibility with a fixed point t permits at most H source colours
statement: If x has colour i and ||h(x)-h(t)||_inf < D then h_i(t) < D, so the colour of x lies in C_t = {i : h_i(t) < D}, |C_t| <= H.
why: Immediate from the own-colour coordinate being 0; the useful idea is to forget labels and keep only colours (an independence trick).

name: Lemma finite-support (lem:finite-support): perturb T_0 to T with range in span{delta_j: j in S}, S finite, ||T||<=2p, anchor errors <1
statement: Write T_0 = sum phi_i(.) v_i and replace v_i by finitely supported w_i with total error < eta < min{p,1/(2B)}.
why: Standard small-perturbation of finite-rank operators.

name: label bump b_x(t) = L(1 - ||h(x)-h(t)||_inf / K)_+
statement: Nonnegative, height L at the anchor a(x), Lipschitz constant <= L/K <= 1; positive only where the label is within K of h(x).
why: Tent/hat function of a 1-Lipschitz map; routine once labels and anchors exist.

name: Lemma measure-bounds (lem:measure-bounds): affine signed representation mu_x of T delta_x on S, TV <= V = 1+4pB, and int b_x d mu_x >= 3L/4
statement: mu_x puts c_x(j) on j != o and the balance at o, so int g d mu_x = (T delta_x)(g - g(o)) + g(o); a sign test (Lip <= 2 by separation) bounds TV; comparing T delta_x with delta_{a(x)} (distance R, anchor error <1) and pairing with the small-slope bump gives the mass bound.
cited_or_new: new statement; affine signed representation is standard
why: Affine signed representation + TV bound are standard (Naor21 named); the anchor-to-vertex bump-mass transfer is a short new step.

name: compatible (graph vertex x, state j): ||h(x)-h(j)||_inf <= K+2L+1 = D-4
statement: Threshold allows label distance < K (bump positive), one source-edge step, one state step of length <= 2L.
why: A thresholded proximity relation.

name: matched nonbacktracking walk: states j_0..j_t in S, (x_s,j_s) compatible, d_p(j_{s-1},j_s) <= 2L
statement: A source walk 'tracked' by a sequence of support points with compatible labels and bounded jumps; states and vertices may repeat.
why: Close in spirit to 'a finite automaton tracking a random coloured tree' and to graph homomorphism/tracking arguments; as a definition it is small. Graded N2; it is part of the N3 complex I31-I34.

name: Lemma rare-walks (lem:rare-walks): fraction beta_m of roots starting a matched walk of length n has limsup <= |S|(H/k)(Delta Q H / k)^n
statement: Weaken 'matched' to 'colour of x_s in C_{j_s} with allowed state transitions' (determined by the radius-n coloured ball); count Delta^n walks x |S|Q^n state paths x (H/k)^{n+1}; local limit transfers the bound to G_m. Choose n then m with beta < 1/(20V).
why: Standard first-moment count on an iid-coloured tree; the order-of-choices remark (S fixed before n,m) is the only subtlety.

name: Remark non-tree-bad-set (rem:non-tree-bad-set)
statement: Bad set may be enlarged by roots with non-tree neighbourhoods at no cost.
why: Commentary.

name: good / bad vertex
statement: Bad if a matched walk of length n starts there; good otherwise.
why: Thresholded predicate.

name: continuation record r_x(e,j) = max length of matched walks starting through incidence e with initial state j (0 if none)
statement: Finite (< n) at good vertices because any longer matched walk has a matched prefix of length n.
why: Named precedent: Ben-David et al. Algorithm 1 FindParent picks the direction with the longest nonbacktracking continuation (arXiv 2006.12760 Sec 6.1.2). Here records are deterministic and indexed by support states.

name: exceptional incidence at (x,j) (record strictly larger than all others; at most one; ties give none); E_e = states for which e is exceptional at its tail; all …
statement: At a good vertex each state is exceptional in at most one direction.
why: Strict-argmax parent direction, as in Ben-David et al. (argmax of continuation lengths). The state indexing and the use as 'discard set' for scalar tests are new.

name: Lemma exceptional-directions (lem:exceptional-directions): if (x,j),(y,j') compatible across incidence e:x->y and d(j,j')<=2L then j in E_e or j' in E_{e-bar}
statement: Prepending e to a longest walk in another direction at y gives r_x(e,j) >= 1+A_y and symmetrically r_y(e-bar,j') >= 1+A_x; if neither were exceptional, A_x >= 1+A_y >= 2+A_x.
why: Very close to Ben-David et al. Lemma 58 (arXiv numbering; Lemma 6.3 in SICOMP), whose proof derives l_v > l_u and l_v < l_u from prepending an edge. The paper names this precedent. Transfer from TCS, adapted.

name: Lemma edge-test (lem:edge-test): 1-Lipschitz f_e: M_p->[-L,L] equal to b_x on S\E_e and to -b_y on S\E_{e-bar}
statement: Within each set the bump's Lipschitz bound suffices; cross pairs at distance >= 2L are fine since values lie in [0,L]; for closer cross pairs a positive value forces compatibility of both pairs, which I31 forbids; then McShane extension + clipping.
why: Weak N3 (as the core of the complex I30-I34). No near-equivalent found: a 1-Lipschitz test that is +bump(x) and -bump(y) on a finite support except on a combinatorially selected discard set. Against: once one decides to compare mu_x and mu_y with opposing bumps, the need to discard close cross pairs is forced and the record trick is imported from TCS.

name: edge lower/upper bounds and incidence averaging: int f_e d(mu_x - mu_y) >= 3L/2 - 2L(|mu_x|(E_e)+|mu_y|(E_{e-bar})) and <= 2p; average over oriented incidences…
statement: Each state is exceptional in at most one of the Delta directions at a good vertex, so averaging over incidences divides the discarded variation by Delta; bad vertices are rare. Regularity makes the uniform vertex-then-incidence sampling uniform on incidences and reversal-invariant.
why: Averaging-over-edges contradictions are standard (Poincare-type/expander arguments); the specific accounting (one exceptional direction per state, diluted by degree) is new but follows once I30-I32 exist. Part of the N3 complex.

name: order of choices: graph sequence, block and anchors fixed before the operator; S from the operator; then n, then one large graph G_m
statement: Local convergence applies to every finite coloured event, including events specified by an already-fixed support, so no independence between the operator and the graph is needed.
why: A quantifier-order observation, but it dictates that the block is an infinite union of ever larger graphs (so the block is infinite while A_p is finite).

name: Remark abstract-obstruction (rem:abstract-obstruction): sufficient criterion (i)-(iv) for the finite-anchor obstruction
statement: Any countable pointed 1-separated space of diameter <= B with finite A, disjoint Delta-regular coloured graphs with tree-like colour statistics, a 1-Lipschitz label map with own-colour zero and anchors at distance <= R, and ball/label bounds, satisfies the obstruction.
why: Abstraction of the proof.

name: McShane extension formula F(z)=min_j {v(j)+d(z,j)} followed by clipping
statement: Finite 1-Lipschitz data extend to a 1-Lipschitz function; clipping to [-L,L] keeps values and bound.
why: McShane 1934.

name: finite permutation quotients of free-group word balls and their Cayley port graphs (girth > N)
statement: WordBall A N = reduced words of length <= N; extend left multiplication by each generator to a permutation (Equiv.Perm.exists_extending_pair); the induced action of FreeGroup A is injective on words of length <= N, so reduced walks of length <= N in the Cayley graph of Perm(WordBall) visit distinct vertices.
why: Residual finiteness of free groups / large-girth Schreier graphs (e.g. Margulis, Erdos-Sachs style); a standard derandomization.

name: all-colourings graph: vertex set (colourings of Cayley_N) x Cayley_N, one component per colouring; exact colour counting replaces probability
statement: Because reduced walks are injective, the number of colourings making a walk's colours land in prescribed sets is exactly prod|P_i| k^{|X|-(n+1)} (cardinal_identity); a union bound over walks and state paths gives the bad-root fraction with walk length n = component index N.
cited_or_new: new to this formalization (paper uses random colourings)
why: Standard derandomization (sum over the whole probability space).

name: complete weighted graph metric with fallback weight 4R+cap and integer metric closure
statement: weight = 1 on graph edges, R vertex-to-own-anchor, 2R+label distance between anchors, 4R+cap otherwise; NatMetricClosure gives an integer metric; short_distance shows any path of length < R is a source-graph walk.
why: Engineering variant of I18.

name: Operator-adapted opposing edge tests with exceptional discard sets, averaged over incidences
statement: Given a finite-rank T (norm <= 2p) with finite support S and measures mu_x, for each oriented incidence e:x->y build a 1-Lipschitz f_e: M_p -> [-L,L] equal to b_x on S\E_e and -b_y on S\E_{e-bar}; then int f_e d(mu_x - mu_y) >= 3L/2 - 2L(|mu_x|(E_e)+|mu_y|(E_{e-bar})) and <= 2p. Since each state is exceptional in at most one of Delta directions at a good vertex, E|mu_x|(E_e) <= V/Delta + V*beta < 1/10, giving 2p > 11p.
why: No neighbour found in searches over Lipschitz-free/BAP literature, expander Poincare inequalities, AP-counterexample averaging (Enflo/Davie/Szankowski), extension obstructions, or coarse geometry. The non-obvious content is the coupling: operator-dependent tests whose inconsistency on nearby support states is resolved by discarding states in at most one direction, so averaging divides the loss by the degree. Downward pressure: its hardest sub-step (C3) is TCS transfer, the averaging is mass-tra…

name: Label-anchor block: capped colour-distance labels, one anchor per realised label, label bumps
statement: Label every source vertex by h(x) = (min(D, dist(x, colour class i)))_i; attach x by an edge of length R to the anchor of its label; join anchors by 2R + ||v-w||_inf. The block is bounded (diam <= B_p), 1-separated, h is 1-Lipschitz, small balls stay in one graph, and at most H label coordinates are uncapped; the bump b_x peaks (value L) at a(x) with slope L/K.
why: Each component is a known device (Frechet/Bourgain distance-to-set coordinates, coning to hubs, tent functions). The fit (labels that make the block bounded and give every vertex an anchor lever, while keeping at most H uncapped coordinates for later colour restriction) is a design choice, not a new concept. It pays off only after C1/C4 (chain depth). Upgrade to N3 only if Test 4 shows proposers never produce label-indexed anchors.

name: Continuation records and at-most-one-exceptional-direction lemma
statement: At good vertices, r_x(e,j) = longest matched walk through e from state j; e is exceptional at (x,j) iff its record strictly exceeds all others. If (x,j),(y,j') are compatible across e:x->y and d(j,j') <= 2L, then j in E_e or j' in E_{e-bar}.
why: Same argument as Ben-David et al. Lemma 58 (prepend an edge; symmetric strict inequalities), made deterministic and state-indexed; also a Jordan tree-centre template. Cross-field transfer (TCS property testing -> Banach geometry). Its novelty is the decision to use it, which belongs to C1.

name: Matched walks and their rarity via colour restriction
statement: A matched walk tracks a nonbacktracking source walk by support states with compatible labels and consecutive state distance <= 2L. Compatibility with a fixed state allows <= H source colours, so on the iid-coloured tree the fraction of roots starting a length-n matched walk is <= |S|(H/k)(Delta Q H/k)^n.
why: The colour-restriction independence trick is neat but the bound is a standard first-moment count. As a definition it is small and pays off only inside C1/C3.

name: Affine signed-measure representation with anchor-to-vertex bump mass
statement: T delta_x is represented by an affine signed measure mu_x on S with TV <= V = 1 + 4pB, and int b_x d mu_x >= 3L/4 (anchor approximation at a(x), operator norm over distance R, slope L/K).
why: Downgraded from the analyst's N2: the representation is standard (named precedent Naor21, AACD20) and the bump-mass step is a direct computation from items in C2 and L.

name: Per-operator finite-anchor obstruction in bounded infinite blocks, with order of choices
statement: Reduce Kalton's question to bounded 1-separated infinite blocks M_p with a finite anchor set A_p defeating every finite-rank T with ||T|| <= p; glue blocks in a metric wedge. Fix graphs, block and anchors before T; choose walk length and graph size after T's support.
why: Standard assembly (Figiel-Johnson-style sums, Kalton's l_1-sum of free spaces). The insistence on an infinite bounded block (finite blocks always have 1-BAP) is an observation forced by the problem, not a construction.

name: I32 (+I30, I33): opposing edge tests with exceptional discard sets and incidence averaging
why: Not a subterm of the goal or of L: the goal speaks of finite-rank operators and anchors; the proof manufactures, for every oriented edge, a 1-Lipschitz functional that is +bump(x) and -bump(y) on the operator's support minus a combinatorially chosen discard set. It is where the finite-dimensionality of the range (finite S) is actually exploited against the infinite locally-tree-like structure; every other step is preparation. No near-equivalent found in a quick search of Lipschitz-extension / f…

name: I18 (+I17, I22): label-anchor block (capped colour-distance labels, one hub per label, bump peaking at the hub)
why: Simultaneously makes the block bounded (so F(M_p) ~ ell_1 with BAP, needed for AP and for the ell_1 renorming) and gives the anchor approximation a lever on every source vertex through the 1-Lipschitz label map. The Lean label definitions are the only non-carrier items passing the 20% load-bearing proxy (PortGraph.label 0.23, originalLabel 0.21). Not in the goal; nothing in L glues graphs through label-indexed hubs.

name: I31 (+I29, I30): continuation records and the at-most-one-exceptional-direction lemma
why: Short, non-analytic and essential: it is what allows opposing prescriptions to coexist on a 1-Lipschitz function. Transferring a property-testing lemma into Banach-space geometry is an unusual cross-field step.

name: I25 + I26 (+I20): matched walks and their rarity via colour restriction
why: The definition (a support-state sequence tracking a nonbacktracking walk with compatible labels) is invented for the proof, and dropping labels in favour of colours (I20) is a neat way to recover independence.

name: I07: per-operator finite anchor obstruction inside bounded blocks (vs projection/extension obstructions)
why: The paper stresses that earlier finite obstructions (Brudnyi-Brudnyi, Godefroy-Ozawa) only bound projections with prescribed range, while here a fixed finite set defeats every operator of norm <= p.

name: n-regular point
statement: p is n-regular if every pointed GH tangent at p is pointed-isometric to (R^n,|.|,0).
why: Standard (Cheeger-Colding; DPG18).

name: noncollapsed RCD(K,n) space (measure exactly H^n, full CD(K,n), quadratic Cheeger energy)
statement: Noncollapsed means the reference measure is exactly H^n_d; full CD(K,n) with quadratic Cheeger energy; complete separable geodesic, full support.
why: Standard (De Philippis-Gigli 2018).

name: Main theorem (bi-Lipschitz chart at every regular point, L_n depends only on n)
statement: For every n>=2 there is L_n>=1: if X is noncollapsed RCD(K,n) and every tangent at p is R^n, there are open U ni p, open V in R^n and a homeomorphism F:U->V with L_n^{-1}d(x,z)<=|F(x)-F(z)|<=L_n d(x,z) on U, d the ambient distance.
why: Goal statement, not graded.

name: Full-measure open Lipschitz-manifold region
statement: There is an open U containing every n-regular point with H^n(X\U)=0 and a countable atlas of L_n-bi-Lipschitz charts, transition maps L_n^2-bi-Lipschitz.
why: Union of charts + Lindelof; trivial given I03.

name: Quadratic-form notation A[xi], |xi|_A, multilinear norms ||T||_{H->Q}
statement: A[xi]=xi^T A xi, |xi|_A = A[xi]^{1/2}; frozen source/target norms for multilinear maps.
why: Notation.

name: Carre du champ Gamma(f,g)=<grad f, grad g>
statement: Gamma(f,g)=<grad f,grad g>, Gamma(f)=Gamma(f,f); Laplacians of gradient squares as measures.
why: Standard.

name: Local analytic facts, Bochner measure M(w) and shifted Bochner inequality (co:local-calculus)
statement: Constant-Laplacian solutions are local test functions; M(w)=1/2 Delta Gamma(w)+kappa Gamma(w) m is a nonnegative locally finite measure; M(w)-(2b Delta w - n b^2)m >= |Hess w - b g|^2 m; uniform cutoffs, Poincare, Dirichlet-Sobolev (d_*>1).
why: Collection of cited facts; the shifted inequality is algebra.

name: Gram matrix field G and matrix Bochner measure M of the harmonic column u; matrix Cauchy-Schwarz
statement: G=(Gamma(u_j,u_k)), M=(M(u_j,u_k)) (polarized); |M(v,w)|(E)<=sqrt(M[v](E) M[w](E)).
why: Matrix packaging of standard objects.

name: Expanding almost-Euclidean regime (co:flat-setup)
statement: Rescalings X_nu at p with kappa_nu->0, T_nu->infty: all balls centred in B_{64T}(p) of radius <=64T are delta_nu-close to Euclidean in volume and GH; harmonic columns u_nu converging to coordinates, |grad u|<=C_n.
why: Standard (Cheeger-Colding / DPG18 epsilon-regularity).

name: Dyadic mean Gram matrices R_i(y)=avg_{B_{r_i}(y)} G, r_i=2^{-i}
statement: R_i(y) = average of G over B_{2^{-i}}(y).
why: Abbreviation.

name: Uniform harmonic normalization at every centre and scale (co:harmonic-normalization), incl. inline def 'tau-normalizable'
statement: R_i(y)>0; U_{i,y}=R_i(y)^{-1/2}(u-u(y))/r_i is o(1)-close to Euclidean coordinates (up to rotation) on B_{Cr_i}(y); (1+-o(1)) comparability for nearby centres/scales; slow growth C_a 2^{2a|i-j|}; c_a r_i^{2a} Id <= R_i <= C Id.
why: Special case of the cited transformation theorems in the uniformly flat regime.

name: Small normalized Bochner mass (co:bochner-small)
why: Routine consequence.

name: Open harmonic coordinates, ellipsoid containment, separation at scale (co:open-coordinates)
statement: u is a homeomorphism of B_A(p) onto an open set; {P: |P-u(x)|_{R_i(x)^{-1}}<c r_i} subset u(B_{r_i/2}(x)); ||u(z)-u(x)|_{R_i(x)^{-1}} - d(x,z)| <= o(1) r_i at comparable scale.
why: Standard successive-approximation surjectivity argument.

name: Kernel differences and measure sources (co:kernel-measures)
statement: Averaged heat kernel bounds K_t<=C r^{-n}e^{-cD^2/r^2} (t<=r^2), |K_t - p_t(x,.)|<=C r t^{-(n+1)/2} e^{-cD^2/t}; P_tf-P_sf = int P_tau mu for measure Laplacians.
why: Standard heat-kernel calculus.

name: Cutoff source formula Delta(chi G)=2chi M - 2kappa chi G m + E_cut m
statement: Distributional Laplacian of the cut-off Gram field.
why: Routine.

name: Monotone heat Gram matrices Q_i=P_{r_i^2}(chi G)+lambda r_i^2 Id, H_i=Q_i^{-1} (co:heat-matrices)
statement: P_t(chi M) <= d/dt(P_t(chi G)+lambda t Id) <= 3P_t(chi M)+C Id; (1+-o(1))R_i <= Q_i; H_i <= H_{i+1} <= (1+o(1))H_i; ||H_i||<=C_a 2^{2ai}.
why: Close to CJN21's heat Gram normalization; lambda t shift is routine.

name: Raw dyadic masses N_j(x)=r_j^{2-n}M(B_{r_j}(x))
statement: Unconjugated masses; N_j <= eps_nu Q_j.
why: Abbreviation.

name: Dyadic heat comparison; exponentially smoothed mass F_i=2^{-gamma i}Id+sum_j 2^{-gamma(i-j)}N_j (co:heat-comparison)
statement: c_A r_i^{2-n}M(B_{Ar_i}(x)) <= Q_i-Q_{i+1} <= C F_i; |v^T(R_i(y)-Q_i(x))w| <= C|v|_{Q_i} sqrt(F_i[w]). Gaussian shell coefficients k_h.
why: Heat-kernel bookkeeping; precedent in CJN21.

name: Fixed enlargements and indexing (co:enlargement-indexing)
statement: Enlarged masses r_j^{2-n}M(B_{Ar_j}) <= 2^{h(n-2)} N_{j-h}.
why: Plumbing.

name: Weighted inverse increments / central cumulative comparison (co:inverse-increments)
statement: B_i=H_{i+1}-H_i satisfies H_i Delta_i H_i <= B_i <= (1+C eps)H_i Delta_i H_i; sum_{i<k} F_i[H_i xi] <= C H_k[xi]; C^{-1}H_k <= Id + sum_{i<k} H_i N_i H_i <= C H_k, without commutativity.
why: Non-commutative version of CJN21 telescoping; convolution trick is careful but standard.

name: Changing the mean normalization (co:normalization-error)
statement: e_{i,y}=R_i(y)^{-1}xi - H_i(x)xi has |e|_{Q_i}^2 <= C F_i[H_i xi]; sums <= C_J H_k[xi]; mass error <= C_J eps H_k[xi].
why: Routine dual-form estimate.

name: Local mass forms D_{i,y}=R_i(y)^{-1}[r_i^{2-n}M(B_{Lr_i}(y))]R_i(y)^{-1}; cumulative comparison Z_i<=o(1)H_i, Id+sum Z_i <= C_* H_k, H_k <= C_*(Id+sum S_i) (co…
statement: For boundedly many centres y within C_0 r_i of x with weights theta in [0,1] (one weight-1 centre covering B_{r_i}(x)), Z_i=sum D_{i,y}, S_i=sum theta D_{i,y}: Z_i<=o(1)H_i(x), Id+sum_{i<k} Z_i <= C_* H_k(x), H_k(x) <= C_*(Id+sum_{i<k} S_i).
why: Object is a re-expression of known normalized Hessian/Bochner energies; the two-sided cumulative comparison with weights is new but follows I20.

name: Radii R=16(L+C_sep+2), S=32R and domain nesting
statement: Fixed enlargements chosen before the late rescaling.
why: Plumbing.

name: Linear gradient bound for a positive source (pi:positive-source)
statement: If -Delta h = mu >= 0, h in W^{1,2}_0, mu(Omega)<=P then int|grad h| <= CP and int|grad h|^2 <= ||h||_inf P.
why: Known (Boccardo-Gallouet 1989 measure-data estimates; truncation + layer cake).

name: Shifted Bochner measure B_kappa(w,b)=M(w)-(2b Delta w - n b^2)m and its quadratic triangle inequality
statement: Nonnegative, quadratic in (w,b); B(w1-w2,b1-b2)<=2B(w1,b1)+2B(w2,b2).
why: Abbreviation.

name: Poisson replacements f_i^a of d_a^2/2 with summable defects P_i(a) (pi:poisson-pinching)
statement: Delta f_i^a = n + C_0 kappa r_i^2, f-q in W_0^{1,2}(B_{8Sr_i}(a)); P_i(a)=r_i^{-n}mu_i^a(B_{8Sr_i}(a))+kappa r_i^2 with sup_a sum_i P_i(a)=o(1) by exact telescoping of volume ratios A_a(8Sr_i)-A_a(16Sr_i); Poisson, gradient and shifted-mass bounds linear in P_i.
why: Standard (Cheeger-Colding Poisson replacement; summability of volume pinching is classical in quantitative stratification).

name: Units of the Poisson estimates (pi:poisson-units)
statement: Rescaling; difference of two replacements is harmonic with Bochner mass <= C(P_i(x)+P_i(z)).
why: Routine.

name: Weak radial cancellation (pi:weak-cancellation)
statement: For f with constant Laplacian and a harmonic, g_a=<grad f, grad a> satisfies int<grad g_a, grad phi> = 2 int (Hess f - g)(grad a, grad phi).
why: Routine commutation identity.

name: Harmonic affine improvement (pi:affine-improvement)
statement: Harmonic w on B_{Sr_i}(a) is approximated on B_{S theta r_i} by an affine combination of u with factor theta^{3/2}/2.
why: Standard.

name: Summable radial invariance; defect functions E_i(a)=C_E sum_l 2^{-beta|i-l|} Ptilde_l(a) (pi:radial-invariance)
statement: E_i>=P_i, sup_a sum_i E_i(a)=o(1), positive floor; ||<grad fhat_i^a, grad U> - A_i^a(T)(U-U(a))||_{W^{1,2}(B_{S/2})} <= C sqrt(E_i(a)) with ||A-Id||=o(1). Inline defs g_b, e_j(b), Ptilde_i.
why: Variant of CJN21 sharp radial/cone-splitting machinery, with smoothing so that only sum E_i (not sum sqrt E_i) is needed.

name: Two-centre commutator (pi:commutator)
statement: v=f^z-f^x harmonic, |grad v|<=C, M(v)(B_{8R}(z))<=Cs^2 (s^2=E_i(x)+E_i(z)); h=<grad v, grad U> = U(x)-U(z) + O_{L^2}(s), via a commutator identity L_vL_zU - L_zh and a Sylvester-type bound ||B||<=Cs.
why: Quantitative two-point version of a Euclidean triviality; ingredients in CJN21.

name: Radial transport of an unnormalized residual (pi:radial-transport)
statement: If L_z w = w + l.U + k + e_w with ||e_w||<=C_1 s, ||w||_inf<=C_1, |l|+|k|<=C_1(alpha+s), alpha=||w||_{L^2(B_R)}, then ||w||_{L^2(B_{2R})}<=C(alpha+s); weighted radial cutoff phi with -t phi' - (a+2)phi >= |phi'|+phi.
why: Device is new as stated; technique (exponential radial weights for first-order transport) is standard.

name: Sharp approximation by the harmonic coordinate span (pi:sharp-projection)
statement: There is b, |b|<=C, with ||grad(v - b.U)||_{L^2(B_{2L+4}(y))} <= Cs (linear in s), by contradiction: normalized residual converges to a Euclidean harmonic w with X.grad w = w + affine, hence affine, contradicting orthogonality.
why: Close in method to CJN21 sharp splitting (linear Hessian bound by pinching).

name: Summable directional pinching (pi:directional-pinching)
statement: For fixed L,C_sep, for x,z,y in B_4(p) with d(x,y),d(z,y)<=C_sep r_i: D_{i,y}[u(x)-u(z)] <= C r_i^2 (E_i(x)+E_i(z)), with sup_x sum_i E_i(x) -> 0.
why: Close variant (one-direction, two-point, value-space form) of CJN21 sharp splitting estimates; paper itself names antecedents. Could be argued N3 for the 'evaluate mass on coordinate differences' reading.

name: Use with the heat-normalized matrices (pi:heat-interface)
statement: Q_i and R_i interchangeable up to constants; floor for centre selection.
why: Plumbing.

name: Value domain Omega=u(B_1(p)), P_x=u(x); frozen H_i/Q_i norms on vectors/covectors
statement: Construction lives in Euclidean value space; matrices frozen at P_x.
why: As an object, abbreviation; the representational choice is graded with I43/I47.

name: Quantitative inputs for Section 4 (monotone metrics, ellipsoid, cumulative, directional)
statement: Collects I13, I16, I22, I34 with fixed constants.
why: Restatement.

name: Gevrey-class bump psi with ||D^m psi|| <= C_b^{m+1}(m!)^s, s=2
statement: Gevrey cutoff from e^{-1/t}.
why: Standard.

name: Patches: maximal r_i-separated nets Y_i, value-space cutoffs phi_{i,y}(P)=psi(r_i^{-1}R_i(y)^{-1/2}(P-P_y)), active sets A_i(x), sums Z_i(x), S_i(x)
statement: Bounded overlap |A_i(x)|<=N; net point within r_i has phi=1 (weight-one centre).
why: Routine.

name: Fixed patch centres z_{i,y} nearly minimizing E_i on the patch, c_{i,y}=P_{z_{i,y}}
statement: E_i(z_{i,y}) < 2 inf_{x in T_{i,y}} E_i(x); positive floor guarantees existence; no measurable selection needed.
why: New small selection trick, part of the field construction (graded with I41).

name: Covector field v_i(P)=sum_y phi_{i,y}(P) D_{i,y}(P - c_{i,y})
statement: Smooth field whose derivative at P_x is S_i(x)+e(xi) and whose value is O(sqrt(eps) r sqrt(E)) in Q-norm.
why: Localized gradient of the quadratic potentials 1/2 D[P-c]; new as a device but simple once D_{i,y} and the directional estimate are given.

name: Field estimates (re:field-estimates)
statement: r^{-1}|v_i|_Q<=C sqrt(eps E); Dv_i xi = S xi + e(xi); |S xi|_Q<=sqrt(eps Z[xi]); |e|_Q<=C sqrt(eps E)|xi|_H; |xi^T e(xi)|<=C sqrt(Z[xi]E)|xi|_H; r|D^2 v(xi,xi)|_Q <= C(sqrt(Z[xi])|xi|_H + sqrt(E)|xi|_H^2); Gevrey jets eps C_v^{m+1}(m!)^s.
why: Direct consequences of I34 + positivity; the diagonal bound (Cauchy-Schwarz before summing) is the key subtlety.

name: Value-space renormalization iteration h_0=Id, h_{i+1}=h_i + (Dh_i)^{-T} v_i, with the exact metric-step identity |(J+DW)xi|^2-|J xi|^2 = 2 xi^T Dv xi - 2<D^2h(…
statement: The inverse transpose turns the leading derivative of v into a positive metric increment 2S_i; the only first-order error is the diagonal second-derivative term.
why: No neighbour found for a map built in coordinate-value space whose pullback metric accumulates per-scale Bochner mass forms; resembles Nash's positive-metric-increment iteration and Newton/gradient updates, but in a different setting and purpose.

name: Simultaneous metric + all-order Gevrey jet bootstrap: A^{-1}H_i <= J_i^TJ_i <= A H_i and r_i^{m-1}||D^m h_i||_{H_i->R^n} <= B^{m-1}(m!)^{1+sigma}
statement: IH carries all-order jet bounds to beat loss of one derivative per step.
why: Templated strengthening (capped at N2): Gevrey/analytic majorant bootstrap is standard for derivative loss.

name: Factorial convolution and inverse coefficients (re:inverse-majorant)
statement: With L_m=(m+1)((m+1)!)^sigma, sum L_l L_{m-l} <= C L_m and the inverse of J inherits jet bounds with the same base B.
why: Standard (Gevrey class algebra / majorant series).

name: One step for all jets (re:jet-step)
statement: Jet bounds propagate from level i to i+1 for eps small depending on A,sigma,B.
why: Routine majorant bookkeeping.

name: Uniform metric and jet bounds with the diagonal second-derivative recurrence (re:metric-iteration)
statement: b_i=r_i|D^2h_i(xi,xi)|/q_i obeys b_{i+1}<=b_i/2 + C_A f_i, f_i=sqrt(Z_i[xi])+sqrt(E_i)q_i; hence sum b_i^2 <= C_A H_k[xi] and ||J_k xi|^2 - |xi|^2 - 2 sum_{i<k} S_i[xi]| <= C_A(sqrt eps + eps) H_k[xi]; 'Only the sum of E_i has been used, never the sum of its square roots.'
why: The l^2 diagonal recurrence that pairs b_i with sqrt(E_i) q_i by Cauchy-Schwarz, so that only sum E_i is needed, is the decisive new estimate; no equivalent found.

name: The limiting chart (re:limit-chart)
statement: F=lim h_i o u is uniformly convergent with tail tau r_i; for x,z in B_rho(p), choose D t <= r_i < 2Dt, Taylor along segment in the central ellipsoid, metric bound and tails give (4 sqrt A)^{-1} d <= |F(x)-F(z)| <= 4 sqrt A d; invariance of domain gives open image.
why: Routine.

name: Proof of Thm main: constants depend only on n; L_n = 4 sqrt(A(n))
statement: Fix enlargements with n, s=sigma=2; choose a late rescaling; rescale chart back.
why: Routine.

name: Value-space renormalization: h_{i+1}=h_i+(Dh_i)^{-T}v_i with the l^2 diagonal second-derivative recurrence
why: Turns a non-summable first-order drift of the harmonic coordinates (H_k may be unbounded) into a realizable metric on a single map. The inverse transpose makes the leading change a positive sum of mass forms; the only first-order error is <D^2h(xi,xi), J^{-T}v>, handled by an l^2 recurrence that pairs with sqrt(E_i) q_i so that only sum E_i is needed. Nothing like it is in the goal or in L; it is exactly where the classical bi-Holder barrier (sum sqrt E_i = infinity) is crossed.

name: Summable directional pinching D_{i,y}[u(x)-u(z)] <= C r_i^2 (E_i(x)+E_i(z))
why: Evaluating the conjugated Bochner mass on actual coordinate differences, with a linear-in-s sharp projection and quadratic defect preservation (radial transport), is the input that makes the field small in a summable way.

name: Mass forms D_{i,y} on coordinate-value space and their two-sided cumulative comparison with H_k
why: The per-scale metric increment written as a quadratic form on values; non-commutative cumulative comparison without bounded H_k.

name: Non-commutative inverse-increment comparison C^{-1}H_k <= Id+sum H_iN_iH_i <= C H_k
why: Handles noncommuting heat Gram matrices across infinitely many scales with only slow-growth control.

name: Radial transport of an unnormalized residual
why: Keeps the defect quadratic (s^2) when normalizing a tiny residual; flagged by the authors as the step preserving the squared defect.

name: Value-space renormalization iteration with l^2 diagonal second-derivative recurrence
statement: Build smooth maps h_i on the value domain Omega=u(B_1(p)) by h_{i+1}=h_i+J_i^{-T}v_i, v_i=sum_y phi_{i,y}D_{i,y}(P-c_{i,y}). The inverse transpose makes |J_{i+1}xi|^2-|J_ixi|^2 = 2 xi^T Dv_i xi - 2<D^2h_i(xi,xi), J_i^{-T}v_i> + |DW xi|^2; with b_i=r_i|D^2h_i(xi,xi)|/q_i obeying b_{i+1}<=b_i/2+C(sqrt(Z_i[xi])+sqrt(E_i)q_i), all errors are summed using sum E_i only, giving J_k^TJ_k ~ H_k (possibly unbounded) and a bi-Lipschitz limit F=lim h_i o u.
why: No equivalent found in GMT (Toro/David-Toro), metric Reifenberg (GV25), Ricci-limit transformation theory (CN15, CJN21, HH24, HZ26) or Nash-type iterations. The decisive content is the pairing of (i) a value-space representation in which a non-summable first-order Gram drift becomes a positive metric increment and (ii) the l^2 diagonal recurrence that lets errors be summed with sum E_i instead of sum sqrt E_i. Risks: a judge may treat it as the David-Toro sigma_k construction plus a Newton-type…

name: Summable directional pinching (two-centre commutator + radial transport + sharp projection)
statement: D_{i,y}[u(x)-u(z)] <= C r_i^2 (E_i(x)+E_i(z)) for x,z,y within C_sep r_i, with sup_x sum_i E_i(x) -> 0: the normalized Bochner mass in the direction of actual coordinate differences is controlled by summable volume-pinching defects at the two points.
why: Close variant of CJN21 sharp splitting (named by the paper). The radial transport and the linear-rate sharp projection are careful new technique but not a new concept.

name: Mass forms D_{i,y} on coordinate-value space and their two-sided cumulative comparison with H_k
statement: D_{i,y}=R_i(y)^{-1}[r_i^{2-n}M(B_{Lr_i}(y))]R_i(y)^{-1}; for bounded weighted families of nearby centres, Id+sum Z_i <= C_* H_k and H_k <= C_*(Id+sum S_i).
why: Re-expression of known normalized energies plus a non-commutative telescoping that follows CJN21 Sec 8.

name: Non-commutative weighted inverse increments
statement: C^{-1}H_k <= Id+sum_{i<k} H_iN_iH_i <= C H_k and sum F_i[H_i xi] <= C H_k[xi], without commutativity and without bounded H_k.
why: Careful non-commutative extension of a named precedent.

name: Radial transport of an unnormalized residual
statement: For L_z w = w + l.U + k + e_w with bounded w, the L^2 norm on B_{2R} is controlled by the norm on B_R plus s, keeping the defect quadratic.
why: Technical device with a generic technique precedent; could be judged N1.

name: Summable radial invariance and smoothed defects E_i
statement: Radial derivatives of normalized coordinates are W^{1,2}-close to A(U-U(a)) with error sqrt(E_i(a)), E_i a geometric smoothing of the Poisson defects with sum E_i = o(1).
why: Variant of CJN21-type radial estimates; the smoothing that keeps only sum E_i is bookkeeping.

name: Gevrey all-order jet bootstrap (strengthened IH)
statement: Carry r_i^{m-1}||D^m h_i|| <= B^{m-1}(m!)^{1+sigma} in all orders to absorb the loss of one derivative per update.
why: Templated strengthening (capped at N2 anyway); a standard majorant device.

name: Near-minimizing fixed patch centres
statement: Choose z_{i,y} in each patch with E_i(z) < 2 inf E_i (positive floor guarantees existence) so the directional bound at any active point costs only E_i(x).
why: Small selection device; part of the C1 cluster's plumbing.

name: no conjugate points
statement: A metric has no conjugate points if no nonzero Jacobi field along a geodesic vanishes at two distinct times.
why: Textbook notion.

name: no focal points
statement: For every nonzero normal Jacobi field J along a unit-speed geodesic with J(0)=0, d/ds|J(s)|^2>0 for s>0.
why: Standard (O'Sullivan, Eberlein).

name: cometric P = Q^{-1}
statement: The inverse torus metric P(t)=Q(t)^{-1} of the neck metric dt^2+dx^T Q(t) dx; 'concave' means -P'' is positive semidefinite.
why: Renaming of the inverse metric tensor. The concavity requirement is graded separately (P19/P20).

name: manifold M: two copies of Sigma_{1,1} x S^1 glued by h2=h1+f1, f2=h1
statement: N_i = Sigma x S^1 (Sigma genus one, one boundary circle); gluing phi_* = [[1,1],[1,0]], det -1, so M is closed, connected, orientable; a product collar [0,1] x T^2 is inserted.
why: Explicitly cited as an instance of Leeb Example 4.1.

name: lattice and period choice B1 = eps*B2, end frames T1=(e1,e2), T2=(e2+eps e1, e1)
statement: On T^2=R^2/(Z B1 e1 + Z B2 e2) with B1=eps B2, the frames realise h1:B1e1, f1:B2e2, h2:B1e1+B2e2, f2:B1e1. The integral gluing [[1,1],[1,0]] becomes a coordinate swap plus a shear of size eps=delta^2.
why: Choosing the flat torus lattice to fit the gluing is standard in constructions of metrics on graph manifolds (Leeb; Buyalo-Svetlov). The specific swap+small-shear normalisation is new but it is one step from L.

name: pi_1 as amalgam and boundary-commutator relation
statement: G_i = F(a_i,b_i) x <f_i>, boundary groups inject, Gamma = G_1 *_{Z^2} G_2; G_i in C(f_i) and h_i in [C(f_i),C(f_i)].
why: Textbook.

name: Thm no-cat0-action
