statement: pi_1(M) admits no proper cocompact isometric action on a nonempty proper CAT(0) space. Proof: semisimplicity; flat torus theorem for Gamma_T; cyclic minset splitting Min(f_i)=Y_i x R with translation homomorphism tau_i vanishing on commutators; Pythagoras on a common flat gives <v(h_i),v(f_i)>=0; the gluing gives |u|^2=0.
why: Leeb1995 Ex 4.1 and KapovichLeeb1996 Thm 2.4 contain it; the paper says so.

name: Cor no-local-cat0
statement: M admits no locally CAT(0) length metric inducing its topology (metric Cartan-Hadamard + Hopf-Rinow + P07).
why: Standard corollary.

name: Prop no-npc
statement: M admits no smooth Riemannian metric of nonpositive sectional curvature (Riemannian NPC metric is locally CAT(0), BH II.1A.6).
why: Standard.

name: cutoff a(u)=exp(-1/(2/3-u)), primitive A, transition chi
statement: a smooth, vanishing for u>=2/3; A=int_0^u a; chi=0 on (-inf,5/12], 1 on [7/12,inf). Key property a^2 <= -a' and |a'|<=1 on [0,1].
why: Standard bump functions; only the inequality a^2<=-a' is problem-specific.

name: concave cometric path P(t)=d1 e1e1^T + d2 H H^T, H=e2+eps chi e1, d1=1+delta A(t), d2=1+delta A(1-t), eps=delta^2
statement: Diagonal concave variation of size delta, plus a shear of size delta^2 introduced only on [5/12,7/12] where both diagonal second derivatives are strictly negative. In the end frames P_i(tau)=diag(1+delta A(tau), b) exactly for tau<=1/4, P_i'(0)=kappa e1e1^T.
why: A neck metric dt^2+g(t) between two flat tori is the natural first try (the obstruction forces Q(0) and Q(1) to be different flat metrics). New: choosing the path so that its inverse is matrix-concave, with the shear subordinated (eps=delta^2) to the diagonal concavity. Close neighbour: warped/torus-bundle necks in Gulliver-type and graph-manifold constructions.

name: neck metric g=dt^2+dx^T Q(t) dx and endpoint germs
statement: Neck metric on [0,1] x T^2 in original and end coordinates; constants b=1+delta A(1), kappa=delta a(0).
why: Standard metric ansatz.

name: Lemma cometric-bounds (uniform bounds, concavity, domination)
statement: For 0<delta<=delta_0: Id/9 <= P <= 18 Id, Id/18 <= Q <= 9 Id, ||P'||<=C delta, -P''>=0 and |P'p|^2 <= C delta p^T(-P'')p, in original and both end frames; constants independent of B1,B2.
why: Routine to verify; the specific domination inequality is a new, designed hypothesis.

name: convex warped collars ell, k, r
statement: End surface metric dtau^2+ell_0^2 dy1^2 has K=-ell_0''/ell_0 <= 0; extended over [-1,0] by ell=exp(-int k), k=1-lambda+lambda r, so ell''=(k^2-k')ell>0, exactly matching (1+delta A)^{-1/2} near 0 and the hyperbolic cusp germ ell(-1)e^{-(tau+1)} near -1.
why: Standard warped-product gluing.

name: punctured-torus cores, hyperbolic cusp, final gluing; Appendix explicit punctured torus
statement: Truncate a complete finite-area hyperbolic punctured torus (ideal quadrilateral, side pairings phi(z)=(z+1)/(z+2), psi(z)=(z-1)/(2-z), peripheral element = [[1,6],[0,1]] up to sign) at horocycles of lengths B_i ell(-1); product with circles of length B_{3-i}; attach to neck. delta fixed first, then B2.
why: Textbook hyperbolic punctured torus.

name: index form I_J and normal index form I_J^perp
statement: I_J(V)=int_J(|D_sV|^2-<R(V,T)T,V>), q_V=<V,T>, I_J^perp = I_J - int |q_V'|^2.
why: Textbook; I^perp is the index of the normal part.

name: Lemma tangential-invariance
statement: I_J^perp(V+hT)=I_J^perp(V) pointwise for any smooth h, no endpoint condition.
why: Standard.

name: neck geodesic equations: p=Q xdot constant, F(t)=p^T P(t) p, v^2=1-F, vdot=-F'/2; F concave
statement: Momentum conservation in the cyclic torus variable; effective potential F is concave because P''<=0.
why: Standard conservation law; concavity of F is immediate from P11.

name: coordinate (linear) energy E_[a,c](V)=int(wdot^2+|zdot-P'p w|_Q^2 - F''w^2/2)
statement: Second derivative of energy along the coordinate-linear variation (t+rw, x+rz); every term is nonnegative because P is concave.
why: Transfer of the classical calculus-of-variations fact that a Lagrangian jointly convex in (position, velocity) has nonnegative second variation; the observation that concave cometric = joint convexity for dt^2+Q(t) is not cited and is the key change of representation (coordinate-linear instead of intrinsic variations).

name: Lemma coordinate-index (endpoint correction and boundary Christoffel term)
statement: I_[a,c](V)=E_[a,c](V)-[<T,Gamma(V,V)>]_a^c; at a neck boundary with w=0, Gamma(V,V)=(kappa/2) z1^2 d_tau, so the endpoint contribution is nonnegative at every entry and exit.
why: Textbook formula (do Carmo / Milnor) specialised; the nonnegativity of the boundary term, from P_i'(0)=kappa e1e1^T, is a designed feature of the construction.

name: neck passage
statement: A connected component J of {s : 0<t(gamma(s))<1}.
why: Abbreviation.

name: Lemma neck-passages (classification)
statement: Finite endpoints are transverse; a passage is (1) J=R at constant height, (2) monotone (crossing or half-infinite to an interior equilibrium), or (3) a symmetric return [0,L] with one turn at L/2, 0<F'<=kappa p1^2, p1 != 0, 0<v0^2<=kappa p1^2.
why: Routine phase-plane analysis.

name: Lemma elementary-passages
statement: I_J^perp(V)>=0 for J=R, monotone passages (gauge Vtilde=V-(w/v)T kills the interval component; Cauchy-Schwarz (p^T xi)^2 <= F |xi|_Q^2 with F<1), and returns inside an end collar (NPC).
why: Variant of the standard proof that monotone (graph-like) geodesics have no conjugate points; one step from P19/P20.

name: Lemma turning-gauge
statement: For every smooth V on a returning passage there is a tangentially equivalent field with w(0)=w(L)=0 and <V,T> affine; then I^perp = E + (kappa v0/2)(z1(0)^2+z1(L)^2) - (p^T Delta z)^2/L >= E + mu (e^T Delta z)^2 - (p^T Delta z)^2/L, mu=kappa v0/4.
why: A designed gauge; elementary once one decides to allow arbitrary endpoint data.

name: Lemma turning-time (chord bound and strict timing margin)
statement: int_0^L v^2 <= L v0^2/3 (v convex on the first half); if t_*>1/4 then 4 v0 <= beta kappa p1^2 L with beta=(1+exp(-9/26))/2<1, from a(1/8)/a(0)=exp(-9/26).
why: Elementary; the idea of a strict timing margin to get uniformity is the non-obvious part.

name: Hilbert space D=H_0^1(0,L) with (w1,w2)_D=int(w1'w2'-F''w1w2/2), functional Phi_q(w)=int q^T P'(t) p w, form S(q,r)=int q^T P r + (Phi_q,Phi_r)_{D*}
statement: Squared norm of the functional (xi,w) -> q^T X on L^2(Q) (+) D; positive definite.
why: Standard functional-analytic packaging of a Cauchy-Schwarz bound; new as applied here.

name: Lemma turning-duality
statement: |q^T X|^2 <= S(q,q) E; with the boundary penalty, |p^T X|^2 <= (S(p-alpha e,p-alpha e)+alpha^2/mu)(E+mu(e^T X)^2), minimised at alpha=S(p,e)/(S(e,e)+1/mu) to S(p,p)-S(p,e)^2/(S(e,e)+1/mu).
why: Cauchy-Schwarz and Schur complement; the content is in what it is applied to.

name: Lemma turning-S-bounds
statement: S(p,p)<=L(1+v0^2) (via Phi_p(w)=2 int v w'); S(e,e)<=C_e L (via domination); |S(p,e)-L p1| <= C_m delta L |p1| (via D(t)=P'(0)-P'(t)>=0 and Cauchy-Schwarz for the PSD form D).
why: Technical estimates; the |p1|-relative bound on the mixed term (exploiting P'(0)=kappa e e^T and concavity) is the clever part.

name: Prop turning-index (returning passages have I^perp>=0, uniformly)
statement: For all small delta, every returning passage has I^perp(V)>=0 for every smooth V with no endpoint restriction; delta<=min{1,1/(2C_m),(1-beta)/(2C_m+C_e a(0))} works for both ends, arbitrarily shallow incidence and arbitrarily long excursions.
why: No near-equivalent found in a quick search: Gulliver-type constructions control conjugate points by radial comparison/Riccati arguments in a ball, not by a free-endpoint index estimate summed over passages. Against: each ingredient (Cauchy-Schwarz, Schur complement, convexity of v) is elementary and the estimate is a one-off device for this metric; a judge may call it N2.

name: Prop passage-index (all neck passages)
statement: With delta as above and periods chosen afterwards, every passage J of every complete unit-speed geodesic has I_J^perp(V)>=0 and I_J(V)>=0.
why: Case assembly.

name: Prop global-assembly
statement: If K<=0 off an open set U and I_J(V)>=0 on every component J of gamma^{-1}(U), then I_R(V)>=0. Countable additivity; infinitely many passages allowed; per-passage gauges need not match.
why: The localisation principle (free-endpoint index nonnegativity on each visit to the bad region + NPC elsewhere) is natural but, as far as a quick search shows, not a stated tool; one step from L.

name: Lemma index-criterion
statement: If I_R(V)>=0 for all compactly supported smooth fields along all complete geodesics then no conjugate points (H^1 density, broken Jacobi field, derivative-jump contradiction).
why: Textbook Morse theory.

name: Thm main
statement: There is a closed connected orientable smooth 3-manifold with a C^infinity metric without conjugate points that admits no C^infinity metric of everywhere nonpositive sectional curvature.
why: Headline theorem, not graded.

name: No metric without focal points on M
statement: By IK Thm 7.1 (no focal points iff NPC for closed 3-manifolds) and Thm main.
why: Direct consequence of a cited theorem.

name: coordinate Riemannian geometry: metricMatrix, christoffel, curvatureCoefficient, curvatureTerm, NonpositiveSectionalCurvature, IsGeodesicOn, IsJacobiFieldOn, N…
statement: Chart-wise Christoffel symbols and Riemann tensor of a ContMDiffRiemannianMetric; NPC: g(R(u,v)v,u)<=0 in every atlas chart; geodesic/Jacobi equations in every atlas chart on an open interval U.
why: Coordinate definitions of textbook notions.

name: closedGeodesic_essential + ncp_exponential_isCoveringMap
statement: If g has no conjugate points, exp_p is a covering map (Hadamard-Cartan for no conjugate points), hence a nonconstant closed geodesic is not null-homotopic.
why: Classical.

name: fiberClass_ne_one via the constructed metric
statement: The circle fibre of each piece is a closed geodesic of realCompactMetric (which has no conjugate points), so by L02 its class in pi_1(M) is nontrivial.
why: Known principle (closed geodesics in NCP manifolds are essential) used as a shortcut around van Kampen; clever engineering, not new mathematics.

name: smooth Cartan-Hadamard: npc_exponential_isCoveringMap, exponentialMetric_expanding, npc_jacobiNorm_lower, universalMetric, universalMetric_radial_CN, universal…
statement: For an NPC metric, exp_p is a covering, the pulled-back length metric on E3 is proper and satisfies the Bruhat-Tits CN inequality; deck transformations act by isometries with attained minimal displacement.
why: Classical theorems formalized.

name: CNMidpoint.cyclic_shear_obstruction
statement: In a proper CN-midpoint metric space with linear geodesic segments, no isometries f,h (fixed-point free, nonempty minsets) can satisfy [f,h]=1, h=[a,b] with a,b in C(f), hf=[c,d] with c,d in C(h).
why: Variant of the Leeb/Kapovich-Leeb orthogonality argument using only common minimum points, axes and axis shifts (no flat torus theorem). The paper-style Euclidean orthogonality lemmas (NoNPC.shear_orthogonality_impossible, Distance.lean:574) are present but not on the proof DAG.

name: HyperbolicCore.Gamma = <phi,psi,-1> in SL(2,Z), Surface = H / Gamma, height, cusp, clipCusp
statement: Explicit model of the punctured torus; torsion-freeness/no elliptics via reductions mod 2 and mod 3 checked by decide.
why: Textbook model; decide used on finite group tables.

name: TwoGluing.Space / GluedConstruction.Manifold with collar im z in (2,8), collarFlip x->16/x, torusShear (z1,z2)->(z1+z2,z1)
statement: Gluing of two open pieces along a collar; compact, T2, connected, second countable, oriented (manifold_oriented, Gluing.lean:1541).
why: Formal realisation of P04.

name: DirectTurning.direct_pointwise_quadratic / direct_endpoint_cauchy / returning_endpoint_bound
statement: Pointwise quadratic inequality whose integral gives ((p-alpha e)^T X)^2 <= (int P(q,q)+4v^2+alpha^2 K)(int energy density), using p^T P' p = -2 vdot and integration by parts against w; then add the boundary term.
why: Simplification of the paper's dual-norm argument to an explicit pointwise Cauchy-Schwarz.

name: truncated_return_nonnegative / framed_truncated_return_index
statement: Returning-type estimate for a passage cut by the edge of a compact support window where the field vanishes.
why: Bookkeeping variant.

name: exists_uniform_compact_noConjugatePoints
statement: There is delta_0 in (0,1/2] such that realCompactMetric(delta) has no conjugate points for all delta<=delta_0.
why: Headline half.

name: Returning-passage free-endpoint index estimate
statement: For all sufficiently small delta, every returning neck passage [0,L] and every smooth field V (no endpoint condition) satisfy I^perp_[0,L](V) >= 0, uniformly in the entry angle, turning height and duration L. Proof: a gauge makes w(0)=w(L)=0 and <V,T> affine. The boundary Christoffel term then gives mu(e^T Delta z)^2. Cauchy-Schwarz in L^2(Q)+H_0^1 and a Schur complement reduce the claim to S(p,p) - S(p,e)^2/(S(e,e)+1/mu) <= L, which is closed by three S-bounds and a strict timing margin beta <…
why: No neighbour found (Test 1 passes), and it is load-bearing by knockout. But the statement is a localised, endpoint-free, uniform strengthening of the goal's own index-nonnegativity predicate. That is the 'uniform/quantitative version' and 'all substructures' strengthening templates by analogy (no induction is involved, and docs/templates.md does not exist), and family.md already noted this fit. Its proof is elementary once C2 and C3 are in place. The analyst's provisional 'N3 weak' is withdrawn…

name: Concave cometric => nonnegative coordinate second variation, with an engineered nonnegative boundary term
statement: For g = dt^2 + dx^T Q(t) dx with P = Q^{-1} concave, the second derivative of energy along coordinate-affine variations equals E = int(wdot^2 + |zdot - P'p w|_Q^2 - F'' w^2/2), a sum of nonnegative terms. The intrinsic index is I = E - [<T,Gamma(V,V)>]. Because P'(0) = kappa e1 e1^T at both ends, the endpoint term is >= 0 at every entry and exit when w = 0 there.
why: The nonnegativity of E is the second-order form of a classical convex-analysis theorem (joint convexity <=> concave-convex Hamiltonian; matrix-fractional convexity). That is N0 transfer, uncited in 358. What is new is the bridge (using it to certify no conjugate points across a positively curved neck) and the design of the end germs so that the intrinsic-coordinate discrepancy has a sign. Transfer plus problem-specific engineering gives N2. The analyst's 'N2 leaning N3' resolves to N2. It could…

name: Concave cometric neck path with delta/delta^2 scaling and the period trick B1 = delta^2 B2
statement: A smooth concave path of cometrics on [0,1] equals diag(1+delta A(tau), b) exactly near each end, with P'(0) = kappa e1e1^T. A shear of size delta^2 is introduced only on [5/12,7/12], where both diagonal second derivatives are strictly negative. Choosing the torus periods B1 = delta^2 B2 after delta turns the integral gluing [[1,1],[1,0]] into this coordinate swap plus a tiny shear.
why: Neck metrics between flat tori and choosing periods to realise gluings are standard (close variants). The specific scaling and ordering is new but designed to meet hypotheses that C2 and C1 set. It is a bespoke F3-type gadget whose difficulty is downstream of choosing C2. Graded N2, as the analyst did.

name: Localisation of the index form to neck passages with independent per-passage gauges
statement: If K <= 0 off an open set U and I^perp_J(V) >= 0 on every component J of gamma^{-1}(U) for every field (no endpoint condition), then I_R(V) >= 0. Countable additivity is used; gauges need not match between passages.
why: It conjoins two L-facts. Its only content is the decision to ask for free-endpoint estimates, which is credited to C1. Downgraded from the analyst's N2.

name: (Lean only) Cyclic shear obstruction in CN-midpoint spaces
statement: In a proper CN-midpoint space with linear geodesics, there are no isometries f, h with nonempty minsets satisfying [f,h] = 1, h = [a,b] with a,b in C(f), and hf = [c,d] with c,d in C(h). It uses only minsets, axes and axis shifts, with no flat torus theorem.
why: A leaner re-proof of a known obstruction in a weaker metric setting, produced as a Lean engineering choice. Close variant, not a new concept.

name: (Lean only) Fibre nontriviality via essential closed geodesics of the constructed metric
statement: The circle fibres are closed geodesics of the no-conjugate-points metric, hence not null-homotopic (exp is a covering map), so their classes in pi_1 are nontrivial.
why: A clever cross-use, but mathematically a corollary of a classical theorem. Downgraded from the analyst's N2.

name: Topological obstruction: the two-piece graph manifold with gluing h2 = h1 + f1, f2 = h1 has no NPC metric (and no proper cocompact CAT(0) action)
statement: pi_1(M) admits no proper cocompact isometric action on a proper CAT(0) space, so M has no NPC metric.
why: It is Leeb's Example 4.1, re-proved. The choice of the simplest non-base-preserving gluing is natural.

name: P29 (+P24-P28) returning-passage estimate
why: Nothing in L or the goal resembles a free-endpoint nonnegativity statement for the normal index along every returning geodesic segment through a positively curved neck, uniform in duration and incidence. It needs three coordinated insights: the boundary term controls only the e-component of the endpoint change; the mixed coefficient S(p,e) must be within O(delta|p1|) of L p1 (not O(delta|p|)); and a strict timing margin beta<1 for excursions leaving the end collar. The paper itself flags it as …

name: P19/P20 concave cometric => nonnegative coordinate second variation, with nonnegative boundary Christoffel term
why: The change of representation (second variation along coordinate-linear variations, where concavity of Q^{-1} makes it a sum of squares) turns a positively curved neck into one where the index form is 'almost' manifestly nonnegative; the defect is a single boundary term whose sign is engineered via P'(0)=kappa e1e1^T. It is not cited from anywhere and is the conceptual core.

name: P31 localisation of the index form to neck passages (with per-passage gauges)
why: Reduces a global question about Jacobi fields on all complete geodesics, with infinitely many visits, to independent free-endpoint estimates per visit; gauges need not match across passages.

name: P11/P05 cometric path with delta/delta^2 scaling and period choice B1=delta^2 B2
why: Realises an integral gluing that is far from the identity as a coordinate swap plus a tiny shear, so a concave path can do the job; the order (diagonal concavity first, shear only where both second derivatives are strictly negative) is what makes concavity possible.

name: L05 cyclic_shear_obstruction (Lean only) + L03 fibre nontriviality via closed geodesics
why: Avoids the flat torus theorem and van Kampen entirely; a leaner proof of the obstruction.

name: Signed-increment bootstrap with a two-term profile and the doubling argument
statement: There are M,A,P₀ such that for every dyadic P ≥ P₀ above 1024·(max momentum), every supported receiver, every dyad w and every interval with w/8 ≤ q_X ≤ 8w: |V_X(t₂)−V_X(t₁)| ≤ MP√(t₂−t₁) + A(t₂−t₁)P²log(2+P)/w. Doubling the maximal energy then takes time ≥ c/log P, and Σ1/log(2^n) diverges.
why: Capped at N2 as a templated strengthening: a uniform/quantitative momentum bootstrap carrying the receiver-energy scale. Independently downgraded by Wang's 2020/2026 velocity-characteristic bootstrap closed by signed time integration (in L via Wang 2026 I), and by Cheverry–Ibrahim's signed momentum increment. What is specific to 362 is the profile: a √I diffusive term plus I·P²L/w, tuned so that the doubling time is ≳ 1/log P and so buys exactly a divergent harmonic-log series. That is design, …

name: Signed force identity (transport + source-acceleration kernels = total derivative + residuals 𝓡 and 𝓐) and the weighted signed formula
statement: Along a retarded branch t = s + r of a source label, with d = 1−n·u, D = 1−n·a, e = 1−a·u and k0 = u−(e/D)n, the interior Lorentz-force kernel 𝒦 = −(H/r)∂_s^{(u)}g − Hg/(r²q²d) equals −(k0/(rd))′ + (e/(r²D²))(n/(q_X²D) − a) + n(a_t·k0)/(rD²). The residuals contain neither the source acceleration nor inverse powers of d. Integrated against Lipschitz endpoint-vanishing weights and a bounded C¹ matrix Π, this gives the weighted signed formula with an initial-cone boundary term.
why: Downgraded from the trace's N2–N3. For a stationary receiver the identity is the Heaviside–Feynman formula integrated in time (checked by hand). For a moving receiver it is that formula under the Lorentz force, plus a product-rule term. Its PDE role, signed time integration along the receiver with a receiver-acceleration residual at angle cost D⁻¹, is the Klainerman–Staffilani/Wang move, which is in L. New here: the physical-space retarded form, the exact absence of source acceleration and of i…

name: Direction-change count: the number of δ-exits of V/|V| on a stable window is ≤ C(M,A)L⁶/δ
statement: Assume the signed bootstrap. Take w ≥ P^{3/5}, an interval of length ≤ (w/P)² with q_X ∈ [w/8,8w], and w^{-3/5} ≤ δ ≤ w^{-1/10}. Then the greedy first-exit partition of the direction ξ = V_X/|V_X| at chordal scale δ has at most C(M,A)L⁶/δ pieces. Proof: on each complete piece a ramped weight ψ gives |∫ψ w ξ_t dt| ≥ wδ/2, and w ξ_t = ΠK with Π = wP_X/|V_X|. Apply the weighted signed formula with the fixed selection θ < κφ, pθ√h ≤ 1. Because the weights sum to ≤ 1, every bulk term over the union …
why: The only item with no neighbour found. It replaces an unattainable uniform directional modulus with a count of direction exits, bounded through the projected signed identity. That count is why the improved occupation, and hence the selection contradiction, works without symmetry. A Vlasov–Maxwell neighbour (Cheverry–Ibrahim) explicitly deemed direction control impractical. Against: the counting device is generic (greedy partitions, jump counting), and the trace reaches it in one propagation ste…

name: Direction-based occupation at intermediate angles (monotone crossing within combined direction cells)
statement: In small-sector bins with p,w ≥ P^{7/10} and j^{-49/100} ≤ φ ≤ j^{-4/25}, the hit measure satisfies 𝖬 ≤ C(h/p)φ^{-29/25}·max(1, I/I⁰_m, h/I⁰_m), with C independent of M,A. Proof: refine the source and receiver direction partitions (C3, with δ = c₂φ), discard hits that straddle a receiver boundary, and use a monotone crossing of e_F·(Y−X) at rate ≥ cφ inside each combined cell.
why: Pfaffelmoser's monotone crossing (in L), run on cells supplied by C3. Its novelty is inherited from C3, and it is scored with C3 as a cluster.

name: Summable selection rule and exponent contradiction for the receiver coefficient
statement: Select only those narrow-sector dyadic bins whose near/far direct bounds exceed P√I·W; the unselected bins sum to CP√I. On selected bins the receiver coefficient satisfies U ≤ w^{-1/2}W. The proof is by contradiction: an unsafe selected bin is forced into the actual regime and then into the improved-occupation window, where its exponent inequalities are incompatible. Summing exactly cancels the √w loss in ∫|K|.
why: The design insight is economical: improved occupation is needed only in a window, because selection forces every obstruction into it. But it follows from routine exponent bookkeeping once C2–C4 are in hand, so it is borderline N1. This is where the KS/Wang receiver-acceleration loss is closed without symmetry, the paper's real advance over Wang; that advance, however, rests on C3.

name: Cutoff-derivative cancellation for selected sums of a partition of unity
statement: ∂(Σ_{j∈S}β_j) = −Σ_{j∉S}∂β_j, supported where selected and unselected supports meet.
why: Plumbing; a negative control.

name: Endpoint-ramp closure of the bootstrap
statement: Weight with an endpoint-vanishing ramp ψ and bound the bulk by the selected estimate. Restore the edges by ∫χK = −∫χ′F, using the signed bootstrap on intervals of length ηI. Then choose η, M and A in that order and conclude by continuity.
why: A standard bootstrap closure. The edge restoration by signed anchoring is a small, natural trick.

name: Pfaffelmoser-type residence-time occupation on retarded bins, with a joint time-averaged energy budget
statement: Under the bootstrap, short cells of length λ keep source and receiver velocities stable, giving 𝖬 ≤ C(hk₁/p)·max(1, I/λ, h/λ). A time-averaged energy budget ℰ_{pφ} with Σℰ_{pφ} ≤ C makes the small sector summable.
why: Cross-field transfer (Vlasov–Poisson to retarded Vlasov–Maxwell) with substantial adaptation. The joint energy budget is borderline N2. Transfer never yields D3.

name: Finite-horizon field modification for the continuation criterion
statement: Keep the Coulomb field, cut off the vector potentials of the divergence-free remainders, and evolve the removed part as a vacuum Maxwell field that vanishes on the particle region up to the horizon (finite propagation). This puts C_b^∞∩L² data into the H⁵ class of the Luk–Strain form of Glassey–Strauss.
why: A routine repair of a hypothesis gap.

name: Retarded label change and moving-cone change of variables
statement: dz = d·dy·dv from retarded phase points to initial labels; dy = r²D dt dn; dt/ds = d/D.
why: Credited prior results.

name: Signed-increment bootstrap: |V_X(t2)-V_X(t1)| <= M P sqrt(t2-t1) + A (t2-t1) P^2 log(2+P)/w for receivers at energy ~ w, with the doubling argument (gaps >= c/…
against: A momentum-support bootstrap is the standard GS/Pfaffelmoser pattern; this is a 'uniform/quantitative version' of it, a templated strengthening capped at N2 by the codebook. Taking the norm after integration is a natural move once cancellation is sought. The doubling/divergent-sum step is classical.
why: Not a subterm of the goal: the GS route asks for a bound on sup |v|, not for an interval-uniform bound on the signed vector impulse with a sqrt(I) term and a receiver-energy-dependent linear term. Load-bearing: every later estimate assumes it (occupation stability, direction count, selection) and the closure improves it. Its log P time scale exactly balances the doubling argument; the two-term form is tuned, not generic.

name: Signed force identity: along a retarded source branch, the transport + source-acceleration kernel equals -(k0/(r d))' + geometric residual R + receiver-acceler…
against: Integration by parts along characteristics in the GS representation is classical; once one decides to integrate in s, the identity is a computation. The trace derives it at once, with no visible search: low pivot distance and evidence of reachability for the model. The model offers a physical reading (Lienard-Wiechert impulse), which suggests it is retrievable from physics intuition.
why: The paper names precedents for ingredients (GS representation, Luk-Strain energy flux, Pallard's orthogonality, Lazarovici's label change) but none for this identity. Decisive: it removes the sqrt(w) loss and is used twice (direction count with projection, and impulse on selected bins). Non-analytic: the residual with the receiver acceleration, and the cancellation of the transport kernel against the cone-geometry term, occur nowhere in the goal.

name: Direction-change count (number of delta-exits of V/|V| is <= C(M,A) L^6/delta, from the signed identity with Pi = w P_X/|V_X|) and the resulting direction-base…
against: Stopping-time counting is a standard device (cf. bounded-variation/oscillation counts). It is one propagation step from learned clause C4 (explicit at L82-83), which is evidence of reachability (low pivot distance).
why: Replaces an unattainable uniform modulus by a countable quantity derived from the bootstrap: a reformulation not suggested by the goal. Uses the signed identity a second time in a non-obvious way (perpendicular projection, weights with disjoint interiors). Load-bearing: without improved occupation, the exponent contradiction in Lemma sel:exponents fails.

name: Selection rule + exponent contradiction: select narrow-sector bins whose direct bounds exceed a summable threshold; show an unsafe selected bin is forced into …
against: Exponent bookkeeping over dyadic parameters is routine (a small linear-programming feasibility check). It depends on E1-E3 (chain depth 2).
why: The improved occupation needs to hold only in a window, because selection forces every potential obstruction into it: an economical design.

name: Field localization for the continuation criterion (Coulomb + truncated vector potentials + vacuum Maxwell)
against: Standard finite-propagation localization; no compression of the proof; it does not touch the main difficulty.
why: Removes a real gap between the problem's data class and the literature's H^5 hypothesis.

name: One-phase Bernoulli energy J(v;B) and global minimizer (ballwise, arbitrary nonnegative H^1 competitors with v-u in H^1_0(B))
statement: J(v;B)=int_B |grad v|^2 + 1_{v>0}; u>=0 in H^1_loc(R^d) is a global minimizer if J(u;B)<=J(v;B) for every ball B and nonnegative v with v-u in H^1_0(B).
why: Alt-Caffarelli 1981.

name: One-homogeneous; flat solutions (x.e)_+; critical dimension d_* (least dimension with a nonzero nonflat one-homogeneous global minimizer)
statement: u(rx)=r u(x) a.e.; flat = (x.e)_+, |e|=1; d_* = least d admitting a nonzero, nonflat, one-homogeneous global minimizer.
why: Standard critical-dimension notion (Weiss 1999; CJK 2004; Velichkov 2023 Ch. 10).

name: Local minimizer, blowup at a free-boundary point, regular vs singular points, Sing(u)
statement: Local minimizer in open D: same comparison on balls compactly in D; blowup = locally uniform limit of u(x0+rx)/r; regular if some blowup is flat.
why: Velichkov 2023 Ch. 6-10.

name: Regularity and blowups of minimizers (Lipschitz, nondegeneracy, compactness, homogeneous blowups, flat blowup => smooth free boundary with grad u = N_E)
statement: (i) locally Lipschitz, harmonic in {u>0}; (ii) blowup sequences subconverge to nonzero one-homogeneous global minimizers; (iii) a flat blowup gives a smooth one-sided free boundary with u=0, grad u=N_E.
why: Pure citation; the paper only checks hypotheses (one-phase as a two-phase viscosity solution with G(b)=1+b).

name: Translation invariance of an off-origin blowup of a one-homogeneous minimizer
statement: If u is one-homogeneous and 0!=x0 in free boundary, any blowup U satisfies U(y+t x0)=U(y).
why: Standard dimension-reduction lemma (Federer/Weiss; Velichkov 10.9).

name: Minimality of a translation-invariant factor
statement: If U(y,s)=v(y) is a global minimizer in R^k x R then v is a global minimizer in R^k (cutoff eta_L in s; energy gain 2L delta beats bounded transition cost).
why: Standard.

name: Flatness in dimension one
statement: Nonnegative 1-homogeneous minimizers on R are b x_+ with b=1 (two slopes ruled out by a bump; b=1 from a translation family).
why: Folklore (Alt-Caffarelli).

name: Smooth original link: on a first nonflat cone in d in {5,6}, every nonzero free-boundary point is regular; link components are smooth domains with Delta g=-m g…
statement: Assume d=d_* in {5,6}; fix a nonzero nonflat 1-homogeneous minimizer u; off-origin blowups are (d-1)-dimensional minimizers times R, hence flat; so the spherical positive set has finitely many smooth components with the overdetermined Bernoulli boundary conditions.
why: Standard minimal-dimension/dimension-reduction argument.

name: Selection of a nonflat component (T_o = Hess g_o + g_o Id not identically zero on some component)
statement: If T_o vanished on every component, each positive cone is a half-space with |b|=1, and disjoint closures force a single half-space, contradicting nonflatness.
why: Routine.

name: Suspension preserves global minimality; suspended link on S^5 with two singular tips p_+-; g~(Phi(t,y))=sin t g_o(y)
statement: u minimizer in R^k => u(x,s)=u(x) minimizer in R^{k+1}; for the d=5 cone, the singular set of the product is the axis, meeting S^5 only at two tips; the link component is the spherical suspension of Omega_o.
why: Minimality of cylinders is classical (also used in Cor 1.2 sharpness and in dimension-reduction literature); the unification is a convenience, not a large budget drop (alternative: a second certificate on S^4 with constant 9/4).

name: Working domain: Omega in S^5 = Omega_o (m_o=5) or its suspension (m_o=4); Sigma = tips; regular boundary
statement: Fix Omega subset S^5 connected, from a nonnegative 1-homogeneous global minimizer in R^6; tests supported away from Sigma.
why: Notation.

name: Spherical jet data p=grad g, T=Hess g+g Id, B=grad T, w=|T|, s^2=g^2+|p|^2
statement: T is the tangential block of r D^2u; s^2=|D u|^2 on the sphere.

name: Interior identities: T symmetric trace-free Codazzi; B fully symmetric trace-free; Ricci commutator for B; Delta T=mT; Delta w^2=2m w^2+2|B|^2; Delta s^2=2w^2;…
statement: Spherical Simons/Bochner-type identities for g with Delta g=-mg.
why: Simons 1968 / JS 2015 Prop 3.1 style identities.

name: Strict gradient bound s_o^2<1 inside; H_o>0, T_o p_o=-H_o p_o, w_o>0 on the boundary
statement: Subharmonicity of s^2 and Hopf lemma.
why: Same argument as JS 2015 Sec 2.2.

name: Boundary jets: T_{N alpha}=0, T_{alpha beta}=second fundamental form, H=tr h; odd-normal components of B determined pointwise (B_{N alpha beta}=T_NN T_ab-(T^2)…
statement: Odd-normal part of B/w^2 equals V built from (A,p).
why: JS 2015 eq. (2.2) contains the odd-normal jet identities; V is a coordinate-free repackaging.

name: Suspended data: T~=rho^{-1}T_o, B~ components, w~=rho^{-1}w_o, |B~|^2=rho^{-4}(|B_o|^2+3c^2 w_o^2), H~=rho^{-1}H_o, measures rho^4 dt dV_o
statement: Warped-product computation for the suspension.
why: Routine.

name: Euclidean stability on a component: int_D |grad phi|^2 >= int_{dD} H_E phi^2 for smooth phi compactly supported away from vertex/singular points, arbitrary tra…
statement: Second variation of J under (F+eps phi)_+ competitor.

name: Spherical stability on S^5: int_{dOmega} H v^2 <= int_Omega |grad v|^2 + 4 v^2
statement: Separation of variables plus sharp radial Hardy constant beta^2=((m-1)/2)^2=4 for m=5.
why: JS 2015 Prop 2.1.

name: Constants a=29/50, Q=250000, eps_*=438907/12000000, delta_*=6984137359/31250000000; STF^r(R^5)
statement: Fixed rational parameters of the certificate; a in (1/2,1).
why: Parameter choice.

name: Formal normalized derivation D_l on tensor polynomials in (A,p,g,delta): D_l A=X_l - q_l A, D_l p=wA - g z delta, D_l g=z p, with free STF three-tensor X and f…
statement: Jet-space encoding of covariant differentiation of functions of the normalized Hessian shape A=T/w, with q_l=X_lij A_ij = grad log w.
why: Jet-space/Lie-derivative encodings of differential inequalities for SOS are known (Valmorbida-Ahmadi-Papachristodoulou; Chernyshenko et al. auxiliary-function SOS); normalization by w is new to this problem.

name: Universal algebraic certificate: there are rational equivariant tensor polynomials f,U,K,M,P (Table I, 231 rows) such that the interior polynomial I >= eps_*(z…
statement: I = z^2[5 U:A + C(delta A+delta A) - 4f] + [D G + (2a-1) q G]:X + w[D M + (2a+1) q M] + z[D P + 2a q P] + f|ell|^2 - (D f + 2a q f).ell >= eps_*(z^2+|ell|^2); S = -lambda f + U:(S_0+p p) + C p V + p.M >= delta_*.
why: No neighbour found in quick searches (JS 2015 uses w^alpha and w^2=sum lambda_+^2 + a sum lambda_-^2, subsolution form; FR-Serra 2026 is dim 4 stable solutions; SOS-Lyapunov PDE literature is control-theoretic). Paper names JS as precedent for 'functions of the Hessian' and Parrilo for Gram certificates.

name: Flux pair: h = w^a sqrt(f(A,p,g)), Z_l = w^{2a}(G_lijk X_ijk + w M_l + P_l), G_lijk = delta_li U_jk + C_lijk, C_lijk = K_lijk - K_iljk
statement: Scalar test h and vector field Z built from the normalized Hessian shape, g, grad g and grad T/w; target inequalities div Z >= |grad h|^2+4h^2+eps w^{2a} in Omega_+, N.Z + H h^2 >= 0 on the regular boundary.
why: Closest: JS 2015 Sec 3-4 (v=w^alpha; w^2 = sum lambda_+^2 + a sum lambda_-^2), a strict subsolution criterion (Prop 2.1-2.2). New: (i) a non-gradient flux Z, (ii) dependence on g and grad g (not only Hessian eigenvalues), (iii) free coefficient polynomials found by certificate.

name: Normalized differentiation and fourth-derivative elimination: (1/w) G_lijk grad_l B_ijk = 5 U:A + C_lijk(delta_lj A_ik + delta_lk A_ij)
statement: Choosing G = delta U + (skew in l,i) makes every undetermined fourth derivative of g drop out, via Delta T = 5T and the Ricci commutator of B.
why: Null-Lagrangian / divergence-structure ideas are classical (Weitzenbock, Codazzi, Simons); the restriction of the ansatz is a careful but natural engineering step once one seeks a flux of B.

name: Interior comparison div Z >= 4h^2 + |grad h|^2 + eps_* w^{2a}, via the exact divergence identity and completing the square in the free vector ell
why: Mechanical given P21/P22 (square completion is the standard way |grad sqrt f|^2 is linearized).

name: Boundary reflection parity: F=p_l G_lijk changes sign under reflection in p^perp, so it kills all even-normal (undetermined) components of B; p.G.B/w^2 = U:(S_…
statement: Orthogonal equivariance + evenness of U,K in p => F has only odd-normal components; those of B/w^2 equal V.
why: Standard symmetry argument used as a design constraint.

name: Boundary comparison: N.Z + H h^2 = w^{2a+1} S >= delta_* w^{2a+1} > 0
statement: Uses P=0 at g=0, P25, and the boundary certificate.
why: Mechanical given P21/P25.

name: Uniform field bounds |h|<=Cw^a, |grad h|, |Z| <= C w^a (resp. w^{2a})(1+w+|X|)
statement: Compactness of the coefficient domain.
why: Routine.

name: Tensor-monomial graph encoding (digit triples: g^h (tr A^3)^b w/z; edges carrying A^k between slots/p/ell/X) and Tables I/II
statement: Finite specification of f,U,K,M,P (231 rows) and of 21 Gram blocks (557 rows).
why: Plumbing.

name: Gram-block comparison forms with scaled projections (sym2, sym3, hook, anti) are PSD; Gamma >= 0 when chi >= 0
statement: Gram-matrix (SOS) certificate in tensor variables; hook projection onto trace-free (2,1)-Young component.
why: Parrilo 2003 Gram-matrix method; Young-symmetrizer projections.

name: Closure of the graph calculation (finite, degree two in (w,z,ell,X), at most two copies of X)
statement: Contraction/differentiation rules on graph keys are exact and terminate.
why: Plumbing.

name: Tensor bounds: ||A||_op^2<=4/5, |A^k|^2<=theta^{k-1}, |tr A^3|^2<=9/20, |X:A|^2<=(5/7)|X|^2, mixed g/p bound
statement: Elementary eigenvalue/Lagrange-multiplier bounds for unit STF A in R^5 and STF projection bound.
why: Folklore (e.g. Okumura-type trace inequality |tr A^3| <= (n-2)/sqrt(n(n-1)) |A|^3).

name: Complete graph bound |M(t)| <= L_t y_i y_j for every retained scalar graph
statement: Classification of graph components with at most two cubic vertices; Cauchy-Schwarz with operator norms.
why: Routine.

name: Interior remainder and coercive margin: E = Gamma + sum d_i y_i^2 - I has 1714 nonzero keys; |E| <= y^T D0 y <= y^T Dbar y; slacks with nu=(2484,1440,996,304) …
statement: Exact rational arithmetic; this report re-checked the ten D0<=Dbar comparisons, the four slacks and delta_* from the printed integers.
why: Verification step of P21.

name: Boundary reduction to four tangential eigenvalues; E_b has eleven symmetric-monomial coefficients; S >= 1/4 - 1656725282/Q^2 = delta_*
statement: p=e_5, A=diag(x_1..x_4,lambda), lambda=-sum x_i; Lambda >= 0 when sum x_i >= 0.
why: Verification step of P21.

name: Weighted Bochner estimate: int w_o^{2a-2}|B_o|^2 < infinity for a in (1/2,1), via W_delta = w_o^2 + delta and absorption (4a-2 = 8/25)
statement: Regularized Bochner identity integrated against a cutoff controls derivatives near Hessian zeros without any structure of the zero set.
why: Standard regularization (delta-regularized Bochner, absorption with exponent > 1/2).

name: Product cutoffs xi_j = theta(j w_o) [times theta(j sin t) in the suspension]
statement: Smooth cutoffs vanishing near Hessian zeros and near tips.
why: Routine.

name: Integrated comparison: eps_* int xi^2 w^{2a} <= int (h^2|grad xi|^2 + 2 xi h grad h.grad xi - 2 xi Z.grad xi)
statement: Combine P24, divergence theorem, P26 and P18 applied to v=xi h.
why: Routine assembly.

name: Vanishing of all three cutoff errors by dominated convergence (dominator C D_o, resp. s_t^{2-2a} D_o in the suspension; 21/25 > -1)
statement: Explicit suspension scaling makes the tip errors integrable.
why: Routine.

name: Exclusion: the first dimension admitting a nonflat one-homogeneous global minimizer is not 5 or 6
statement: Positive mass I_o = int w_o^{2a} > 0 (resp. times int sin^{71/25}) contradicts P37 after j -> infinity.
why: Target.

name: Sharp singular-set bound: Sing empty for n<=6, locally finite for n=7, dim_H <= n-7, attained by DJ cone x R^{n-7}
statement: Weiss dimension reduction with d_*=7; sharpness by products with the De Silva-Jerison cone.
why: Standard.

name: Main theorem: every nonzero 1-homogeneous global minimizer in R^d, d<=6, is flat; there is a nonflat one in R^7; d_*=7
statement: Combine JS (d_*>=5), DJ (d_*<=7) and P39.
why: Target.

name: Model: Test, WeakGradient, H1, H10, H1Loc, energy, LocalMinimizer, GlobalMinimizer, OneHomogeneous, Nonzero, Flat
statement: Ad hoc Sobolev model on EuclideanSpace R (Fin d).
why: Faithful encodings of standard notions; Mathlib lacks H^1.

name: De Silva-Jerison profile: f(t) = (8-25t^2+15t^4)/(8(1-t^2)^2) - (15/8) t artanh t solving (1-t^2)f''-6tf'+6f=0, root t7, c7, kappa, p, Z(x)=|x| p(x_7/|x|), U=k…
statement: The DJ cone.
why: De Silva-Jerison 2009.

name: U_global_minimizer: split any competitor v into max(v,U) and min(v,U) (Sobolev lattice identity) and apply upper and lower comparisons
statement: energy(m)+energy(p)=energy(U)+energy(v) with p=U+(v-U)_+, m=U-(U-v)_+.
why: Standard.

name: U_upper_comparison via a calibrated foliation by homothetic upper barriers (upperFamily, upperParameter, upperCalibration) with an explicit glued cap/exterior …
statement: Calibration (divergence of the foliation's gradient field with nonpositive seam flux) proves U <= any upper competitor in energy.
cited_or_new: cited method (DJ 2009 foliation), explicit barriers new to the formalization
why: Formalization of DJ 2009's minimality proof; barrier details possibly re-engineered (N1-N2), but the result is known and the method is DJ's.

name: U_lower_comparison via Picone ground-state inequality (picone_test, picone_h10_eLpNorm) on the positive cone
statement: Competitors below U cannot lower energy: ground-state square completion with the positive superharmonic barrier.
why: Picone (1910) / ground-state transform.

name: SobolevCalculus: positive part preserves H10, gradient zero a.e. on level sets, lattice operations (2,035 lines)
statement: Standard Sobolev facts built from scratch.
why: Textbook Sobolev facts absent from Mathlib.

name: ThresholdRecovery.upper_variation_of_threshold_tests: comparison against smooth threshold tests extends to all H10 competitors
statement: Approximation step from smooth tests to Sobolev competitors.
why: Routine density.

id: P22 + P21 (flux pair (h,Z) with a unive…
why: Directly overcomes the obstruction JS 2015 Sec 3.2 identified for 4<=n<=6: the interior and boundary constraints on a single Hessian-power test are optimized by different configurations. Here a non-gradient flux Z decouples the two (interior: div Z; boundary: N.Z), so the same tensor data serve both. Non-analytic: neither f,U,K,M,P nor Z occurs in the goal, in Mathlib, or in the bibliography; JS's tests are scalar functions of Hessian eigenvalues with the subsolution form (equivalent to Z = h g…

Key enabling design constraint: only the Laplacian contraction and the (l,i)-skew contraction of grad B are controlled by identities, so restricting the flux to these makes div Z a function of the 3-jet. Not a subterm of the goal.
Makes the boundary inequality pointwise in (A,p) without knowing tangential derivatives of curvature (which JS handle only via the specific scalar w).
Allows one certificate (m=5, Hardy constant 4) for both dimensions; tips handled by an integrable power sin^{21/25}.
Removes all regularity assumptions on the Hessian zero set.

name: Flux pair (h = w^a sqrt f, Z = w^{2a}(G:X + wM + P)) with the universal equivariant tensor certificate (f,U,K,M,P; Prop 4.1)
statement: There exist rational O(5)-equivariant tensor polynomials f,U,K,M,P in (A,p,g) (A unit STF 5x5, g^2+|p|^2<=1) such that, with G = delta U + (K - K^(12)), h = w^a sqrt f and Z = w^{2a}(G:X + wM + P), on any smooth link of a nonflat one-homogeneous Bernoulli solution in S^5: div Z >= |grad h|^2 + 4h^2 + eps_* w^{2a} and N.Z + H h^2 >= delta_* w^{2a+1}; combined with stability this is a contradiction.
why: Passes tests 1-3 on searches named above: no near-equivalent object, non-analytic, fully load-bearing. Not a templated strengthening (no induction). Downgrade risks are real: (i) the paper names JS's Hessian-function tests as the precedent and C1 is, conceptually, 'JS with a flux and a computer search'; (ii) the meta-method is an import (SOS auxiliary functions), so a strict judge could call the IDEA N2 and the OBJECT a search output; (iii) correctness rests on unrefereed, uncompiled-in-Lean, c…

name: Fourth-derivative elimination: restricting the flux to G = delta U + (l,i)-skew C so that (1/w) G:grad B = 5U:A + C(delta A + delta A)
statement: Only the Laplacian contraction (Delta T = 5T) and the (l,i)-antisymmetric part (Ricci commutator) of grad B are determined by the jets; choosing G in this span makes div Z a function of the 3-jet.
why: Natural engineering step for anyone who writes a flux linear in grad T; uses classical identities. Capped as variant of null-Lagrangian design.

name: Boundary reflection parity: equivariance + evenness of U,K in p kills undetermined even-normal jets in p.G.B
statement: F = p_l G_lijk is odd under reflection in p-perp, so it pairs only with odd-normal components of B/w^2, which equal V(A,p).
why: Variant of standard symmetry reasoning; could be N1. Load-bearing only as part of C1.

name: Normalized jet derivation D_l (A = T/w on the unit sphere of STF^2, q = X:A = grad log w, free X, w, z homogenizer, free ell)
statement: Encodes covariant differentiation of functions of the normalized Hessian shape as a formal derivation in free variables, turning the PDE inequalities into a single polynomial inequality.
why: Formal-jet encoding is standard in SOS PDE work; normalization by w mirrors JS's log w.

name: Suspension unification: d=5 cone suspended to R^6 so both cases live on S^5 (Hardy constant 4) with two tips, handled by sin^{21/25} integrability
statement: Products u(x,s)=u(x) of minimizers are minimizers; the suspended link carries all tensor identities with m=5.
why: Standard device.

name: domain; Sobolev homeomorphism; fixed-target approximation
statement: Domain = nonempty connected open set; fixed-target problem asks for diffeomorphisms f_j: Omega->Lambda with f_j-f, Df_j-Df -> 0 in L^p, each f_j onto exactly Lambda.
why: Problem statement (Ball 2001).

name: Main theorem 1<=p<=2
statement: Bounded domains Omega,Lambda in R^3, 1<=p<=2, homeomorphism f in W^{1,p}: there are C^infty diffeomorphisms f_j:Omega->Lambda in W^{1,p} with int |f_j-f|^p+|Df_j-Df|^p -> 0.
why: Goal; grading applies to its proof items.

name: fine value tolerance; absolute constants
statement: Fine value tolerance = positive continuous function on U; absolute constant depends only on dimension and fixed reference shapes.
why: Renaming of standard notions.

name: Local tolerances (Lipschitz/smooth positive minorants)
statement: Positive L-Lipschitz minorants d<=min{a,1,L dist}, smooth minorants with value/derivative bounds, summable budgets on exhaustions.
why: Inf-convolution / partition of unity, textbook.

name: Straight-homotopy properness
statement: |G-H|<dist(H,complement)/2 makes straight homotopy proper in V.
why: Folklore degree argument.

name: Fine relative PL approximation
statement: Homeomorphism of PL 3-manifolds, PL near closed K, has fine PL approximation agreeing near K.
why: Restatement of Hamilton/Moise relative approximation.

name: Strong smoothing of locally bi-Lipschitz maps
statement: Locally bi-Lipschitz W^{1,p} homeomorphism H:Omega->Omega' admits diffeomorphism g onto Omega' with ||g-H||_{W^{1,p}}<eps and fine value control, all 1<=p<infty.
cited_or_new: new (partly overlapping CampbellDOnofrioVitek2026 Thm A for PL->smooth)
why: PL->diffeo half is CDV 2026 Thm A (N0); the bi-Lipschitz->PL half with strong derivative control is a variant of Vaisala 1977 PL approximation of lipeomorphisms.

name: Small local ambient extension (Edwards-Kirby)
statement: Close embedding equal to Id on D cup dB extends to ambient homeo, = e on C, Id outside B, uniform delta over finite configuration list.
why: Corollary of Edwards-Kirby deformation theorem.

name: Fine control, properness, and the target
statement: Smooth g with det Dg>0 and |g-h|<dist(h,dLambda)/2 is a diffeomorphism onto Omega'.
why: Standard degree argument.

name: Strong PL smoothing (edge tubes, variable convolution, Smale vertex isotopy)
statement: Locally finite PL homeomorphism in W^{1,p} smoothed with summable errors: edge tube radial interpolation to affine axis model; variable-radius convolution (convex hull of gradients in GL^+ via rank-one face jumps); vertex homogeneous maps isotoped to rotation by Smale.
cited_or_new: new local proof; same result in CDV 2026 Thm A
why: Known result (CDV 2026, Mora-Corral-Pratelli 2014 planar); techniques standard (rank-one convexity of det along face jumps).

name: Rank-one face-jump determinant identity
statement: det((1-t)A_- + tA_+) = (1-t)det A_- + t det A_+ when A_+-A_- has rank <=1.
why: Affinity of det along rank-one lines.

name: Adapted dyadic meshes
statement: Locally finite dyadic Whitney-type decomposition with finite normalized configuration list, n_0-colouring, coarse index graph.
why: Whitney decomposition + colouring.

name: Insertion with protected cores
statement: Given homeomorphism G and PL embedding h_Q close to H at scale l_Q, an ambient homeo A supported in B_Q(5) installs G∘A=h_Q near B_Q(2) keeping older cores; tolerance independent of derivatives.
why: Direct corollary of M1-08 plus bi-Lipschitz of H.

name: Strong PL approximation via finite PL libraries chosen before resolution
statement: Bin normalized H-maps into finitely many sup-norm classes per coarse index; choose one PL model per (configuration, bin, protected data) combination before the final mesh; fixes derivative bounds M_P before bad-cube measure is made small; good cubes keep affine interpolation L.
why: Paper names the precedent (Vaisala 1977 / Carleson). New: combination with strong W^{1,p} accounting and order of choices.

name: Essential tangential compatibility
statement: Lipschitz v on polygonal disk/cell: interior a.e. essential limits of Dv; boundary-direction derivatives have essential limits equal to boundary restriction derivative.
why: Technical hypothesis bundling standard notions.

name: Compatibility of finite closed-piece formulas
statement: Maps given by finitely many C^1 closed-piece formulas have M1-15.
why: Density-point argument.

name: Boundary-parametrized disk estimate (weak and sharp)
statement: Weak: reparametrization fixing dQ with int|D(h∘rho)|^2 <= C(Area+boundary energy)+eps. Sharp: area<=1+o(1), boundary -> square boundary => D(h_j∘rho_j)->D iota in L^2. Proof: dominating metric conformal on collar, Ahlfors-Bers uniformization to rectangle, coordinate rigidity.
why: Morrey eps-conformal parametrization (named precedent) plus boundary agreement; sharp rigidity is a standard energy=2 area argument.

name: Cell collapse (subcritical radial reparametrization)
statement: For p<m (m=2,3), bi-Lipschitz reparametrization F of H(D) with F=H∘sigma on boundary and int|DF|^p <= C l int_{dD}|D_t(H∘sigma)|^p + eps.
why: Homogeneous radial extension estimate with injective reparametrization; standard for p<m.

name: Cleaning an isolated crossing
statement: Isolated crossing of locally flat disk with tame interval made empty or single standard transverse crossing by small ambient modification (cylinder surgery, linking, Schoenflies).
why: Standard innermost-disk surgery.

name: Affine germs at cleaned crossings
statement: After cleaning, homeomorphism can be made affine near each retained crossing.
why: Schoenflies extension.

name: Two-point cut of an unknot
statement: Ball meeting a tame unknot in two transverse points: arc is boundary-parallel.
why: Standard.

name: Sphere crossing radial strands once (punctured product)
statement: Region between inner sphere and locally flat sphere S crossing n>=3 radial strands once is a product of pairs; boundary map homotopic to radial projection rel marked points.
why: Standard product recognition.

name: Replacement at a star center
statement: Local homeomorphism with marked forward/reverse ray germs in narrow cones and angular loop tests can be modified near 0 to equal Id as germ.
why: Germ-straightening via mapping class group of punctured sphere; standard tools, new packaging.

name: Relative regularization with protected germs
statement: Fine locally bi-Lipschitz approximation retaining exact germs, crossing counts, angular conditions.
why: Corollary.

name: Generic trace properties
statement: For a.e. translation of Lipschitz semialgebraic templates (curves; surfaces if p=2), f-images rectifiable with area formula, regular branches at complementary-dimensional hits.
why: Sobolev slicing + CHM Lusin on planes.

name: Target mesh with lattice patches (jittered Delaunay)
statement: Random locally finite triangulations with lattice (Kuhn) patches; joint density bound q(t,z)<=Cd^{-3} for translation + relative coordinates.
why: Jittered Delaunay + change of variables.

name: Tie budget (dual strata by barycentric leader ties)
statement: Z_{sigma,I} = points where coordinates in I tie for maximum; budget B_m(Gamma) = sum over trace visits to complementary-dimensional Z of H^m(conv{v_i: i in I}).
why: Close variant of the dual-skeleton intersection count in the Federer-Fleming deformation theorem (cited White 1999).

name: Compatible simplex squeeze (variable softmax)
statement: T_i(lambda)=lambda_i e^{a lambda_i}/sum lambda_j e^{a lambda_j}, a=e^{1/b}-e with b a face-compatible min; face-preserving locally bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism; m-Jacobian of T∘G converges to tie budget as floors of a -> infinity.
why: Realizes Federer-Fleming-type pushing by a homeomorphism (softmax tempering); novel device but close in role to radial projection from dual skeleton.

name: Topological transfer of trace budgets
statement: Onto locally bi-Lipschitz H_0=T∘G close to f whose image lengths/areas on measured traces are <= tie budgets + eps, retaining protected germs.
why: Composite of M1-27/28 with topological cleaning; its novelty is that of M1-28.

name: Expected budgets
statement: E B_m(Gamma) <= C int J_m D(f∘P).
why: Standard averaging, as in Federer-Fleming.

name: Length budgets with high probability
statement: B_1(Gamma) <= C length(Gamma)+e with probability >=1-delta (graph decomposition, monotone crossing).
why: Elementary refinement of expectation bound.

name: Sharp costs along a thin-grid subspace
statement: Anisotropic Kuhn lattice (side d along E, eta d across): tie-budget coefficient on tangent k-vectors <= 1+C eta (degree-one torus map argument).
why: Clever computation; neighbour: anisotropic grids in Hencl-Pratelli planar W^{1,1} proof.

name: Shape-controlled source sampling
statement: Random source meshes with uniform shapes, E sum l_F^{3-m} int_F g <= C int g.
why: Standard.

name: Tangential composition limit
statement: q_j->q_0 with a.e. derivative convergence and bounds; v piecewise C^1: D(v∘q_j)->D(v∘q_0) in L^r, no rank assumption.
why: Dominated convergence.

name: Low-exponent approximation by locally bi-Lipschitz homeomorphisms
statement: 1<=p<=2: f approximated strongly by locally bi-Lipschitz H onto Omega'.
why: Goal-shaped intermediate.

name: Radial block construction (full rank; rank-two planar p<2)
statement: Random centres in compact jet sets, exact germ via star replacement, radial expansion so map = chart b on core; spokes contracted; at p=2 reverse rays (inverse BV, CHM Thm 1.1) and angular attenuation with determinant calculation; weight W fixed before budget.
why: Radial 'blow-up of a good germ' is classical in planar approximation (Hencl-Pratelli; Daneri-Pratelli); the p=2 angular attenuation with first-power envelope is a new technical twist.

name: Angular attenuation (p=2) and outer weight W
statement: Map A expanding tile around random u_j; area factor via det DA (first power of 1+lh/|omega-u_j|, integrable in 2D); weight fixed before budget transfer.
why: Technical device; integrability of 1/r in 2D standard.

name: Finite compact jet selection
statement: Disjoint compacts K_i of ranks 1..3 carrying Whitney C^1 jets; tail int |Df|^p < eps0; excess neighbourhoods small.
why: Standard Lusin-type selection.

name: Kernel compression (rank 1/2) and successful kernel blocks
statement: Collapse kernel directions P_0(y,z)=(y,p_y(z)) onto section S; G_lambda = V(P_lambda(sigma_Y(y),z)) -> [Dh_Y,0]; reduces the core to line/plane sections; expected failed volume small.
why: Paper names Hencl-Pratelli planar singular-model treatment; kernel compression is the natural 3D analogue.

name: Rank-one length sharpness identity
statement: int_0^1 |u'-e|^2 = s^2+1-2e.d for constant-speed u; near-minimal length => L^2 then L^p closeness, valid at p=1 without strict convexity.
why: One-line identity.

name: Completion of uncontrolled cells
statement: Cells reparametrized preserving base image with cost <= C(H sum_F int|D_t g|^p + H^2 sum_e int|D_t g|^p + [p=2] H sum Area).
why: Composition of skeleton estimates.

name: Global choices, summability, strong convergence (M1 assembly)
statement: Order: eps0, M, l, sharp tolerances, eta, tau, delta, neighbourhoods, h, target mesh, H_0, small radial params, lambda, cell completions; Markov selection.
why: Bookkeeping.

name: Completion on fixed target (M1)
statement: Compose low-exponent approximation and smoothing theorem.
why: Assembly.

name: Main theorem 2<p<infty
statement: Same statement as M1-02 for 2<p<infty.
why: Goal.

name: Regular points of a W^{1,p} homeomorphism, p>2
statement: Frechet differentiability a.e., det>0 at invertible points, deficient-rank image null, Lusin N for p>=3, null images of a.e. coordinate planes.
why: Classical (monotone-function oscillation on spheres).

name: Forbidden cone for the transported measure
statement: im Df(x) subset V(nu,f(x)) a.e.; V(nu,y) != R^3 nu-a.e. on f(D) (Alberti-Marchese + De Philippis-Rindler); finite partition with almost-normal directions.
why: Direct transfer of AM decomposability bundle + DPR; the bridge to Sobolev homeomorphisms is new (transfer).

name: Simultaneous graph-null set
statement: One Borel set of full sigma-measure null on every 1/lambda-Lipschitz graph (Sion minimax / Rainwater).
why: Named precedent; variant.

name: Finite thin bands
statement: Compact graph-null K covered by N bands of length L with NL<delta (antichain/chain decomposition).
why: Named precedents.

name: Target flattening S_0 (triangular band collapse)
statement: Lipschitz S_0 collapsing thin bands vertically; F_kappa=S_kappa∘f; |DF_0-Df|<=C lambda|Df| on retained K; F_0(K) on flat plates; homeomorphic off zero-volume Z.
why: Band-collapse is elementary; its use relies on bundle transversality (transfer).

name: Protected wells (paired endpoint contacts)
statement: Bump b_1 with Laplacian bounded so affine L_h supports |x|^2/2+b_1 exactly at q±dn; random d,n make endpoints regular.
why: Double-well design of a convex conjugate; elementary, new purpose.

name: Immersed cubical skeleton
statement: Whitney-layered triangulation of shell {0<t<2s}; local diffeomorphism i on 2-skeleton neighbourhood with |Di|~s/l_D, chart template i(x*+l xi)=y*+sI(xi) from finite list (relative Smale-Hirsch).
why: Quantitative, Whitney-scaled variant of Kirby's torus-trick immersion lift (uncited neighbour; Hirsch 1959 cited for immersion).

name: Cubical cutoff (energy-controlled identity core with ball fibres)
statement: h near Id on |t|<=Cs replaced in B_{2s} by Sobolev F, F=Id on B, same image, int_shell |DF|^p <= C_p int_{|t|<=Cs}|Dh|^p (sum over depths (l/s)^3 (s/l)^2); holes filled by Schoenflies then collapsed to points; ball fibres openable topologically.
why: See M2-08; combination lift + hole collapse (cell-like map, Bing-shrinking flavour) is new in Sobolev setting.

name: Relative opening of ball fibres
statement: Proper onto map with null family of tame ball fibres opened to a homeomorphism agreeing off small balls.
why: Standard.

name: Exceptional inverse data boxes
statement: Cubes around null exceptional source set with small volume and facet budgets (random phase).
why: Standard.

name: Regular affine implantation (condition-number-free)
statement: Exact affine cores in target boxes; cost C_p|Db|^p R^3/det Db <= C_p int_{V_b}|DF|^p, independent of cond(Db).
why: Normalization trick; follows from M2-09.

name: Two-round exact carrier F_b
statement: Continuous proper onto W^{1,p}_loc carrier: exact affine/PL over O with residual volume < a_Q per Whitney cube, = F_kappa near K, marked cubes (2<p<3), universal regional energy estimate.
why: New object, assembled from M2-09/12.

name: Smooth cubical cutoff
statement: Smooth-input version giving locally bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism with same energy bound + eps.
why: Variant of M2-09.

name: Postponed full-rank correction
statement: Reserve Vitali cubes on full-rank points; any smooth k close to f with small band energy can be corrected to equal b_j on inner cubes.
why: Standard Vitali + M2-14.

name: Subcritical marked-cube compression
statement: For 2<p<3 radial compression of marked cubes; inner cost alpha^{3-p}, outer bounded by collar trace.
why: Same as M1-18.

name: Excluding contacts by a Poisson perturbation
statement: b_2 with Delta psi < 0 outside O, small values, preserving protected supports.
why: Elementary but purposeful.

name: Contact curvature and dual separation
statement: Convex envelope phi C^{1,1}; F=phi^* has strong-convexity gap at contacts; contacts in O.
why: Convex analysis.

name: Proper product quantizer T=(dG)^{-1}
statement: G = sup of c-convex quadratic supports at sites; T Lipschitz, identity outside Lambda, onto; over face P input product cq+conv{p_i}; 3D input blocks X_i inside O; outside blocks output in 2-skeleton.
why: Power-diagram (Aurenhammer) / Moreau-proximal construction used as a Lipschitz retraction of the target onto a 2-complex; close neighbours exist; the exact-block property is new.

name: Paired arrays, redistribution, phase calibration
statement: Lattice of paired sites; scalar quantizer Q_c; redistribution J enlarging central fraction to a_*; Dq_0 = a_*^{-1} proj DF_kappa on retained data.
why: Technical.

name: Strict quantizers T_eta
statement: T_eta(y)=q+eta(q)(y-q) is proper locally bi-Lipschitz, close to T in W^{1,p}.
why: Elementary.

name: Subdividing true faces
statement: Voronoi subcells with clearance bounds; vertex neighbourhoods charged by Dq_0=0 on level sets.
why: Standard.

name: Polar labels (t,s) and sharp rectangular bound
statement: t=L_D log r, s=perimeter arclength; |Dt|+|Ds|<=C/r; on rank-one rectangle sharp (1+gamma)/r.
why: Polar coordinates.

name: Graph exterior M_y, walls A_D(t) (annuli) and B_e(s) (meridian disks)
statement: Remove blocks and central prisms; M_y graph handlebody, irreducible, H_2=0; wall families with prescribed incidences.
why: Handlebody recognition standard; the wall families are new objects.

name: Carrier exact on the central tubes
statement: PL h_*, K-bar via lift and caps (M2-09 relative), F_*=K-bar h_* with local fibre formula.
why: Relative reuse of M2-09.

name: Exact edge matching when opening the central carrier
statement: Openings f_n agreeing with F_* on edge-wall hits.
why: Technical.

name: Stairs and sampling
statement: Stratified sampled labels with intervals I_j, stair S of root-slope 1+O(zeta); weighted count density 1+O(zeta+c_*).
why: Stratified sampling.

name: Pre-stack contract
statement: Two-colour collars E_j: Sigma x [0,w_j] with parameter u_j, exact boundary traces, full product boxes at intersections, joint trivializations, slope majorant G.
why: New bookkeeping object; product neighbourhoods of normal surfaces are classical.

name: Diagonal routing and good parameters
statement: Circle-box exchange with d=a-u+v (slope +-1); rooted tree assembly; visit bound sum int N_P <= w_k gives local finiteness a.e.
why: Regular exchange (Haken) with measure-preserving parameter bookkeeping.

name: Conservation of oriented periods
statement: I(gamma,L)=I(gamma,W) for routed vs standard wall, via H_2(M_x)=0.
why: Standard intersection theory.

name: Graph potentials and guards
statement: Potentials on star/perimeter graph; guards kappa_g = fibre paths of T h_g from net points to boundary anchors on distinct blocks; prior capacities C_a for int G^p fixed before guards.
why: No neighbour of 'guard' fibres pinning topological level sets found; mechanism uses oscillation-on-spheres (classical).

name: Crossing lower bound
statement: Any path from a good routed layer to a guard at label distance delta has int_sigma G >= c_delta (weighted period identity + coarea).
why: Coarea + period identity.

name: Spherical path estimate (p>2)
statement: Points on sphere radius R joined by path of g-cost <= C_p R^{1-2/p} ||g||_{L^p(Sigma_R)}.
why: Classical (Morrey-type estimate on 2-spheres).

name: Guard barrier
statement: If pre-stacks obey prior capacities and avoid guards, every good routed layer lies within prescribed accuracy of its standard support (else int G^p >= c a h^{2-p} -> infinity).
why: Combination new; ingredients classical (capacity/modulus counting).

name: Stable intervals

statement: Slot placement on eligible edges; geometric-decay neighbour majorant M_sigma (l^p bounded convolution); auxiliary mesh at scale W/M; axial translation of slabs.

statement: Half-width widened to (1-C eta)W/2 by flow preserving parameters; grad u_j = +-e_i + O(eta), squared Frobenius <= 2+C eta.

statement: Expected weak costs <= C_w carrier budgets; capacities A_j fixed before guards; one common opening realises walls with selected counts.

name: Guard-pinned topological wall realization; energy through two scalar labels only
statement: Represent the approximant as P_0∘T∘h, where T (quantizer) collapses the target to a 2-complex with polar labels (t,s), and h is a homeomorphism built qualitatively so that sampled source walls (pulled-back level annuli/disks, routed with conserved parameter length) go to standard label walls. The derivative of P_0∘T∘h is controlled by the wall-parameter slope density G alone (no Dh). Realized labels are pinned to the carrier's labels because a misplaced layer would have to be joined to many nea…
why: No neighbour found in the searches listed; non-analytic; load-bearing for all of M2's rank-deficient recovery. Not a templated induction strengthening, so no cap. It is a combination of classical parts (Morrey/Gehring oscillation on 2-spheres, H_2=0 intersection numbers, Haken exchange), so a judge could rule it N2 as 'known parts, new assembly'. F5: change of representation (energy carried by scalar labels of a 2-complex-valued factorization) with an F3 auxiliary object (guards). Confidence lo…

name: Immersed cubical skeleton cutoff (universal-constant identity core with collapsible ball fibres)
statement: For h within cs of the identity on a band of the cube, a Whitney-layered 2-skeleton neighbourhood of the shell is immersed at common target scale s (|Di|~s/l). The lift H=i^{-1} h i satisfies |DH|<=A|Dh∘i|; per depth l the energy factor (l/s)^3 times overlap count (s/l)^2 sums geometrically, giving int_shell|DF|^p <= C_p int_band |Dh|^p with C_p universal. Uncontrolled hole fillings (Schoenflies) are collapsed to points, leaving countably many tame ball fibres that are opened later without ener…
why: Quantitative, Whitney-scaled version of the torus-trick immersion lift, combined with collapse of uncontrolled fillings (cell-like map flavour). Close neighbour exists (uncited), so N2. Would rise to N3 only if an expert judges the energy-summing immersion genuinely unlike torus-trick usage.

name: Tie budget + compatible softmax simplex squeeze (topological transfer of trace budgets)
statement: Count unsigned crossings of f-images of measured source curves/surfaces with barycentric leader-tie dual strata of a random target triangulation, weighted by flat edge/face measure; realize the count as actual length/area by a face-compatible, locally bi-Lipschitz softmax squeeze T_i=lambda_i e^{a lambda_i}/sum_j lambda_j e^{a lambda_j} with a=e^{1/b}-e; expected budget <= C int J_m D(f∘P).
why: Paper-named precedent (White/Federer-Fleming). The softmax homeomorphic realization is new but a variant.

name: Convex product quantizer T=(dG)^{-1} with Poisson contact exclusion and protected double wells
statement: A Lipschitz proper self-map of Lambda whose 3D input blocks lie in the carrier's exact region and whose other outputs lie on a 2-complex with orthogonal product fibres; double wells give paired contacts so retained rank-deficient data land on rectangular faces with nearly unchanged gradients.
why: Known convex-geometric construction repurposed (new bridge into Sobolev approximation); the Poisson exclusion is elementary.

name: Finite PL libraries before resolution selection (smoothing theorem)
statement: Bin normalized local maps into finitely many classes and fix one Hamilton-PL model per (configuration, bin, protected data) before the mesh is refined, so derivative bounds of qualitative replacements precede the bad-cube volume.
why: Named precedent.

name: Target flattening via decomposability bundle + converse Rademacher
statement: Images of rank-1/2 regular points carry a proper decomposability bundle (else DPR forces absolute continuity), giving a transverse direction; graph-null set and thin bands then allow a Lipschitz vertical band collapse flattening the data onto plates with |DF_0-Df|<=C lambda|Df|.
why: Named precedent for the measure-theoretic core; the bridge GMT->Sobolev homeomorphisms appears new (see bridge_novelty).

name: Kernel compression with near-sharp line/plane budgets (thin-grid coefficient, sharp disk estimate)
statement: At rank k<3 compress kernel directions onto a section; anisotropic Kuhn lattices give tie-budget coefficient 1+C eta on tangent k-vectors; near-minimal length/area then gives L^p gradient closeness (length identity; conformal disk rigidity).
why: Natural 3D analogue of planar singular-model handling plus classical conformal parametrization.

name: Diagonal routing with conservation of parameter length and oriented periods
statement: Inessential circle intersections of two wall families are exchanged along diagonal levels d=a-u+v (slope +-1), assembling rooted trees whose visit counts are bounded by measure preservation; routed walls have the same intersection numbers as standard walls (H_2=0).
why: Regular exchange with measure-preserving bookkeeping.

name: Canonical snapping with protected buffers (forward-only Lipschitz control)
statement: Finite marked combinatorial types; map new->old coordinates via fixed representatives so parameters become CW/h-Lipschitz independent of sliver altitudes.
why: Bookkeeping device built from standard finite-type compactness; analyst's N2 lowered.

name: Radial blocks with star replacement and p=2 angular attenuation
statement: Install exact identity germs at random block centres (punctured-sphere mapping-class argument) and radially enlarge them to recover full-rank jets; at p=2 use reverse rays from inverse BV and a determinant (first-power) envelope.
why: 3D topological analogue of planar techniques.

name: M2-31 + M2-34 + M2-36 + M2-37 (guard-pinned wall realization; energy through labels only)
why: Nothing in L or the goal resembles realizing the two polar label coordinates (t,s) of a 2-complex-valued map as level walls of a homeomorphism, routing them with conserved parameter length, and pinning the realized labels by reference fibre paths ('guards') through a capacity barrier that diverges like h^{2-p}. It makes the final energy depend only on scalar parameter slopes, never on Dh, which is what lets the p>2 proof survive without a quantitative 3D extension theorem.

name: M2-08 + M2-09 immersed cubical skeleton cutoff
why: A universal-constant energy bound for cutting a near-identity Sobolev homeomorphism off to the identity, obtained by lifting through an immersion of a Whitney-layered 2-skeleton at a common scale s ((l/s)^3 volume factor vs (s/l)^2 overlap) and collapsing uncontrolled hole fillings to points. Replaces the missing 3D quantitative extension theorem; used for every exact implant.

name: M1-27 + M1-28 + M1-29 tie budget and variable softmax simplex squeeze
why: Converts counts of crossings with barycentric-tie dual strata of a random target triangulation into actual image lengths/areas of a homeomorphism, via a face-compatible, injective softmax concentration. Gives the low-exponent energy bounds without any derivative bound on the topological replacement.

name: M2-19 + M2-17 convex product quantizer with Poisson contact exclusion
why: Reduces the 3D target to a polyhedral 2-complex (orthogonal product fibres) whose 3D blocks lie in exact regions; makes 2 scalar labels carry the deficient-rank gradient.

name: M1-14 finite PL libraries before resolution
why: Fixes derivative bounds of qualitative PL replacements before shrinking the exceptional set, breaking a circularity.
